Set-Content -Path ModManager.cs -Value @"
/*
 * Motor Town Server Mod Manager
 * Built to handle multi-server .pak versioning, smart matching, quick layout deployments, and game launch.
 * Cleaned up and restructured to keep everything maintainable without any auto-generated fluff.
 */

using System.IO;
using System.IO.Compression;
using System.Drawing;

        [DllImport("user32.dll")]
        private static extern bool SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext(int dpiContext);
        private static readonly int DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT_PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2 = -4;

        [DllImport("user32.dll", CharSet = CharSet.Auto)]
        private static extern IntPtr SendMessage(IntPtr hWnd, int msg, IntPtr wParam, IntPtr lParam);
        private const int EM_SETMARGINS = 0xD3;
        private const int EC_LEFTMARGIN = 0x1;

        // Fix: when ModManager.exe is run elevated ("Run as administrator") - which many
        // users do because the default paks path is under Program Files (x86) - Windows'
        // User Interface Privilege Isolation (UIPI) silently blocks drag-and-drop coming
        // from a non-elevated Explorer window. No exception is thrown; the drop is just
        // swallowed. ChangeWindowMessageFilterEx explicitly allows the messages that
        // drag-and-drop relies on through that isolation boundary.
        [DllImport("user32.dll")]
        private static extern bool ChangeWindowMessageFilterEx(IntPtr hWnd, uint message, uint action, IntPtr changeInfo);
        private const uint MSGFLT_ALLOW = 1;
        private const uint WM_DROPFILES = 0x0233;
        private const uint WM_COPYDATA = 0x004A;
        private const uint WM_COPYGLOBALDATA = 0x0049;
        private const int WM_SETREDRAW = 0x000B;

        // Applies Windows' built-in "DarkMode_Explorer" visual style to a control's native
        // scrollbar (Explorer, File Manager, etc. all use this same mechanism for themed
        // scrollbars) - this is what actually recolors the ListBox's scrollbar thumb/track,
        // since there's no public WinForms property for that.
        [DllImport("uxtheme.dll", CharSet = CharSet.Unicode)]
        private static extern int SetWindowTheme(IntPtr hWnd, string pszSubAppName, string pszSubIdList);

        // Lets the window's own title bar (where the minimize/maximize/X buttons live) match
        // the app's theme. DWMWA_CAPTION_COLOR/DWMWA_TEXT_COLOR (Windows 11 22000+) allow a
        // fully custom color; DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE is the older dark/light-only
        // fallback for Windows 10. Both are best-effort - older systems simply keep the
        // default title bar if neither call is supported.
        [DllImport("dwmapi.dll")]
        private static extern int DwmSetWindowAttribute(IntPtr hwnd, int attr, ref int attrValue, int attrSize);
        private const int DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE = 20;
        private const int DWMWA_CAPTION_COLOR = 35;
        private const int DWMWA_TEXT_COLOR = 36;

        // --- XInput (Xbox/Steam Deck-style controller input for Console Mode) ---
        // Two DllImports pointing at different DLL names under different C# method names,
        // since not every Windows install has xinput1_4.dll (older systems only ship the
        // 9.1.0 back-compat version) - TryGetControllerState below tries the newer one first
        // and falls back to the older one, so Console Mode's navigation degrades to
        // keyboard-only instead of crashing if neither is present.
        [DllImport("xinput1_4.dll", EntryPoint = "XInputGetState")]
        private static extern int XInputGetState14(int dwUserIndex, out XINPUT_STATE pState);

        [DllImport("xinput9_1_0.dll", EntryPoint = "XInputGetState")]
        private static extern int XInputGetState910(int dwUserIndex, out XINPUT_STATE pState);

        [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)]
        private struct XINPUT_GAMEPAD
        {
            public ushort wButtons;
            public byte bLeftTrigger;
            public byte bRightTrigger;
            public short sThumbLX;
            public short sThumbLY;
            public short sThumbRX;
            public short sThumbRY;
        }

        [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)]
        private struct XINPUT_STATE
        {
            public uint dwPacketNumber;
            public XINPUT_GAMEPAD Gamepad;
        }

        private const ushort XINPUT_GAMEPAD_DPAD_UP = 0x0001;
        private const ushort XINPUT_GAMEPAD_DPAD_DOWN = 0x0002;
        private const ushort XINPUT_GAMEPAD_DPAD_LEFT = 0x0004;
        private const ushort XINPUT_GAMEPAD_DPAD_RIGHT = 0x0008;
        private const ushort XINPUT_GAMEPAD_A = 0x1000;
        private const ushort XINPUT_GAMEPAD_B = 0x2000;
        // Y is the top bar's "start typing in this field" shortcut - see the (Y TO TYPE)
        // hint printed on the search row of the server/mod pickers.
        private const ushort XINPUT_GAMEPAD_Y = 0x8000;
        private const short XINPUT_STICK_THRESHOLD = 16000;

        private static bool TryGetControllerState(out XINPUT_STATE state)
        {
            try
            {
                if (XInputGetState14(0, out state) == 0) return true;
            }
            catch { }

            try
            {
                if (XInputGetState910(0, out state) == 0) return true;
            }
            catch { }

            state = new XINPUT_STATE();
            return false;
        }

        // Fix: reading virtual "FileContents" (dragging files out of an open Zip/Explorer
        // preview window) with no index always returns the FIRST file's bytes for every
        // entry, so a multi-file virtual drop silently duplicates one file's content under
        // every dropped name. These P/Invokes let us pull each file's content by its own
        // index instead.
        [DllImport("ole32.dll")]
        private static extern void ReleaseStgMedium(ref System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.STGMEDIUM medium);
        [DllImport("kernel32.dll")]
        private static extern IntPtr GlobalLock(IntPtr hMem);
        [DllImport("kernel32.dll")]
        private static extern bool GlobalUnlock(IntPtr hMem);
        [DllImport("kernel32.dll")]
        private static extern int GlobalSize(IntPtr hMem);

        // Fix: names coming from FILEDESCRIPTORW (virtual drag-drop) are attacker-influenced
        // data, not real filesystem paths. Path.Combine will happily honor "..\..\evil.exe"
        // or an absolute path like "C:\Windows\..." and write outside the intended folder.
        // This strips any directory component and re-validates the final path stays inside
        // destDir before anything is written to disk.
        // Fix (Zip Slip): ZipFile.ExtractToDirectory on .NET Framework does not validate
        // that entry paths stay inside the destination folder. A crafted .pak/.zip with an
        // entry named e.g. "..\..\..\AppData\Roaming\Startup\evil.exe" would otherwise be
        // written outside destDir. This extracts entry-by-entry and rejects any entry whose
        // resolved path would escape destDir.
        private static void SafeExtractZip(string zipPath, string destDir)
        {
            Directory.CreateDirectory(destDir);
            string destFull = Path.GetFullPath(destDir);
            if (!destFull.EndsWith(Path.DirectorySeparatorChar.ToString()))
                destFull += Path.DirectorySeparatorChar;

            using (ZipArchive archive = ZipFile.OpenRead(zipPath))
            {
                foreach (ZipArchiveEntry entry in archive.Entries)
                {
                    string entryName = entry.FullName.Replace('/', Path.DirectorySeparatorChar);

                    if (Path.IsPathRooted(entryName) || entryName.Contains(".."))
                    {
                        continue; // reject suspicious entry outright
                    }

                    string targetPath = Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(destFull, entryName));
                    if (!targetPath.StartsWith(destFull, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                    {
                        continue; // resolved path still escaped destDir - extra safety net
                    }

                    if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(entry.Name))
                    {
                        // directory entry
                        Directory.CreateDirectory(targetPath);
                        continue;
                    }

                    string parentDir = Path.GetDirectoryName(targetPath);
                    if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(parentDir))
                    {
                        Directory.CreateDirectory(parentDir);
                    }

                    entry.ExtractToFile(targetPath, true);
                }
            }
        }

        private static string SafeCombineWithinDirectory(string destDir, string untrustedName)
        {
            string bareName = Path.GetFileName(untrustedName);
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(bareName)) return null;

            string destFull = Path.GetFullPath(destDir);
            if (!destFull.EndsWith(Path.DirectorySeparatorChar.ToString()))
                destFull += Path.DirectorySeparatorChar;

            string candidate = Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(destFull, bareName));
            if (!candidate.StartsWith(destFull, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                return null;

            return candidate;
        }

        private static byte[] GetVirtualFileContents(object dataObject, int index)
        {
            System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.IDataObject comData = dataObject as System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.IDataObject;
            if (comData == null) return null;

            System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.FORMATETC formatEtc = new System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.FORMATETC
            {
                cfFormat = (short)DataFormats.GetFormat("FileContents").Id,
                ptd = IntPtr.Zero,
                dwAspect = System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.DVASPECT.DVASPECT_CONTENT,
                lindex = index,
                tymed = System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.TYMED.TYMED_ISTREAM | System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.TYMED.TYMED_HGLOBAL
            };

            System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.STGMEDIUM medium;
            try
            {
                comData.GetData(ref formatEtc, out medium);
            }
            catch
            {
                return null;
            }

            try
            {
                if (medium.tymed == System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.TYMED.TYMED_ISTREAM)
                {
                    System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.IStream nativeStream =
                        (System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.IStream)Marshal.GetObjectForIUnknown(medium.unionmember);

                    System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.STATSTG stat;
                    nativeStream.Stat(out stat, 0);
                    int size = (int)stat.cbSize;

                    byte[] buffer = new byte[size];
                    nativeStream.Read(buffer, size, IntPtr.Zero);
                    return buffer;
                }
                else if (medium.tymed == System.Runtime.InteropServices.ComTypes.TYMED.TYMED_HGLOBAL)
                {
                    IntPtr ptr = GlobalLock(medium.unionmember);
                    if (ptr == IntPtr.Zero) return null;
                    try
                    {
                        int size = GlobalSize(medium.unionmember);
                        byte[] buffer = new byte[size];
                        Marshal.Copy(ptr, buffer, 0, size);
                        return buffer;
                    }
                    finally
                    {
                        GlobalUnlock(medium.unionmember);
                    }
                }
            }
            finally
            {
                ReleaseStgMedium(ref medium);
            }

            return null;
        }

        private const string DefaultGamePath = @"C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Motor Town\MotorTown\Content\Paks";
        private const string ConfigFileName = "config.json";
        private const string AppVersion = "0.3";

        // Checks Version.txt on the public GitHub repo for updates - far simpler and more
        // reliable than scraping or authenticating against a third-party site. The file's
        // first line is the version; everything after that is treated as the changelog.
        private const string GitHubVersionUrl = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ModManager-Guy/MTModManager/main/version.txt";
        private const string NexusModPageUrl = "https://www.nexusmods.com/motortownbehindthewheel/mods/166";
        private const string DiscordInviteUrl = "https://discord.gg/9Hs7AXDpZu";
        private static readonly System.Net.Http.HttpClient updateHttpClient = CreateUpdateHttpClient();

        private static System.Net.Http.HttpClient CreateUpdateHttpClient()
        {
            try
            {
                System.Net.ServicePointManager.SecurityProtocol |= System.Net.SecurityProtocolType.Tls12;
            }
            catch { }

            System.Net.Http.HttpClient client = new System.Net.Http.HttpClient();
            client.Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10);
            client.DefaultRequestHeaders.UserAgent.ParseAdd("ModManager/" + AppVersion);

            // raw.githubusercontent.com sits behind a CDN that caches responses for a few
            // minutes per edge node - without these, a user could push a new version.txt and
            // still have some players fetch a stale cached copy (same version number showing
            // up with the OLD changelog text, since the whole file - both lines - comes from
            // that same cached response). These headers combine with the cache-busting query
            // string added in CheckForUpdatesAsync to make sure every check hits the origin.
            try
            {
                client.DefaultRequestHeaders.CacheControl = new System.Net.Http.Headers.CacheControlHeaderValue
                {
                    NoCache = true,
                    NoStore = true
                };
                client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Pragma.ParseAdd("no-cache");
            }
            catch { }

            return client;
        }

        private string skippedUpdateVersion = "";
        private string pendingUpdateVersion = "";
        private string pendingUpdateChangelog = "";

        // Version whose first-launch "What's New" dialog has already been shown/dismissed
        // (persisted to settings.txt as LastSeenChangelogVersion). Empty on a brand new
        // install, so the very first launch always counts as "first launch of the
        // application" too, not just the first launch after an update.
        private string lastSeenChangelogVersion = "";

        // Guards against the settings file being corrupted mid-load: LoadCheckboxSettings
        // assigns saved values straight to controls (chkSmartMatching.Checked = val, etc.)
        // whose CheckedChanged/SelectedIndexChanged handlers call SaveCheckboxSettings().
        // WinForms fires those events synchronously the instant an assignment actually
        // changes a control's value, which can happen partway through the load loop - well
        // before later lines in the file (like LastSeenChangelogVersion=) have been parsed
        // into their in-memory fields. Without this guard, that premature save would write
        // the file back out with those not-yet-loaded fields still at their "" defaults,
        // silently wiping e.g. LastSeenChangelogVersion on disk even though the in-memory
        // value for the current session ends up correct - which was making the first-launch
        // "What's New" dialog re-show every other boot (the corrupted-on-disk boot loads
        // blank and shows it again; closing it saves correctly since that save happens after
        // the load loop finishes; the next boot's load then corrupts it again; repeat).
        private bool isLoadingSettings = false;
        private readonly string serverStorageDir = Path.Combine(AppDomain.CurrentDomain.BaseDirectory, "ServerMods");
        private readonly string settingsFilePath;
        private readonly string backupStorageDir;
        private readonly string saveGameBackupDir;
        private readonly string undoCacheDir;
        private string customEngineIniPath = null;

        // Undo history for deleted mods/servers: deletions move the file/folder into
        // undoCacheDir instead of actually deleting it, and push an entry here so Undo can
        // move it back. The whole cache directory is wiped when the app closes (see
        // OnModManagerFormClosing), since undo history isn't meant to survive a restart.
        private enum UndoActionType { DeletedServerFolder, DeletedModFile }

        private class UndoEntry
        {
            public UndoActionType Type;
            public string OriginalPath;
            public string CachedPath;
            public string ServerName;
        }

        private readonly Stack<UndoEntry> undoHistory = new Stack<UndoEntry>();
        // Redo history: whenever Undo successfully restores something, the same entry gets
        // pushed here instead of being thrown away, so Redo can re-delete it. Any *new*
        // deletion clears this (see OnDeleteServerClicked/OnDeleteModClicked) since it would
        // otherwise let Redo replay a branch of history that's no longer valid.
        private readonly Stack<UndoEntry> redoHistory = new Stack<UndoEntry>();

        private TextBox txtGamePath;
        private ComboBox cboServerDropdown;

        private float busySpinnerAngle = 0f;
        private string busyStatusText = "Working...";
        private ShinyButton btnResizeModList;
        private Dictionary<Control, int> listSplitterControlOffsets;

        private CheckBox chkAutoEngineIni;
        private ComboBox cboEditorSelector;

        // Shared base text for chkVirtualKeyboard - see its (ON)/(OFF) suffix, appended fresh
        // on every CheckedChanged rather than baked into the literal above.
        private const string VirtualKeyboardBaseLabel = "On-Screen Virtual Keyboard (Controller Accessible)";

        // --- Console Mode (controller-navigable dashboard, aimed at Steam Deck) ---
        private CheckBox chkConsoleMode;
        private Panel pnlConsoleTiles;
        private Panel pnlConsoleSidebar;
        private Panel pnlConsoleContent;
        private Button btnConsoleLaunchGame;
        private Label lblConsoleControlHint;
        private readonly List<Button> consoleCategoryButtons = new List<Button>();
        private readonly List<Button> consoleTileButtons = new List<Button>();
        private readonly string[] consoleCategoryNames = { "Mods", "Servers", "Backups", "Utility" };
        private string[][] consoleCategoryTileLabels;
        private EventHandler[][] consoleCategoryTileHandlers;
        private ConsoleIconKind[][] consoleCategoryTileIcons;
        private int selectedConsoleCategoryIndex = 0;
        private int selectedConsoleTileIndex = 0;
        private bool consoleLaunchFocused = false;
        // True while D-pad/arrow focus is parked on the permanent "Resize Mod List" button
        // that sits directly above the tile overlay (see btnResizeModList/SetupListResizeButton).
        // That button used to sit completely outside every Console Mode focus zone - Up/Down
        // navigation walked straight from the tile grid's Launch Game button into the top bar
        // (or back), stepping over it entirely, so a controller-only session had no way to
        // select it at all. Now it is its own stop between the top bar and Launch Game: Up
        // from Launch parks here first, and a further Up from here enters the top bar (and
        // symmetrically for Down coming back out of the top bar).
        private bool consoleResizeFocused = false;
        // True while D-pad/arrow focus is parked on the left-hand category sidebar rather than
        // on the content tiles. Left/Right used to switch category outright, which meant the
        // sidebar itself was never a focus target you could look at before committing to it.
        // Now Left moves focus onto the sidebar, Up/Down browse it WITHOUT switching anything,
        // and A/Enter is what actually enters that category (ActivateConsoleSidebarSelection).
        private bool consoleSidebarFocused = false;
        private int consoleSidebarIndex = 0;
        // Set while a top-bar ComboBox is genuinely dropped down under controller control:
        // Up/Down then move the open list's highlight, A commits whatever is highlighted, and
        // B reverts to whatever was selected at the moment it opened.
        private bool consoleDropdownOpen = false;
        private int consoleDropdownOriginalIndex = -1;
        // One shared ToolTip for the top-right corner icons (Undo/Redo/Settings/Update). They
        // are bare owner-drawn Panels rather than Buttons, so they have no hover text of their
        // own and nothing on screen says which curved arrow is which.
        private readonly ToolTip cornerIconToolTip = new ToolTip { InitialDelay = 300, ReshowDelay = 100, ShowAlways = true };
        // Sibling ring panels created by AttachFocusHighlight - kept so ApplyTheme can force
        // them to repaint in the new accent color the instant the theme changes.
        private readonly List<Panel> focusHighlightPanels = new List<Panel>();
        // True while list-resize mode is toggled on (via the "Resize Mod List" button that
        // sits directly under the mod list, in both desktop and Console Mode) - while active,
        // Up/Down resize the mod list in notches instead of their normal navigation meaning.
        // See btnResizeModList's Click handler and the ProcessCmdKey/FireDirectionalMove
        // branches below for the two separate input paths (real keyboard vs. D-pad/XInput)
        // that both key off this same flag.
        private bool listResizeModeActive = false;
        // Polls the controller's raw state on an edge-triggered basis (a move only fires the
        // instant a direction goes from not-pressed to pressed - see upPressed/downPressed/etc.
        // in ControllerPollTimer_Tick), so the Interval below is effectively the sampling
        // window for every D-pad tap. At 120ms, a quick tap shorter than that window could fall
        // entirely between two polls and never get sampled as "pressed" at all - dropped input,
        // not sluggish input. 16ms (~60Hz) is well under normal human tap speed and about as
        // fast as a plain WinForms Timer's WM_TIMER-based resolution can reliably deliver, so
        // navigation now reads as close to instant as this timer mechanism allows.
        private readonly Timer controllerPollTimer = new Timer { Interval = 16 };
        private ushort prevControllerButtons = 0;
        // Previous tick's combined "is this direction currently being pushed" state - D-pad,
        // left stick, or a physically-held arrow key, all OR'd together (see upHeld etc. in
        // ControllerPollTimer_Tick). Comparing against this each tick is what detects the
        // rising edge that fires a direction's immediate first move, regardless of which of
        // the three input sources it came from.
        private bool prevUpHeld = false;
        private bool prevDownHeld = false;
        private bool prevLeftHeld = false;
        private bool prevRightHeld = false;

        // --- D-pad / arrow-key hold-to-repeat ---
        // The first move on a fresh press fires immediately (within one 16ms poll tick);
        // holding a direction past RepeatInitialDelayMs then starts auto-repeating the same
        // move every RepeatIntervalMs while it's still held. Using our own timer for this
        // (instead of the OS's native keyboard repeat rate) means a held physical arrow key
        // and a held D-pad direction repeat at exactly the same, consistent speed regardless
        // of the user's own system keyboard-repeat settings.
        private const int RepeatInitialDelayMs = 350;
        private const int RepeatIntervalMs = 90;
        private int heldMsUp = 0, heldMsDown = 0, heldMsLeft = 0, heldMsRight = 0;
        private bool repeatingUp = false, repeatingDown = false, repeatingLeft = false, repeatingRight = false;

        // Tracks which arrow keys are currently physically held down, set by ProcessCmdKey
        // (Console Mode's tile/top-bar/list-resize navigation) and by frmVirtualKeyboard's own
        // KeyDown/KeyUp handlers, and fed into the same hold-to-repeat state machine the D-pad
        // uses above - see ControllerPollTimer_Tick.
        private bool physUpHeld = false;
        private bool physDownHeld = false;
        private bool physLeftHeld = false;
        private bool physRightHeld = false;

        // --- Virtual (on-screen) Keyboard - lets Console Mode reach text fields and
        // dropdowns with just a controller, no physical keyboard attached. Built as its own
        // small owned popup Form (rather than a Panel glued onto the main window) so it can
        // just as easily float above ShowThemedInputBox/ShowSettingsDialog-style dialogs as it
        // can the main window - those are separate Form instances with their own fixed
        // ClientSize, so a Panel could never have been made to fit inside all of them.
        private CheckBox chkVirtualKeyboard;
        private VirtualKeyboardForm frmVirtualKeyboard;

        // --- Color Blindness accessibility mode ---
        // "Off", "Protanopia", "Deuteranopia", or "Tritanopia". Persisted like Theme, and
        // read by GetThemeColors/ApplyTheme to swap the app's red/green/blue "meaning"
        // colors (Delete = red, Add/Launch = green, Undo = blue, plus the general accent)
        // for an Okabe-Ito-derived palette that stays distinguishable under that specific
        // type of color vision deficiency. Lives in the Settings dialog the same way
        // chkConsoleMode/chkVirtualKeyboard do: created once, unparented, and only attached
        // into whichever settings surface (desktop dialog or console picker menu) is
        // currently showing.
        private string colorBlindMode = "Off";
        private static readonly string[] ColorBlindModeOptions = { "Off", "Protanopia", "Deuteranopia", "Tritanopia" };
        private ComboBox cboColorBlindMode;
        private Label lblColorBlindHeader;
        private Button btnKeyboardClose;
        private TextBox keyboardTargetTextBox;
        // Guards against the keyboard reopening itself the instant it's closed: every
        // keystroke typed via the on-screen keyboard calls target.Focus() (see
        // InsertTextToTarget/BackspaceTarget) so the real textbox's caret stays visible while
        // typing, which means the textbox - not the keyboard Form - is what Windows hands
        // focus back to the moment the keyboard Form is hidden. That refocus fires the exact
        // GotFocus handler that opens the keyboard (AttachVirtualKeyboardOnFocus), so without
        // this flag, closing the keyboard would immediately reopen it. See HideVirtualKeyboard.
        private bool suppressKeyboardAutoShow = false;
        private bool keyboardShiftActive = false;
        private bool keyboardSymbolsActive = false;
        // Row 0 is always exactly the Close button (kept in this same grid so Up/Down naturally
        // reaches it like any other row); rows 1-4 are the letter/number/symbol keys; the last
        // row is Shift/123-ABC/Space/Backspace/Enter. Kept as Buttons (not ShinyButton) so their
        // Tag can carry the row/col into the shared layout arrays - see RebuildKeyboardLabels.
        private readonly List<List<Button>> keyboardKeyRows = new List<List<Button>>();
        private int keyboardSelRow = 0;
        private int keyboardSelCol = 0;

        // Controller-accessible focus zone for the search boxes/dropdowns that sit ABOVE the
        // Console Mode tile overlay (which only covers the action buttons/drop zone below the
        // mod list) - without this, a controller-only session could see the theme dropdown,
        // server search/dropdown, and mod search box, but had no way to reach or use them.
        // Pressing Up from the Launch Game tile (the top of the normal tile grid) enters this
        // zone; pressing Down from its first entry returns to Launch Game.
        private Control[] consoleTopBarControls;
        private bool consoleTopBarActive = false;

        private Panel pnlTopBarFocusHighlight;

        // The two custom dropdown fields that stand in for cboThemeSelector/cboServerDropdown.
        // The real ComboBoxes are still there and still hold every item and the selection -
        // the whole app reads them - they are just hidden, with these owner-drawn fields shown
        // in their place. A native ComboBox cannot be made to match this app's look (its

        // visible half while leaving the data half alone gets the look without rewriting the

        private ShinyButton btnThemeDropDown;
        private ShinyButton btnServerDropDown;

        // --- Pulsing focus ring ---
        // The selection outline breathes in and out rather than sitting at a flat brightness,
        // the way a console dashboard's tile border does. One timer drives every ring in the
        // app (top bar, the per-field rings, and the open picker's) off a single alpha value,
        // so they all pulse in step instead of drifting apart.
        private readonly Timer focusPulseTimer = new Timer { Interval = 40 };
        private int focusPulsePhase = 0;
        private int focusRingAlpha = 255;

        // The themed picker window that replaces the top bar's native dropdowns and search
        // boxes while Console Mode is on - see ShowConsolePicker. Non-null only while one is
        // open, and read by ControllerPollTimer_Tick/FireDirectionalMove so the app still has
        // exactly one XInput poll driving every zone rather than one per window.
        private ConsolePickerForm activeConsolePicker;
        // Whatever was typed into the last picker's search row, read back by the caller once
        // it closes so the (hidden) desktop search box can be kept in step with it.
        private string lastPickerQuery = "";
        // The lightweight themed drop-down list shown for the Theme/Server fields in ordinary
        // desktop (mouse) mode - see ShowThemedDropdown. Console Mode keeps using the full
        // ConsolePickerForm instead, since that one is what makes those fields controller/
        // D-pad navigable; this one is only ever the mouse-driven equivalent of a native
        // ComboBox's own drop-down list, so it never needs to be huge or centered on screen.
        // Tracked so opening a second one (or the same one twice) closes any prior instance
        // first instead of stacking popups.
        private Form activeDesktopDropdown;
        // Set while a picker is writing its query back into one of the desktop search boxes,
        // so that write can't re-run the filter the picker already ran.
        private bool suppressServerSearchEvent = false;
        private bool suppressModSearchEvent = false;
        // Every top-row field's Light Mode outline is a separate sibling panel rather than a
        // real border (see WrapControlWithLightModeBorder). Console Mode moves and resizes
        // those fields, so it needs to be able to find each field's panel and move it too.
        private readonly Dictionary<Control, Panel> lightModeBorderPanels = new Dictionary<Control, Panel>();

        private Label lblPathHeader;
        private Label lblServerHeader;
        private Label lblThemeHeader;
        private Label lblModSearchHeader;
        private Label lblEditorHeader;
        private Button btnBrowsePath;
        private Button btnOpenDirectory;
        private Button btnAddServerFolder;
        private Button btnDeleteServerFolder;
        private Button btnDeleteSelectedPak;
        private Button btnUndoLastAction;
        private Button btnMergeServerMods;
        private Button btnDeployMods;
        private Button btnRevertVanilla;
        private Button btnBackupPaks;
        private Button btnRestoreBackup;
        private Button btnBackupSaves;
        private Button btnManageSaves;
        private Button btnLaunchGame;
        private Panel btnUpdateIcon;
        private Panel btnSettingsGear;
        private Panel btnUndoIcon;
        private Panel btnRedoIcon;
        private Panel btnDiscordIcon;
        private Button btnOpenEngineIni;
        private Button btnOpenSaveDirectory;

        private List<string> cachedServerPaks = new List<string>();
        private List<string> cachedServerFolders = new List<string>();

        private readonly Color ThemeDarkBg = Color.FromArgb(30, 30, 36);
        private readonly Color ThemeControlDark = Color.FromArgb(42, 44, 53);
        private readonly Color AccentOrange = Color.FromArgb(255, 123, 0);
        private readonly Color AccentYellow = Color.FromArgb(255, 200, 0);
        private readonly Color TextLight = Color.FromArgb(240, 240, 240);
        private readonly Color TextMuted = Color.FromArgb(180, 185, 195);

        [STAThread]
        public static void Main()
        {
            try
            {
                try { SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext(DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT_PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2); } catch { }

                Application.EnableVisualStyles();
                Application.SetCompatibleTextRenderingDefault(false);
                Application.Run(new ModManagerForm());
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                MessageBox.Show("Fatal Startup Error: " + ex.ToString(), "Launch Failed", MessageBoxButtons.OK, MessageBoxIcon.Error);
            }
        }

        public ModManagerForm()
        {
            SetStyle(ControlStyles.AllPaintingInWmPaint | ControlStyles.UserPaint | ControlStyles.OptimizedDoubleBuffer, true);

            Text = "MotorTown: Behind The Wheel - Mod Manager";
            Width = 560;
            Height = 1170;
            MinimumSize = new Size(560, 1170);

            FormBorderStyle = FormBorderStyle.Sizable;
            MaximizeBox = true;
            StartPosition = FormStartPosition.CenterScreen;

            // KeyPreview lets the Form see KeyUp for every key (arrow keys included)
            // regardless of which child control actually has focus - needed so
            // OnConsoleModeKeyUp can reliably clear physUpHeld/physDownHeld/physLeftHeld/
            // physRightHeld the instant a held arrow key is released (ProcessCmdKey only ever
            // sees the KeyDown side). This doesn't change normal typing: KeyPreview only adds
            // a KeyUp observer here, it doesn't mark anything Handled or block the key from
            // still reaching the focused control afterward.
            KeyPreview = true;
            KeyUp += OnConsoleModeKeyUp;

            // /win32icon: in the compile script sets the .exe file's own icon (what Explorer
            // shows) - it does NOT set the icon WinForms shows in the taskbar and the
            // window's own title bar while the app is running; without Form.Icon set
            // explicitly, WinForms falls back to its own generic default icon instead of
            // reusing the exe's file icon. Form.Icon used to be loaded from a
            // ModManagerIcon.ico file sitting next to the .exe at runtime, which meant the
            // taskbar/title-bar icon silently reverted to that generic default the moment the
            // .ico file wasn't there anymore. The compile script now also embeds the same
            // .ico as a manifest resource INSIDE the .exe (see /resource: below) so the icon
            // travels with the compiled binary - the .ico file is only needed once, at
            // compile time, not afterward.
            // Fix: the /resource: flag itself had gone missing from the csc.exe call below
            // (only /win32icon: was still there, which sets the Explorer file icon but NOT
            // the runtime Form.Icon), so GetManifestResourceStream below always returned
            // null and the title bar/taskbar silently fell back to the generic default icon.
            try
            {
                using (Stream iconStream = Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly().GetManifestResourceStream("ModManagerIcon.ico"))
                {
                    if (iconStream != null)
                    {
                        Icon = new Icon(iconStream);
                    }
                }
            }
            catch { }

            backupStorageDir = Path.Combine(serverStorageDir, "Backup_Vanilla");
            saveGameBackupDir = Path.Combine(serverStorageDir, "Backup_Saves");
            undoCacheDir = Path.Combine(serverStorageDir, "UndoCache");
            settingsFilePath = Path.Combine(serverStorageDir, "settings.txt");

            FormClosing += OnModManagerFormClosing;

            EnsureStorageDirectoryExists();
            InitializeComponentLayout();

            // txtGamePath was the one top-row field left without the Light Mode border, so in
            // Light Mode it was the only one with no visible outline at all.
            WrapControlWithLightModeBorder(txtGamePath);
            WrapControlWithLightModeBorder(txtServerSearchBox);
            WrapControlWithLightModeBorder(txtModSearchBox);
            // The two dropdown fields need no border panel - ShinyButton draws its own
            // outline, in a shade derived from its own fill, in every theme.
            WrapControlWithLightModeBorder(cboEditorSelector);

            // Thick accent focus ring on every top-row field, in every theme and with any
            // input device - mouse, keyboard or controller.
            AttachFocusHighlight(txtGamePath);
            AttachFocusHighlight(btnThemeDropDown);
            AttachFocusHighlight(txtServerSearchBox);
            AttachFocusHighlight(btnServerDropDown);
            AttachFocusHighlight(txtModSearchBox);

            BuildDragOverlay();
            BuildBusyOverlay();
            SetupListResizeButton();
            EnsureActionRowMinimumWidth();

            // The action-button row can't rely on ordinary Anchor stretching (see
            // LayoutActionButtonRow's own comment), so it has to be explicitly recalculated
            // every time the window is resized. Same reasoning for the Console Mode tiles.
            // Batched in one SuspendLayout/ResumeLayout pass rather than letting each of the
            // ~19 individual Location/Size assignments below trigger its own layout+paint -
            // that per-control repainting on every single WM_SIZE tick during a live window
            // drag (compounded by ShinyButton's custom gradient OnPaint, which costs more than
            // a plain native button) is what was making resizing feel choppy/laggy.
            Resize += delegate
            {
                SuspendLayout();
                LayoutActionButtonRow();
                LayoutConsoleTiles();
                RepositionSettingsGear();
                ResumeLayout(true);
            };

            Load += delegate
            {
                // Re-run once more after the window has its real, final, DPI-settled size -
                // InitializeComponentLayout's own call happens before the window is actually
                // shown, so its ClientSize.Width can be slightly off from what actually renders
                // on screen, which is what let "Delete Server" render clipped until the window
                // was nudged.
                LayoutActionButtonRow();
                LayoutConsoleTiles();
                RepositionSettingsGear();
            };

            controllerPollTimer.Tick += ControllerPollTimer_Tick;

            focusPulseTimer.Tick += FocusPulseTimer_Tick;
            focusPulseTimer.Start();

            dragLeaveTimer.Tick += delegate { dragLeaveTimer.Stop(); HideDragOverlay(); };

            // Make the whole window (not just the drop panel) a drag-and-drop target, so
            // dragging a file anywhere over the app - not just the little panel - triggers
            // the full-screen overlay and accepts the drop.
            EnableDragDropRecursive(this);
            
            LoadCheckboxSettings();

            // The first-launch "What's New" dialog is now driven entirely from
            // CheckForUpdatesAsync below - it needs version.txt's contents anyway, so rather
            // than issuing a second GitHub request here, ShowFirstLaunchChangelogIfNeeded is
            // called from there once that response comes back and its version line matches
            // AppVersion exactly (see the comments in CheckForUpdatesAsync).

            if (cboThemeSelector.SelectedIndex == -1)
            {
                cboThemeSelector.SelectedIndex = 0; 
            }
            if (cboEditorSelector.SelectedIndex == -1)
            {
                cboEditorSelector.SelectedIndex = 0;
            }

            LoadInitialPath();
            RefreshServerList();
            UpdateDropDownDisplays();
            UpdateUndoButtonState();

            CheckForUpdatesAsync();
        }

        private void EnableDragDropRecursive(Control parent)
        {
            parent.AllowDrop = true;
            parent.DragEnter += OnPanelDragEnter;
            parent.DragLeave += AnyControl_DragLeave;
            parent.DragDrop += OnPanelDragDrop;

            foreach (Control child in parent.Controls)
            {
                EnableDragDropRecursive(child);
            }
        }

        private void BuildDragOverlay()
        {
            pnlDragOverlay = new DoubleBufferedPanel
            {
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                BackColor = Color.FromArgb(20, 20, 24),
                Visible = false
            };

            Label lblOverlayText = new Label
            {
                Text = "Drop .pak, .zip or ReadMe Files Here",
                Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 18, FontStyle.Bold),
                ForeColor = Color.White,
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleCenter
            };

            pnlDragOverlay.Paint += delegate(object s, PaintEventArgs pe)
            {
                pe.Graphics.SmoothingMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.SmoothingMode.AntiAlias;
                int margin = 22;
                Rectangle borderRect = new Rectangle(margin, margin, pnlDragOverlay.Width - (margin * 2), pnlDragOverlay.Height - (margin * 2));
                using (Pen whitePen = new Pen(Color.White, 4f) { DashStyle = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.DashStyle.Dash })
                {
                    pe.Graphics.DrawRectangle(whitePen, borderRect);
                }
            };

            pnlDragOverlay.Controls.Add(lblOverlayText);
            Controls.Add(pnlDragOverlay);
            pnlDragOverlay.BringToFront();
        }

        private void BuildBusyOverlay()
        {
            pnlBusyOverlay = new DoubleBufferedPanel { Dock = DockStyle.Fill, Visible = false };

            pnlBusyOverlay.Paint += delegate(object s, PaintEventArgs pe)
            {
                bool isLight = IsLightTheme();
                pe.Graphics.Clear(isLight ? Color.FromArgb(235, 250, 250, 250) : Color.FromArgb(235, 20, 20, 24));
                pe.Graphics.SmoothingMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.SmoothingMode.AntiAlias;

                int size = 48;
                Rectangle spinnerRect = new Rectangle(pnlBusyOverlay.Width / 2 - size / 2, pnlBusyOverlay.Height / 2 - size / 2 - 16, size, size);
                Color spinnerColor = isLight ? Color.FromArgb(70, 70, 70) : Color.White;
                using (Pen spinnerPen = new Pen(spinnerColor, 4.5f) { StartCap = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.LineCap.Round, EndCap = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.LineCap.Round })
                {
                    pe.Graphics.DrawArc(spinnerPen, spinnerRect, busySpinnerAngle, 270);
                }

                Rectangle textRect = new Rectangle(0, spinnerRect.Bottom + 14, pnlBusyOverlay.Width, 30);
                Color textColor = isLight ? Color.FromArgb(40, 40, 40) : TextLight;
                using (Font statusFont = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 10, FontStyle.Bold))
                {
                    TextRenderer.DrawText(pe.Graphics, busyStatusText, statusFont, textRect, textColor, TextFormatFlags.HorizontalCenter);
                }
            };

            busySpinnerTimer.Tick += delegate
            {
                busySpinnerAngle = (busySpinnerAngle + 18f) % 360f;
                if (pnlBusyOverlay.Visible) pnlBusyOverlay.Invalidate();
            };

            Controls.Add(pnlBusyOverlay);
        }

        // Shows a full-window, theme-aware spinner that blocks interaction with the rest of
        // the app (it simply covers everything, on top) without freezing the window itself -
        // the actual work is expected to run on a background thread via Task.Run while this
        // is visible, so the UI stays responsive and repaints normally.
        private void ShowBusyOverlay(string statusText)
        {
            busyStatusText = statusText;
            pnlBusyOverlay.Visible = true;
            pnlBusyOverlay.BringToFront();
            busySpinnerTimer.Start();
        }

        private void HideBusyOverlay()
        {
            busySpinnerTimer.Stop();
            pnlBusyOverlay.Visible = false;
        }

        // Used to be a thin mouse-drag splitter bar glued directly under the mod list
        // (MouseDown/MouseMove/MouseUp on a 10px grip panel). That's what produced the
        // "two resize bars" rendering glitch users were seeing, and it had no controller
        // equivalent at all - Console Mode had to bolt on an entirely separate tile just to
        // resize the same list. Replaced with one real, permanently visible button sitting
        // directly under the mod list in both desktop and Console Mode: click/tap it (or A on
        // a controller) to toggle "adjust mode", then Down grows the list and Up shrinks it
        // back - real keyboard arrows in desktop mode (see ProcessCmdKey), D-pad/physical
        // arrows via the existing Console Mode poll loop otherwise (see FireDirectionalMove).
        private void SetupListResizeButton()
        {
            btnResizeModList = new ShinyButton
            {
                Text = "Resize Mod List",
                Location = new Point(lstServerPaks.Left, lstServerPaks.Bottom + 1),
                Width = lstServerPaks.Width,
                Height = 26,
                FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
                Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 8f, FontStyle.Bold),
                Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right
            };
            btnResizeModList.Click += OnToggleListResizeModeClicked;
            // Keeps the controller/keyboard focus cursor in sync when the button is reached
            // by mouse instead - mirrors the MouseEnter wiring on the category tiles.
            btnResizeModList.MouseEnter += delegate
            {
                if (chkConsoleMode == null || !chkConsoleMode.Checked || listResizeModeActive) return;
                consoleLaunchFocused = false;
                consoleSidebarFocused = false;
                consoleTopBarActive = false;
                consoleResizeFocused = true;
                RefreshConsoleHighlights();
            };

            // Remember every control that currently sits below the list, as an offset from
            // the list's bottom edge, so they can all be shifted down/up together whenever
            // the list is resized - otherwise resizing the list would make it overlap the
            // buttons below it instead of pushing them out of the way. Everything in this
            // set was switched to Top-only anchoring (see InitializeComponentLayout) so
            // WinForms' own anchor engine never fights with this manual repositioning.
            listSplitterControlOffsets = new Dictionary<Control, int>();
            int listBottom = lstServerPaks.Bottom;
            foreach (Control ctrl in Controls)
            {
                if (ctrl != lstServerPaks && ctrl.Top >= listBottom)
                {
                    listSplitterControlOffsets[ctrl] = ctrl.Top - listBottom;
                }
            }

            Controls.Add(btnResizeModList);
            btnResizeModList.BringToFront();
        }

        // LayoutActionButtonRow's proportional squeeze is a fallback for a window that's been
        // actively dragged narrower than the row needs - it was never meant to be the NORMAL
        // state. Without this, the app's own default/minimum width (560) sat right at the edge
        // of what "Add Server / Delete Server / Delete Mod / Undo / Merge Servers" actually
        // measure out to, so "Delete Server" (the longest label besides "Merge Servers") could
        // render clipped the very first time the app ever opened, before anyone touched the
        // window border. Called once, right after those five buttons exist, so the window
        // starts out already wide enough for every label to render in full.
        private void EnsureActionRowMinimumWidth()
        {
            if (btnAddServerFolder == null || btnDeleteServerFolder == null || btnDeleteSelectedPak == null ||
                btnUndoLastAction == null || btnMergeServerMods == null) return;

            const int leftMargin = 15;
            const int rightMargin = 15;
            const int gap = 6;
            const int perButtonPadding = 18;

            Button[] buttons = { btnAddServerFolder, btnDeleteServerFolder, btnDeleteSelectedPak, btnUndoLastAction, btnMergeServerMods };
            int naturalTotal = 0;
            foreach (Button b in buttons)
            {
                naturalTotal += TextRenderer.MeasureText(b.Text, b.Font).Width + perButtonPadding;
            }
            int requiredClientWidth = leftMargin + rightMargin + gap * (buttons.Length - 1) + naturalTotal;

            // A Sizable form's client area runs narrower than its outer Width by the window's
            // own border/frame - padding generously here rather than querying exact frame
            // metrics just leaves a few extra pixels of breathing room, never a bug.
            int requiredOuterWidth = requiredClientWidth + 40;

            if (MinimumSize.Width < requiredOuterWidth)
            {
                MinimumSize = new Size(requiredOuterWidth, MinimumSize.Height);
            }
            if (Width < requiredOuterWidth)
            {
                Width = requiredOuterWidth;
            }
        }

        private const int ServerListMinHeight = 60;
        private const int ServerListMaxHeight = 400;

        // Shared by both the mouse-drag splitter above and Console Mode's D-pad/keyboard list
        // resize (see OnToggleListResizeModeClicked) - one implementation of "resize the list
        // to this height and shift everything below it to match" used by both input methods.
        private void AdjustServerListHeight(int desiredHeightRaw)
        {
            int desiredHeight = Math.Max(ServerListMinHeight, Math.Min(ServerListMaxHeight, desiredHeightRaw));
            int heightDelta = desiredHeight - lstServerPaks.Height;
            if (heightDelta == 0) return;

            // SuspendLayout only batches layout MATH (anchor/dock recalculation) - it does
            // NOT stop the OS from repainting each moved child window as it's moved. With
            // ~20 controls being repositioned on every mouse-move tick, that produced the
            // "hundreds of buttons" ghosting glitch. WM_SETREDRAW actually suspends
            // painting at the window level, so nothing is drawn until the single Update()
            // call at the end - eliminating the ghosting at its real cause.
            SendMessage(Handle, WM_SETREDRAW, (IntPtr)0, IntPtr.Zero);
            SuspendLayout();

            lstServerPaks.Height = desiredHeight;
            RepositionControlsBelowList();

            // Resized live (not deferred to mouse-up) so the window never clips content
            // while dragging down, and dragging back up shrinks it smoothly in real time
            // instead of leaving it the wrong size afterward. Order matters: shrink the
            // floor before the window when getting smaller, and grow the window before
            // the floor when getting bigger, or WinForms clamps the Height change against
            // a stale MinimumSize.
            int newMinHeight = MinimumSize.Height + heightDelta;
            if (heightDelta < 0)
            {
                MinimumSize = new Size(MinimumSize.Width, newMinHeight);
                Height += heightDelta;
            }
            else
            {
                Height += heightDelta;
                MinimumSize = new Size(MinimumSize.Width, newMinHeight);
            }

            ResumeLayout(false);
            SendMessage(Handle, WM_SETREDRAW, (IntPtr)1, IntPtr.Zero);
            Invalidate(true);
            Update();
        }

        private void RepositionControlsBelowList()
        {
            btnResizeModList.Top = lstServerPaks.Bottom + 1;

            int newListBottom = lstServerPaks.Bottom;
            foreach (KeyValuePair<Control, int> kvp in listSplitterControlOffsets)
            {
                kvp.Key.Top = newListBottom + kvp.Value;
            }
        }

        protected override void OnHandleCreated(EventArgs e)
        {
            base.OnHandleCreated(e);

            // Allow drag-and-drop messages through even if this process is running elevated.
            try
            {
                ChangeWindowMessageFilterEx(Handle, WM_DROPFILES, MSGFLT_ALLOW, IntPtr.Zero);
                ChangeWindowMessageFilterEx(Handle, WM_COPYDATA, MSGFLT_ALLOW, IntPtr.Zero);
                ChangeWindowMessageFilterEx(Handle, WM_COPYGLOBALDATA, MSGFLT_ALLOW, IntPtr.Zero);
            }
            catch { }
        }

        // Lets Console Mode's tile navigation work no matter which control currently has
        // focus, since arrow keys/Enter don't move between Buttons on their own in WinForms.
        // Also swallows Tab while Console Mode is on, so a stray Tab press can't focus one of
        // the ordinary controls sitting (invisibly, underneath) behind the tile panel.
        //
        // This used to fall straight into the tile-navigation branch below no matter what -
        // it never checked consoleTopBarActive at all. So the moment Up-navigation handed
        // focus to the top bar (theme dropdown / search boxes / server dropdown -
        // EnterConsoleTopBar), every further arrow/Enter/Escape press kept being treated as
        // tile navigation instead: Up/Down silently corrupted the hidden tile-selection state,
        // Left/Right hijacked category switching away from a focused search box's normal
        // caret movement, Enter activated whatever tile used to be selected instead of opening
        // the virtual keyboard, and Escape closed Console Mode entirely rather than backing
        // out of just the top bar. That combination is exactly what made a focused search box
        // feel "stuck" with no way back and no keyboard appearing. Now this branches on
        // consoleTopBarActive first, mirroring ControllerPollTimer_Tick's own branching, and
        // additionally leaves Left/Right/Space alone whenever the top bar's current control is
        // a textbox that already has real Windows focus, so ordinary text editing still works.
        protected override bool ProcessCmdKey(ref Message msg, Keys keyData)
        {
            if (chkConsoleMode != null && chkConsoleMode.Checked)
            {
                // Up/Down/Left/Right no longer perform the move directly here - they just mark
                // the direction as physically held (physUpHeld etc.), and the actual move(s) -
                // both the immediate first one and any hold-to-repeat ones - are driven by
                // ControllerPollTimer_Tick, the same timer/logic the D-pad uses. That's what
                // makes a held physical arrow key auto-repeat at the same, consistent speed a
                // held D-pad direction does, rather than relying on the OS's own (and highly
                // variable) keyboard-repeat rate. Enter/Space/Escape/Tab are unaffected - those
                // are one-shot actions with no repeat, so they still fire straight from here.
                if (listResizeModeActive)
                {
                    if (keyData == Keys.Up) { physUpHeld = true; return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Down) { physDownHeld = true; return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Enter || keyData == Keys.Space || keyData == Keys.Escape) { OnToggleListResizeModeClicked(this, EventArgs.Empty); return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Tab || keyData == (Keys.Tab | Keys.Shift)) { return true; }
                }
                else if (consoleDropdownOpen)
                {
                    // Mirrors the controller branch in ControllerPollTimer_Tick: while the
                    // list is open, Enter commits and Escape reverts, and Left/Right are
                    // swallowed so they can't sideways-change the value under an open list.
                    if (keyData == Keys.Up) { physUpHeld = true; return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Down) { physDownHeld = true; return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Left || keyData == Keys.Right) { return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Enter || keyData == Keys.Space) { CloseConsoleDropdown(true); return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Escape) { CloseConsoleDropdown(false); return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Tab || keyData == (Keys.Tab | Keys.Shift)) { return true; }
                }
                else if (consoleSidebarFocused)
                {
                    if (keyData == Keys.Up) { physUpHeld = true; return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Down) { physDownHeld = true; return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Right) { physRightHeld = true; return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Left) { return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Enter || keyData == Keys.Space) { ActivateConsoleSidebarSelection(); return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Escape) { LeaveConsoleSidebar(); return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Tab || keyData == (Keys.Tab | Keys.Shift)) { return true; }
                }
                else if (consoleTopBarActive)
                {
                    Control focused = (consoleTopBarControls != null && consoleTopBarIndex >= 0 && consoleTopBarIndex < consoleTopBarControls.Length)
                        ? consoleTopBarControls[consoleTopBarIndex]
                        : null;
                    bool textBoxEditing = focused is TextBox && focused.Focused;

                    if (keyData == Keys.Up) { physUpHeld = true; return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Down) { physDownHeld = true; return true; }
                    // A literal Left/Right while actually typing in the field should move the
                    // text caret, not adjust/repeat-adjust the field's value - same carve-out
                    // as before, just now gating whether the direction ever gets marked held.
                    if (keyData == Keys.Left) { if (textBoxEditing) return false; physLeftHeld = true; return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Right) { if (textBoxEditing) return false; physRightHeld = true; return true; }
                    // A literal space while actually typing should type a space, not
                    // re-trigger Activate - but Space on a not-yet-focused control (or a
                    // dropdown) still acts as the "A button" equivalent, same as Enter.
                    if (keyData == Keys.Space) { if (textBoxEditing) return false; ActivateConsoleTopBarSelection(); return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Enter) { ActivateConsoleTopBarSelection(); return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Escape) { ExitConsoleTopBar(); return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Tab || keyData == (Keys.Tab | Keys.Shift)) { return true; }
                }
                else
                {
                    if (keyData == Keys.Down) { physDownHeld = true; return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Up) { physUpHeld = true; return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Right) { physRightHeld = true; return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Left) { physLeftHeld = true; return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Enter || keyData == Keys.Space) { ActivateConsoleSelection(); return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Escape) { chkConsoleMode.Checked = false; return true; }
                    if (keyData == Keys.Tab || keyData == (Keys.Tab | Keys.Shift)) { return true; }
                }
            }
            else if (listResizeModeActive)
            {
                // Desktop mode has no D-pad/XInput polling loop running (that timer only
                // starts for Console Mode or the virtual keyboard), so this handles resize
                // mode's arrow keys directly off a real physical keyboard instead of routing
                // through physUpHeld/ControllerPollTimer_Tick the way Console Mode does.
                // Down grows the list (dragging its bottom edge further down), Up shrinks it
                // back - the same direction the mouse-drag splitter used to move.
                if (keyData == Keys.Down) { AdjustServerListHeight(lstServerPaks.Height + 20); return true; }
                if (keyData == Keys.Up) { AdjustServerListHeight(lstServerPaks.Height - 20); return true; }
                if (keyData == Keys.Enter || keyData == Keys.Space || keyData == Keys.Escape) { OnToggleListResizeModeClicked(this, EventArgs.Empty); return true; }
            }

            return base.ProcessCmdKey(ref msg, keyData);
        }

        // Clears a direction's "physically held" flag the instant the key is released, so
        // ControllerPollTimer_Tick's hold-to-repeat (AdvanceRepeat) stops for it immediately
        // rather than continuing until some other event happens to reset it. Harmless to fire
        // for keys/contexts where the flag was never set in the first place.
        private void OnConsoleModeKeyUp(object sender, KeyEventArgs e)
        {
            if (e.KeyCode == Keys.Up) physUpHeld = false;
            else if (e.KeyCode == Keys.Down) physDownHeld = false;
            else if (e.KeyCode == Keys.Left) physLeftHeld = false;
            else if (e.KeyCode == Keys.Right) physRightHeld = false;
        }

        private string GetEffectiveEngineIniPath()
        {
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(customEngineIniPath) && File.Exists(customEngineIniPath))
            {
                return customEngineIniPath;
            }

            string defaultPath = Path.Combine(Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.LocalApplicationData), @"MotorTown\Saved\Config\Windows\Engine.ini");
            if (File.Exists(defaultPath))
            {
                return defaultPath;
            }

            return defaultPath;
        }

        private bool EnsureEngineIniExists(out string targetPath)
        {
            targetPath = GetEffectiveEngineIniPath();

            if (File.Exists(targetPath))
            {
                return true;
            }

            DialogResult result = ShowThemedConfirm("Engine.ini Not Found", "Could not locate 'Engine.ini' automatically.\n\nWould you like to browse and locate your 'Engine.ini' file manually?");

            if (result == DialogResult.Yes)
            {
                using (OpenFileDialog ofd = new OpenFileDialog())
                {
                    ofd.Title = "Select Engine.ini File";
                    ofd.Filter = "INI Configuration Files (*.ini)|*.ini|All Files (*.*)|*.*";
                    ofd.FileName = "Engine.ini";

                    if (ofd.ShowDialog(this) == DialogResult.OK)
                    {
                        customEngineIniPath = ofd.FileName;
                        SaveCheckboxSettings();
                        targetPath = customEngineIniPath;
                        return true;
                    }
                }
            }

            return false;
        }

        private void EnsureStorageDirectoryExists()
        {
            try
            {
                if (!Directory.Exists(serverStorageDir))
                    Directory.CreateDirectory(serverStorageDir);
                if (!Directory.Exists(backupStorageDir))
                    Directory.CreateDirectory(backupStorageDir);
                if (!Directory.Exists(saveGameBackupDir))
                    Directory.CreateDirectory(saveGameBackupDir);

                // Wipe any leftover undo cache from a previous run that didn't shut down
                // cleanly (e.g. crashed or was killed) before creating a fresh one - stale
                // cached files from an earlier session have no matching undoHistory entry in
                // this session anyway, so they can never be restored through Undo.
                if (Directory.Exists(undoCacheDir))
                {
                    try { Directory.Delete(undoCacheDir, true); } catch { }
                }
                Directory.CreateDirectory(undoCacheDir);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowError("Initializing Storage Directory", ex);
            }
        }

        private void LoadCheckboxSettings()
        {
            isLoadingSettings = true;
            try
            {
                if (File.Exists(settingsFilePath))
                {
                    string[] lines = File.ReadAllLines(settingsFilePath);
                    foreach (string line in lines)
                    {
                        if (line.StartsWith("SmartMatching=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                        {
                            bool val;
                            if (bool.TryParse(line.Substring(13).Trim(), out val))
                                chkSmartMatching.Checked = val;
                        }
                        else if (line.StartsWith("AutoEngineIni=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                        {
                            bool val;
                            if (bool.TryParse(line.Substring(14).Trim(), out val))
                                chkAutoEngineIni.Checked = val;
                        }
                        else if (line.StartsWith("ConsoleMode=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                        {
                            bool val;
                            if (bool.TryParse(line.Substring(12).Trim(), out val))
                                chkConsoleMode.Checked = val;
                        }
                        else if (line.StartsWith("VirtualKeyboard=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                        {
                            bool val;
                            if (bool.TryParse(line.Substring(16).Trim(), out val))
                                chkVirtualKeyboard.Checked = val;
                        }
                        else if (line.StartsWith("Theme=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                        {
                            string theme = line.Substring(6).Trim();
                            for (int i = 0; i < cboThemeSelector.Items.Count; i++)
                            {
                                if (cboThemeSelector.Items[i].ToString().Equals(theme, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                                {
                                    cboThemeSelector.SelectedIndex = i;
                                    break;
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        else if (line.StartsWith("PreferredEditor=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                        {
                            string editor = line.Substring(16).Trim();
                            for (int i = 0; i < cboEditorSelector.Items.Count; i++)
                            {
                                if (cboEditorSelector.Items[i].ToString().Equals(editor, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                                {
                                    cboEditorSelector.SelectedIndex = i;
                                    break;
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        else if (line.StartsWith("EngineIniPath=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                        {
                            string path = line.Substring(14).Trim();
                            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(path))
                            {
                                customEngineIniPath = path;
                            }
                        }
                        else if (line.StartsWith("SkippedUpdateVersion=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                        {
                            skippedUpdateVersion = line.Substring(21).Trim();
                        }
                        else if (line.StartsWith("LastSeenChangelogVersion=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                        {
                            lastSeenChangelogVersion = line.Substring(25).Trim();
                        }
                        else if (line.StartsWith("ColorBlindMode=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                        {
                            string mode = line.Substring(15).Trim();
                            foreach (string opt in ColorBlindModeOptions)
                            {
                                if (opt.Equals(mode, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) { colorBlindMode = opt; break; }
                            }
                            if (cboColorBlindMode != null)
                            {
                                int idx = cboColorBlindMode.Items.IndexOf(colorBlindMode);
                                if (idx >= 0) cboColorBlindMode.SelectedIndex = idx;
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            catch { }
            finally
            {
                isLoadingSettings = false;
            }
        }

        private void SaveCheckboxSettings()
        {
            // Skip writes triggered by LoadCheckboxSettings itself assigning values to
            // controls (see isLoadingSettings' declaration comment) - saving mid-load would
            // persist fields the load loop hasn't reached yet, corrupting the file with their
            // stale "" defaults. LoadCheckboxSettings clears this flag once it's fully done,
            // at which point every field it read is already in memory, so nothing is lost by
            // skipping these - the real settings only ever change starting from that point on.
            if (isLoadingSettings) return;

            try
            {
                string themeName = (cboThemeSelector.SelectedItem != null) ? cboThemeSelector.SelectedItem.ToString() : "Dark Mode";
                string editorName = (cboEditorSelector.SelectedItem != null) ? cboEditorSelector.SelectedItem.ToString() : "Windows Notepad";
                string iniPathEntry = !string.IsNullOrEmpty(customEngineIniPath) ? customEngineIniPath : "";
                
                string content = "SmartMatching=" + chkSmartMatching.Checked.ToString() + "\n" +
                                 "AutoEngineIni=" + chkAutoEngineIni.Checked.ToString() + "\n" +
                                 "ConsoleMode=" + chkConsoleMode.Checked.ToString() + "\n" +
                                 "VirtualKeyboard=" + chkVirtualKeyboard.Checked.ToString() + "\n" +
                                 "Theme=" + themeName + "\n" +
                                 "PreferredEditor=" + editorName + "\n" +
                                 "EngineIniPath=" + iniPathEntry + "\n" +
                                 "SkippedUpdateVersion=" + skippedUpdateVersion + "\n" +
                                 "LastSeenChangelogVersion=" + lastSeenChangelogVersion + "\n" +
                                 "ColorBlindMode=" + colorBlindMode + "\n";
                File.WriteAllText(settingsFilePath, content);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowError("Saving Checkbox Settings", ex);
            }
        }

        private void InitializeComponentLayout()
        {
            // Every header sits 25px above its field rather than 20px. The focus ring is
            // drawn 5px outside the field on every side, so at 20px the ring's top edge landed
            // exactly on the header's baseline and the two visibly collided.
            lblPathHeader = new Label { Text = "Game Paks Directory:", Location = new Point(15, 10), AutoSize = true, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold) };
            Controls.Add(lblPathHeader);

            txtGamePath = new TextBox { Location = new Point(15, 35), Width = 310, BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right };
            // Browsing for a folder (OnBrowsePathClicked) was the only way editing this field
            // actually got saved to ConfigFileName - typing straight into the box (desktop
            // mode, real keyboard) changed txtGamePath.Text immediately but never called
            // PersistConfigPath, so the edit silently didn't survive a relaunch. Leave fires
            // once the box actually stops being the focused control (tabbing/clicking away,
            // or Enter moving focus), which is the natural "done editing" moment for a real
            // keyboard - the on-screen keyboard's own edits are covered separately in
            // HideVirtualKeyboard, since that path never gives this box real focus back.
            txtGamePath.Leave += delegate { PersistConfigPath(txtGamePath.Text.Trim()); };
            Controls.Add(txtGamePath);

            btnBrowsePath = new ShinyButton { Text = "Browse...", Location = new Point(335, 33), Width = 90, Height = 25, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Right };
            btnBrowsePath.Click += OnBrowsePathClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnBrowsePath);

            btnOpenDirectory = new ShinyButton { Text = "Open Folder", Location = new Point(430, 33), Width = 90, Height = 25, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Right };
            btnOpenDirectory.Click += OnOpenDirectoryClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnOpenDirectory);

            btnUpdateIcon = new DoubleBufferedPanel
            {
                Location = new Point(501, 6),
                Size = new Size(24, 24),
                Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Right,
                Cursor = Cursors.Hand,
                Visible = false
            };
            btnUpdateIcon.Paint += UpdateIcon_Paint;
            // Clicking the corner icon shows the full changelog dialog (same one shown
            // automatically when an update is first detected) instead of a bare "update
            // available?" confirm box, so re-opening it always reflects the current
            // skip/update choices instead of a separate dialog that ignored them.
            btnUpdateIcon.Click += delegate { ShowUpdateChangelogDialog(); };
            Controls.Add(btnUpdateIcon);
            btnUpdateIcon.BringToFront();
            cornerIconToolTip.SetToolTip(btnUpdateIcon, "Update Available");

            // Sits at the update icon's normal spot (501,6) and slides left of it whenever the
            // update icon becomes visible, so the two never overlap - see
            // RepositionSettingsGear, called both here and from ShowUpdateIcon.
            btnSettingsGear = new DoubleBufferedPanel
            {
                Size = new Size(24, 24),
                Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Right,
                Cursor = Cursors.Hand
            };
            btnSettingsGear.Paint += SettingsGear_Paint;
            btnSettingsGear.Click += delegate { ShowSettingsDialog(); };
            Controls.Add(btnSettingsGear);
            btnSettingsGear.BringToFront();
            cornerIconToolTip.SetToolTip(btnSettingsGear, "Settings");

            // Corner Undo icon - same always-on-top corner group as the settings gear and
            // update icon, sitting immediately to the gear's left, so the last mod action can
            // be undone from anywhere without hunting for it inside a category's tile list.
            btnUndoIcon = new DoubleBufferedPanel
            {
                Size = new Size(24, 24),
                Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Right,
                Cursor = Cursors.Hand
            };
            // Painted the same way as the update icon (filled accent disc + contrasting
            // glyph) instead of a bare orange outline on the window background, so all four
            // corner icons read as one matching set - and so the icon stays visible in Light
            // Mode, where the old flat Color.Gray outline nearly disappeared.
            btnUndoIcon.Paint += delegate(object s, PaintEventArgs pe) { PaintCornerIcon(pe, ConsoleIconKind.Undo); };
            btnUndoIcon.Click += OnUndoLastActionClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnUndoIcon);
            btnUndoIcon.BringToFront();
            // These are owner-drawn Panels, not Buttons - without an explicit tooltip there is
            // nothing anywhere on screen telling you which curved arrow is undo and which redo.
            cornerIconToolTip.SetToolTip(btnUndoIcon, "Undo");

            // Corner Redo icon - sits immediately to the right of Undo (between it and the
            // Settings gear), re-deleting whatever the most recent Undo just restored.
            btnRedoIcon = new DoubleBufferedPanel
            {
                Size = new Size(24, 24),
                Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Right,
                Cursor = Cursors.Hand
            };
            btnRedoIcon.Paint += delegate(object s, PaintEventArgs pe) { PaintCornerIcon(pe, ConsoleIconKind.Redo); };
            btnRedoIcon.Click += OnRedoLastActionClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnRedoIcon);
            btnRedoIcon.BringToFront();
            cornerIconToolTip.SetToolTip(btnRedoIcon, "Redo");

            // Corner Discord icon - sits immediately to the LEFT of Undo (the outermost slot
            // in the always-on-top corner group next to Update), one slot further left than
            // Undo/Redo/Settings. Part of the same sliding group as the rest (see
            // RepositionSettingsGear), so it shifts with everything else depending on whether
            // the Update icon is currently claiming the group's outermost spot.
            btnDiscordIcon = new DoubleBufferedPanel
