            {
                Size = new Size(24, 24),
                Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Right,
                Cursor = Cursors.Hand
            };
            btnDiscordIcon.Paint += delegate(object s, PaintEventArgs pe) { PaintCornerIcon(pe, ConsoleIconKind.Discord); };
            btnDiscordIcon.Click += delegate
            {
                try { Process.Start(DiscordInviteUrl); }
                catch (Exception ex) { ShowError("Opening Discord Invite", ex); }
            };
            Controls.Add(btnDiscordIcon);
            btnDiscordIcon.BringToFront();
            cornerIconToolTip.SetToolTip(btnDiscordIcon, "Join Our Discord");

            RepositionSettingsGear();

            lblThemeHeader = new Label { Text = "Theme:", Location = new Point(15, 65), AutoSize = true, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold) };
            Controls.Add(lblThemeHeader);

            cboThemeSelector = new ComboBox { Location = new Point(15, 90), Width = 505, DropDownStyle = ComboBoxStyle.DropDownList, DrawMode = DrawMode.OwnerDrawFixed, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right };
            cboThemeSelector.DrawItem += ThemedComboBox_DrawItem;
            cboThemeSelector.Items.Add("Dark Mode");
            cboThemeSelector.Items.Add("Light Mode");
            cboThemeSelector.Items.Add("Cerulean Blue");
            cboThemeSelector.Items.Add("Amethyst Purple");
            cboThemeSelector.SelectedIndexChanged += delegate(object s, EventArgs e) 
            { 
                if (cboThemeSelector.SelectedItem != null) 
                {
                    ApplyTheme(cboThemeSelector.SelectedItem.ToString());
                    SaveCheckboxSettings();
                } 
                UpdateDropDownDisplays();
            };
            Controls.Add(cboThemeSelector);

            // Kept alive as the list + selection, but never shown: btnThemeDropDown below is
            // what the user actually sees and clicks.
            cboThemeSelector.Visible = false;

            btnThemeDropDown = new ShinyButton
            {
                Location = new Point(15, 90),
                Width = 505,
                Height = 24,
                FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
                DropDownField = true,
                Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9f, FontStyle.Regular),
                Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right
            };
            btnThemeDropDown.Click += delegate
            {
                // Console Mode keeps the big controller-navigable picker; ordinary desktop/
                // mouse use gets a small themed list that opens right under the field instead,
                // the same way a native ComboBox's own drop-down would.
                if (chkConsoleMode != null && chkConsoleMode.Checked) { OpenConsoleThemePicker(); return; }

                List<string> themes = new List<string>();
                foreach (object item in cboThemeSelector.Items) themes.Add(item.ToString());
                ShowThemedDropdown(btnThemeDropDown, themes, CurrentThemeName(), delegate(string chosen)
                {
                    cboThemeSelector.SelectedItem = chosen;
                });
            };
            Controls.Add(btnThemeDropDown);

            // Now lives in the Settings dialog (opened via the gear icon) instead of its own
            // row here - it's created unparented and only gets added into that dialog's
            // Controls each time it's opened (see ShowSettingsDialog), since the checkbox
            // object itself needs to keep existing/wired for the app's whole lifetime
            // regardless of which window is currently showing it.
            chkConsoleMode = new CheckBox
            {
                Text = "Console Mode (Steam Deck)",
                AutoSize = true,
                Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9f, FontStyle.Regular)
            };
            chkConsoleMode.CheckedChanged += OnConsoleModeChanged;

            // Also unparented like chkConsoleMode above - lives in the Settings dialog and
            // only gets added into its Controls each time that dialog is opened.
            chkVirtualKeyboard = new CheckBox
            {
                Text = VirtualKeyboardBaseLabel + "  (ON)",
                AutoSize = true,
                Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9f, FontStyle.Regular)
            };
            chkVirtualKeyboard.CheckedChanged += delegate
            {
                // The checkmark alone already shows the state, but it's easy to miss at a
                // glance (especially at Steam Deck viewing distance) - an explicit (ON)/(OFF)
                // suffix on the label itself, matching the Console Mode Settings menu's own
                // "On-Screen Virtual Keyboard:  ON/OFF" entry, makes the state readable without
                // having to spot a small checkbox glyph.
                chkVirtualKeyboard.Text = VirtualKeyboardBaseLabel + (chkVirtualKeyboard.Checked ? "  (ON)" : "  (OFF)");
                // Turning the setting off while the keyboard happens to be showing should
                // close it immediately rather than leaving an now-orphaned feature on screen.
                if (!chkVirtualKeyboard.Checked) HideVirtualKeyboard();
                SaveCheckboxSettings();
            };

            // Also unparented like chkConsoleMode/chkVirtualKeyboard above - the desktop-mode
            // colorblindness picker. Uses the same owner-drawn ComboBox styling as the Theme/
            // Editor selectors (ThemedComboBox_DrawItem) so it reads as a "custom themed drop
            // down" rather than a stock Windows combo box. Console Mode gets its own version
            // of this same choice as a picker submenu instead - see ShowConsoleColorBlindMenu.
            lblColorBlindHeader = new Label { Text = "Color Blindness Mode:", AutoSize = true, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold) };
            cboColorBlindMode = new ComboBox { Width = 360, DropDownStyle = ComboBoxStyle.DropDownList, DrawMode = DrawMode.OwnerDrawFixed, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9f, FontStyle.Regular) };
            foreach (string opt in ColorBlindModeOptions) cboColorBlindMode.Items.Add(opt);
            cboColorBlindMode.SelectedItem = colorBlindMode;
            cboColorBlindMode.DrawItem += ThemedComboBox_DrawItem;
            cboColorBlindMode.SelectedIndexChanged += delegate
            {
                if (cboColorBlindMode.SelectedItem == null) return;
                colorBlindMode = cboColorBlindMode.SelectedItem.ToString();
                SaveCheckboxSettings();
                ApplyTheme(CurrentThemeName());
            };

            lblServerHeader = new Label { Text = "Select / Search Target Server:", Location = new Point(15, 120), AutoSize = true, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold) };
            Controls.Add(lblServerHeader);

            txtServerSearchBox = new TextBox { Location = new Point(15, 145), Width = 160, BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left };
            txtServerSearchBox.TextChanged += OnServerSearchChanged;
            Controls.Add(txtServerSearchBox);

            cboServerDropdown = new ComboBox { Location = new Point(180, 145), Width = 340, DropDownStyle = ComboBoxStyle.DropDownList, DrawMode = DrawMode.OwnerDrawFixed, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right };
            cboServerDropdown.DrawItem += ThemedComboBox_DrawItem;
            cboServerDropdown.SelectedIndexChanged += delegate(object s, EventArgs e) { LoadSelectedServerPaks(); UpdateDropDownDisplays(); };
            Controls.Add(cboServerDropdown);

            cboServerDropdown.Visible = false;

            btnServerDropDown = new ShinyButton
            {
                Location = new Point(180, 145),
                Width = 340,
                Height = 24,
                FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
                DropDownField = true,
                Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9f, FontStyle.Regular),
                Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right
            };
            btnServerDropDown.Click += delegate
            {
                // Same desktop-vs-console split as the Theme field above.
                if (chkConsoleMode != null && chkConsoleMode.Checked) { OpenConsoleServerPicker(); return; }

                List<string> serverItems = new List<string>();
                foreach (object item in cboServerDropdown.Items) serverItems.Add(item.ToString());
                string current = (cboServerDropdown.SelectedItem != null) ? cboServerDropdown.SelectedItem.ToString() : null;
                ShowThemedDropdown(btnServerDropDown, serverItems, current, delegate(string chosen)
                {
                    cboServerDropdown.SelectedItem = chosen;
                });
            };
            Controls.Add(btnServerDropDown);

            lblModSearchHeader = new Label { Text = "Search Mods:", Location = new Point(15, 175), AutoSize = true, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold) };
            Controls.Add(lblModSearchHeader);

            txtModSearchBox = new TextBox { Location = new Point(15, 200), Width = 160, BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left };
            txtModSearchBox.TextChanged += OnModSearchChanged;
            Controls.Add(txtModSearchBox);

            lstServerPaks = new ListBox { Location = new Point(15, 235), Width = 505, Height = 79, BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right };
            Controls.Add(lstServerPaks);

            btnAddServerFolder = new ShinyButton { Text = "Add Server", Location = new Point(15, 342), Width = 94, Height = 28, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 8f, FontStyle.Bold) };
            btnAddServerFolder.Click += OnAddServerClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnAddServerFolder);

            btnDeleteServerFolder = new ShinyButton { Text = "Delete Server", Location = new Point(115, 342), Width = 94, Height = 28, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 8f, FontStyle.Bold) };
            btnDeleteServerFolder.Click += OnDeleteServerClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnDeleteServerFolder);

            btnDeleteSelectedPak = new ShinyButton { Text = "Delete Mod", Location = new Point(215, 342), Width = 94, Height = 28, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 8f, FontStyle.Bold) };
            btnDeleteSelectedPak.Click += OnDeleteModClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnDeleteSelectedPak);

            // Undoes the most recent server/mod deletion (repeatable - keeps popping the undo
            // history one step at a time). Deletions move the file/folder into undoCacheDir
            // instead of actually deleting it, so this just moves it back. Disabled/relabeled
            // by UpdateUndoButtonState() whenever the history is empty.
            btnUndoLastAction = new ShinyButton { Text = "Undo", Location = new Point(315, 342), Width = 94, Height = 28, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 8f, FontStyle.Bold), Enabled = false };
            btnUndoLastAction.Click += OnUndoLastActionClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnUndoLastAction);

            btnMergeServerMods = new ShinyButton { Text = "Merge Servers", Location = new Point(415, 342), Width = 105, Height = 28, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 8f, FontStyle.Bold) };
            btnMergeServerMods.Click += OnMergeServerModsClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnMergeServerMods);

            btnDeployMods = new ShinyButton { Text = "Deploy Mods To Game", Location = new Point(15, 380), Width = 505, Height = 30, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9.5f, FontStyle.Bold) };
            btnDeployMods.Click += OnDeployModsClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnDeployMods);

            btnRevertVanilla = new ShinyButton { Text = "Remove All Mods (Vanilla)", Location = new Point(15, 418), Width = 505, Height = 30, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9.5f, FontStyle.Bold) };
            btnRevertVanilla.Click += OnRevertVanillaClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnRevertVanilla);

            btnBackupPaks = new ShinyButton { Text = "Backup Main Game File", Location = new Point(15, 456), Width = 245, Height = 30, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold) };
            btnBackupPaks.Click += OnBackupPaksClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnBackupPaks);

            btnRestoreBackup = new ShinyButton { Text = "Restore Main Game File", Location = new Point(275, 456), Width = 245, Height = 30, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Right, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold) };
            btnRestoreBackup.Click += OnRestoreBackupClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnRestoreBackup);

            btnBackupSaves = new ShinyButton { Text = "Backup Character Saves", Location = new Point(15, 494), Width = 245, Height = 30, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold) };
            btnBackupSaves.Click += OnBackupSavesClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnBackupSaves);

            btnManageSaves = new ShinyButton { Text = "Manage / Restore Saves", Location = new Point(275, 494), Width = 245, Height = 30, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Right, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold) };
            btnManageSaves.Click += OnManageSavesClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnManageSaves);

            lblEditorHeader = new Label { Text = "Preferred Text Editor:", Location = new Point(15, 533), AutoSize = true, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold) };
            Controls.Add(lblEditorHeader);

            cboEditorSelector = new ComboBox { Location = new Point(15, 553), Width = 505, DropDownStyle = ComboBoxStyle.DropDownList, DrawMode = DrawMode.OwnerDrawFixed, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right };
            cboEditorSelector.DrawItem += ThemedComboBox_DrawItem;
            cboEditorSelector.Items.Add("Windows Notepad");
            cboEditorSelector.Items.Add("Notepad++");
            cboEditorSelector.Items.Add("VS Code");
            cboEditorSelector.SelectedIndexChanged += delegate(object s, EventArgs e) 
            { 
                UpdateOpenEngineIniButtonText();
                SaveCheckboxSettings();
            };
            Controls.Add(cboEditorSelector);

            btnOpenEngineIni = new ShinyButton { Text = "Open Engine.ini in Windows Notepad", Location = new Point(15, 588), Width = 505, Height = 28, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold) };
            btnOpenEngineIni.Click += OnOpenEngineIniClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnOpenEngineIni);

            btnOpenSaveDirectory = new ShinyButton { Text = "Open Save File Folder", Location = new Point(15, 622), Width = 505, Height = 28, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold) };
            btnOpenSaveDirectory.Click += OnOpenSaveDirectoryClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnOpenSaveDirectory);

            btnLaunchGame = new ShinyButton { Text = "Launch Motor Town (Steam)", Location = new Point(15, 658), Width = 505, Height = 32, FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat, Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9.5f, FontStyle.Bold) };
            btnLaunchGame.Click += OnLaunchGameClicked;
            Controls.Add(btnLaunchGame);

            chkSmartMatching = new CheckBox
            {
                Text = "Enable Smart Version Matching (Auto-detect older mod versions)",
                Location = new Point(15, 698),
                Width = 505,
                Checked = true,
                Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Regular),
                Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right
            };
            chkSmartMatching.CheckedChanged += OnCheckboxSettingChanged;
            Controls.Add(chkSmartMatching);

            chkAutoEngineIni = new CheckBox
            {
                Text = "Enable Auto Engine.ini Smart-Merge on Zip Drop",
                Location = new Point(15, 728),
                Width = 505,
                Checked = true,
                Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Regular),
                Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right
            };
            chkAutoEngineIni.CheckedChanged += OnCheckboxSettingChanged;
            Controls.Add(chkAutoEngineIni);

            pnlDropTarget = new Panel
            {
                Location = new Point(15, 762),
                Width = 505,
                Height = 155,
                BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle,
                AllowDrop = true,
                Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right
            };

            lblDropInstruction = new Label
            {
                Text = "Drag and Drop .pak, .zip or ReadMe Files Here\n\n(Auto-extracts Paks, Reads Readmes & Smart-Merges Engine.ini)",
                Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 10, FontStyle.Bold),
                Dock = DockStyle.Fill,
                TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleCenter,
                AllowDrop = true,
                BackColor = Color.Transparent
            };

            pnlDropTarget.Controls.Add(lblDropInstruction);

            Controls.Add(pnlDropTarget);

            AttachSearchIcon(txtServerSearchBox);
            AttachSearchIcon(txtModSearchBox);

            // Order matters here: Console Mode's "top bar" (the search boxes/dropdowns above
            // its tile overlay) needs these four controls to already exist.
            // txtGamePath is included so Console Mode can actually reach the paks-directory
            // field with a controller - it had the virtual keyboard wired to its GotFocus all
            // along, but with no way to ever focus it there was no way to trigger that.
            // txtServerSearchBox is deliberately NOT in here: in Console Mode it is hidden
            // outright, because its job is done far better by the search row built into the
            // server picker (ShowConsolePicker) - one stop in this list instead of two, and a
            // full-size field with a result grid under it instead of a 160px box feeding a
            // dropdown sitting beside it.
            consoleTopBarControls = new Control[] { txtGamePath, btnThemeDropDown, btnServerDropDown, txtModSearchBox };

            // A single reusable outline that jumps to wrap whichever top-bar control is
            // currently focused via controller, instead of a separate highlight panel per
            // control - only one of the four can ever be focused at a time anyway.
            pnlTopBarFocusHighlight = new DoubleBufferedPanel
            {
                Visible = false,
                BackColor = Color.Transparent
            };
            pnlTopBarFocusHighlight.Paint += delegate(object s, PaintEventArgs pe)
            {
                pe.Graphics.SmoothingMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.SmoothingMode.AntiAlias;
                // 3px instead of 2px, drawn one pixel further in, with RefreshConsoleTopBar
                // Highlight now leaving a 5px margin instead of 3px - the old ring was thin
                // enough to be easy to lose track of on a Steam Deck screen.
                using (Pen pen = new Pen(FocusRingColor(), 3f))
                {
                    pe.Graphics.DrawRectangle(pen, 2, 2, pnlTopBarFocusHighlight.Width - 5, pnlTopBarFocusHighlight.Height - 5);
                }
            };
            Controls.Add(pnlTopBarFocusHighlight);

            AttachVirtualKeyboardOnFocus(txtGamePath);
            AttachVirtualKeyboardOnFocus(txtServerSearchBox);
            AttachVirtualKeyboardOnFocus(txtModSearchBox);

            LayoutActionButtonRow();
            BuildConsoleTilesPanel();
            BuildVirtualKeyboard();
        }

        // Covers the same region as every action button/checkbox/drop-zone below the mod list
        // (y=342 down through the bottom of the drop target) with one big opaque panel full of
        // large, controller-navigable tiles. It's built as an overlay rather than by hiding
        // each of those ~15 controls individually - being on top in Z-order and fully opaque
        // means it already blocks mouse clicks from reaching whatever's underneath, so toggling
        // one panel's Visible is enough instead of touching every control below it.
        // Builds the whole Console Mode dashboard: a prominent "Launch Game" bar across the
        // top, a sidebar of category tabs (Mods/Servers/Backups/Utility) on the left, and the
        // selected category's tiles on the right - replacing the old single 14-tile vertical
        // stack, which took several D-pad presses to reach anything near the bottom.
        private void BuildConsoleTilesPanel()
        {
            int top = btnAddServerFolder.Top;
            int bottom = pnlDropTarget.Bottom;

            pnlConsoleTiles = new Panel
            {
                Location = new Point(15, top),
                Size = new Size(505, bottom - top),
                Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right,
                Visible = false,
                TabStop = true
            };
            Controls.Add(pnlConsoleTiles);

            // A compact, always-visible reminder of the controls this app actually wires up
            // (see ProcessCmdKey and ControllerPollTimer_Tick) - D-pad/arrows to move, A/Enter
            // to pick, B/Esc to back out - so a controller-only session never has to guess.
            lblConsoleControlHint = new Label
            {
                Text = "\u2195 Navigate    \u2190 Menu Tabs    (A) / Enter: Select    (B) / Esc: Back",
                TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleCenter,
                Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 8.5f, FontStyle.Regular)
            };
            pnlConsoleTiles.Controls.Add(lblConsoleControlHint);

            btnConsoleLaunchGame = new ShinyButton
            {
                Text = "\u25B6 Launch Motor Town (Steam)",
                Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 12f, FontStyle.Bold),
                FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat
            };
            btnConsoleLaunchGame.Click += OnLaunchGameClicked;
            pnlConsoleTiles.Controls.Add(btnConsoleLaunchGame);

            pnlConsoleSidebar = new Panel { BackColor = Color.Transparent };
            pnlConsoleContent = new Panel { BackColor = Color.Transparent };
            pnlConsoleTiles.Controls.Add(pnlConsoleSidebar);
            pnlConsoleTiles.Controls.Add(pnlConsoleContent);

            // Same fixed order as consoleCategoryNames (Mods, Servers, Backups, Utility).
            ConsoleIconKind[] categoryIcons = { ConsoleIconKind.Mods, ConsoleIconKind.Servers, ConsoleIconKind.Backups, ConsoleIconKind.Utility };

            for (int i = 0; i < consoleCategoryNames.Length; i++)
            {
                int capturedIndex = i;
                ShinyButton catButton = new ShinyButton
                {
                    Text = consoleCategoryNames[i],
                    Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9.5f, FontStyle.Bold),
                    FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
                    Icon = categoryIcons[i],
                    IconAboveText = true
                };
                catButton.Click += delegate { SwitchConsoleCategory(capturedIndex - selectedConsoleCategoryIndex); };
                consoleCategoryButtons.Add(catButton);
                pnlConsoleSidebar.Controls.Add(catButton);
            }

            // Mods, Servers, Backups, Utility - reusing the exact same handlers already wired
            // to the normal buttons, so nothing about how these actions work is duplicated.
            consoleCategoryTileLabels = new string[][]
            {
                new string[] { "Add Mod", "Delete Mod", "Deploy Mods To Game", "Remove All Mods (Vanilla)", "Undo" },
                new string[] { "Add Server", "Delete Server", "Merge Servers" },
                new string[] { "Backup Main Game File", "Restore Main Game File", "Backup Character Saves", "Manage / Restore Saves" },
                new string[] { "Open Engine.ini", "Open Save Folder", "Settings" }
            };

            consoleCategoryTileHandlers = new EventHandler[][]
            {
                new EventHandler[] { OnConsoleAddModClicked, OnDeleteModClicked, OnDeployModsClicked, OnRevertVanillaClicked, OnUndoLastActionClicked },
                new EventHandler[] { OnAddServerClicked, OnDeleteServerClicked, OnMergeServerModsClicked },
                new EventHandler[] { OnBackupPaksClicked, OnRestoreBackupClicked, OnBackupSavesClicked, OnManageSavesClicked },
                new EventHandler[] { OnOpenEngineIniClicked, OnOpenSaveDirectoryClicked, delegate { ShowSettingsDialog(); } }
            };

            // Same shape as consoleCategoryTileLabels/Handlers above, one icon per tile.
            consoleCategoryTileIcons = new ConsoleIconKind[][]
            {
                new ConsoleIconKind[] { ConsoleIconKind.AddPlus, ConsoleIconKind.Trash, ConsoleIconKind.DeployBox, ConsoleIconKind.Refresh, ConsoleIconKind.Undo },
                new ConsoleIconKind[] { ConsoleIconKind.AddPlus, ConsoleIconKind.Trash, ConsoleIconKind.Merge },
                new ConsoleIconKind[] { ConsoleIconKind.Save, ConsoleIconKind.Restore, ConsoleIconKind.Save, ConsoleIconKind.Folder },
                new ConsoleIconKind[] { ConsoleIconKind.File, ConsoleIconKind.Folder, ConsoleIconKind.Gear }
            };

            RebuildConsoleCategoryContent();
            LayoutConsoleTiles();
        }

        // Tears down and rebuilds pnlConsoleContent's tiles for whichever category is
        // currently selected - called on category switch, and once at startup.
        private void RebuildConsoleCategoryContent()
        {
            pnlConsoleContent.Controls.Clear();
            consoleTileButtons.Clear();
            listResizeModeActive = false;

            string[] labels = consoleCategoryTileLabels[selectedConsoleCategoryIndex];
            EventHandler[] handlers = consoleCategoryTileHandlers[selectedConsoleCategoryIndex];
            ConsoleIconKind[] icons = consoleCategoryTileIcons[selectedConsoleCategoryIndex];

            for (int i = 0; i < labels.Length; i++)
            {
                int capturedIndex = i;
                ShinyButton tile = new ShinyButton
                {
                    Text = labels[i],
                    Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 10f, FontStyle.Bold),
                    FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
                    Icon = icons[i],
                    IconAboveText = false
                };
                tile.Click += handlers[i];
                tile.MouseEnter += delegate { selectedConsoleTileIndex = capturedIndex; consoleLaunchFocused = false; consoleResizeFocused = false; consoleSidebarFocused = false; RefreshConsoleHighlights(); };
                consoleTileButtons.Add(tile);
                pnlConsoleContent.Controls.Add(tile);
            }

            LayoutConsoleContentTiles();
        }

        // Structural layout - the launch bar, sidebar, and content container. Called on
        // creation and on every window resize, same as LayoutActionButtonRow.
        private void LayoutConsoleTiles()
        {
            if (pnlConsoleTiles == null) return;

            const int hintHeight = 18;
            const int launchHeight = 50;
            const int gap = 8;
            const int sidebarWidth = 120;

            int fullWidth = pnlConsoleTiles.ClientSize.Width;
            int fullHeight = pnlConsoleTiles.ClientSize.Height;

            lblConsoleControlHint.Location = new Point(0, 0);
            lblConsoleControlHint.Size = new Size(fullWidth, hintHeight);

            btnConsoleLaunchGame.Location = new Point(0, hintHeight + 2);
            btnConsoleLaunchGame.Size = new Size(fullWidth, launchHeight);

            int lowerY = hintHeight + 2 + launchHeight + gap;
            int lowerHeight = Math.Max(40, fullHeight - lowerY);

            pnlConsoleSidebar.Location = new Point(0, lowerY);
            pnlConsoleSidebar.Size = new Size(sidebarWidth, lowerHeight);

            pnlConsoleContent.Location = new Point(sidebarWidth + gap, lowerY);
            pnlConsoleContent.Size = new Size(Math.Max(40, fullWidth - sidebarWidth - gap), lowerHeight);

            LayoutConsoleSidebarButtons();
            LayoutConsoleContentTiles();
        }

        private void LayoutConsoleSidebarButtons()
        {
            if (pnlConsoleSidebar == null || consoleCategoryButtons.Count == 0) return;

            const int gap = 4;
            const int maxTileHeight = 90;
            int count = consoleCategoryButtons.Count;
            int tileHeight = Math.Min(maxTileHeight, Math.Max(20, (pnlConsoleSidebar.ClientSize.Height - gap * (count - 1)) / count));
            int tileWidth = pnlConsoleSidebar.ClientSize.Width;

            int y = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < count; i++)
            {
                consoleCategoryButtons[i].Location = new Point(0, y);
                consoleCategoryButtons[i].Size = new Size(tileWidth, tileHeight);
                y += tileHeight + gap;
            }
        }

        private void LayoutConsoleContentTiles()
        {
            if (pnlConsoleContent == null || consoleTileButtons.Count == 0) return;

            const int gap = 4;
            const int maxTileHeight = 90;
            int count = consoleTileButtons.Count;
            int tileHeight = Math.Min(maxTileHeight, Math.Max(20, (pnlConsoleContent.ClientSize.Height - gap * (count - 1)) / count));
            int tileWidth = pnlConsoleContent.ClientSize.Width;

            int y = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < count; i++)
            {
                consoleTileButtons[i].Location = new Point(0, y);
                consoleTileButtons[i].Size = new Size(tileWidth, tileHeight);
                y += tileHeight + gap;
            }
        }

        // Left/Right (or a shoulder button) - always changes category, live, regardless of
        // whether the current selection is on a content tile or the Launch Game button.
        private void SwitchConsoleCategory(int delta)
        {
            if (listResizeModeActive) return;

            int count = consoleCategoryNames.Length;
            selectedConsoleCategoryIndex = (selectedConsoleCategoryIndex + delta + count) % count;
            selectedConsoleTileIndex = 0;
            consoleLaunchFocused = false;
            consoleResizeFocused = false;
            // Also reachable by clicking a sidebar tab with the mouse, so the sidebar cursor
            // has to be re-synced here rather than only in ActivateConsoleSidebarSelection.
            consoleSidebarFocused = false;
            consoleSidebarIndex = selectedConsoleCategoryIndex;
            RebuildConsoleCategoryContent();
            RefreshConsoleHighlights();
        }

        // --- Console Mode sidebar focus zone ---
        // Left from the content tiles parks focus on the category sidebar. Browsing it with
        // Up/Down deliberately does NOT switch category - nothing happens until A/Enter - so a
        // controller user can look down the tab list without the content panel churning
        // underneath them on every press (which is what Left/Right switching used to do).

        private void EnterConsoleSidebar()
        {
            if (consoleCategoryButtons.Count == 0 || listResizeModeActive) return;
            consoleSidebarFocused = true;
            consoleSidebarIndex = selectedConsoleCategoryIndex;
            consoleLaunchFocused = false;
            consoleResizeFocused = false;
            RefreshConsoleHighlights();
        }

        private void LeaveConsoleSidebar()
        {
            consoleSidebarFocused = false;
            RefreshConsoleHighlights();
        }

        private void MoveConsoleSidebarSelection(int delta)
        {
            int count = consoleCategoryButtons.Count;
            if (count == 0) return;
            consoleSidebarIndex = (consoleSidebarIndex + delta + count) % count;
            RefreshConsoleHighlights();
        }

        // A/Enter on a highlighted sidebar tab is what actually commits to that category, then
        // drops focus onto its first tile so Up/Down immediately navigates the submenu.
        private void ActivateConsoleSidebarSelection()
        {
            int delta = consoleSidebarIndex - selectedConsoleCategoryIndex;
            consoleSidebarFocused = false;
            if (delta != 0)
            {
                SwitchConsoleCategory(delta);
            }
            else
            {
                selectedConsoleTileIndex = 0;
                consoleLaunchFocused = false;
                consoleResizeFocused = false;
                RefreshConsoleHighlights();
            }
        }

        // --- Console Mode dropdown handling ---
        // A on a highlighted dropdown now genuinely opens it (DroppedDown), Up/Down move the
        // open list's highlight, A commits, B reverts to whatever was selected when it opened.
        // Previously A only focused the box and Left/Right silently cycled its value with the
        // list never opening at all, so there was no way to see the options you were skipping.

        private ComboBox CurrentConsoleTopBarCombo()
        {
            if (consoleTopBarControls == null || consoleTopBarIndex < 0 || consoleTopBarIndex >= consoleTopBarControls.Length) return null;
            return consoleTopBarControls[consoleTopBarIndex] as ComboBox;
        }

        private void OpenConsoleDropdown(ComboBox combo)
        {
            if (combo == null) return;
            combo.Focus();
            consoleDropdownOriginalIndex = combo.SelectedIndex;
            combo.DroppedDown = true;
            consoleDropdownOpen = true;
        }

        private void MoveConsoleDropdownSelection(int delta)
        {
            ComboBox combo = CurrentConsoleTopBarCombo();
            if (combo == null || combo.Items.Count == 0) return;

            // Clamped rather than wrapped, so holding a direction parks at the end of the list
            // instead of silently looping past it.
            int newIndex = Math.Max(0, Math.Min(combo.Items.Count - 1, combo.SelectedIndex + delta));
            if (newIndex != combo.SelectedIndex) combo.SelectedIndex = newIndex;
        }

        private void CloseConsoleDropdown(bool commit)
        {
            ComboBox combo = CurrentConsoleTopBarCombo();
            consoleDropdownOpen = false;

            if (combo != null)
            {
                if (!commit && consoleDropdownOriginalIndex >= 0 && consoleDropdownOriginalIndex < combo.Items.Count
                    && combo.SelectedIndex != consoleDropdownOriginalIndex)
                {
                    combo.SelectedIndex = consoleDropdownOriginalIndex;
                }
                combo.DroppedDown = false;
            }

            consoleDropdownOriginalIndex = -1;
            RefreshConsoleTopBarHighlight();
        }

        // Up/Down - moves within the current category's tiles, and hands off to/from the
        // Launch Game button at the top of the list (Up from the first tile focuses Launch,
        // Down from Launch returns to the first tile). The permanent "Resize Mod List" button
        // sits one further stop above Launch Game (see consoleResizeFocused's field comment),
        // and the top bar is one stop above that.
        private void MoveConsoleTileSelection(int delta)
        {
            if (consoleTileButtons.Count == 0) return;

            // Focus is parked on the Resize Mod List button - Up hands off to the top bar,
            // Down returns to Launch Game.
            if (consoleResizeFocused)
            {
                if (delta < 0)
                {
                    EnterConsoleTopBar(fromBottom: true);
                }
                else
                {
                    consoleResizeFocused = false;
                    consoleLaunchFocused = true;
                    RefreshConsoleHighlights();
                }
                return;
            }

            // Pressing Up while already at the very top of the tile grid (Launch Game) hands
            // off to the Resize Mod List button first, rather than jumping straight past it
            // into the top bar - a further Up from there reaches the top bar.
            if (consoleLaunchFocused && delta < 0)
            {
                consoleLaunchFocused = false;
                consoleResizeFocused = true;
                RefreshConsoleHighlights();
                return;
            }

            if (consoleLaunchFocused)
            {
                if (delta > 0) { consoleLaunchFocused = false; selectedConsoleTileIndex = 0; }
            }
            else if (delta < 0 && selectedConsoleTileIndex == 0)
            {
                consoleLaunchFocused = true;
            }
            else
            {
                selectedConsoleTileIndex = (selectedConsoleTileIndex + delta + consoleTileButtons.Count) % consoleTileButtons.Count;
            }

            RefreshConsoleHighlights();
        }

        // --- Console Mode "top bar" - the theme dropdown, server search/dropdown, and mod
        // search box sitting above the tile overlay. See the field comment on
        // consoleTopBarControls for why this exists as a separate focus zone. ---

        private void EnterConsoleTopBar(bool fromBottom)
        {
            if (consoleTopBarControls == null || consoleTopBarControls.Length == 0) return;
            consoleTopBarActive = true;
            consoleLaunchFocused = false;
            consoleResizeFocused = false;
            consoleSidebarFocused = false;
            consoleTopBarIndex = fromBottom ? consoleTopBarControls.Length - 1 : 0;
            RefreshConsoleHighlights();
            RefreshConsoleTopBarHighlight();
        }

        private void ExitConsoleTopBar()
        {
            if (consoleDropdownOpen) CloseConsoleDropdown(true);
            ReleaseConsoleTopBarTextFocus();
            consoleTopBarActive = false;
            pnlTopBarFocusHighlight.Visible = false;
            // Lands on the Resize Mod List button rather than jumping straight to Launch
            // Game, mirroring the stop MoveConsoleTileSelection inserts on the way up.
            consoleLaunchFocused = false;
            consoleResizeFocused = true;
            RefreshConsoleHighlights();
            // Hand real Windows focus back to the tile panel so a textbox that was focused
            // via ActivateConsoleTopBarSelection can't keep soaking up keystrokes after the
            // highlight has visibly moved away from it.
            if (pnlConsoleTiles != null) pnlConsoleTiles.Focus();
        }

        private void MoveConsoleTopBarSelection(int delta)
        {
            int newIndex = consoleTopBarIndex + delta;

            // Off the top - nowhere further to go. Off the bottom - hand focus back down to
            // the tile grid's Launch Game button, mirroring MoveConsoleTileSelection's own
            // hand-off in the other direction.
            if (newIndex < 0) return;
            if (newIndex >= consoleTopBarControls.Length) { ExitConsoleTopBar(); return; }

            // Moving off a textbox that currently holds real focus (from a previous
            // ActivateConsoleTopBarSelection) used to leave it focused - keystrokes kept
            // going into the box the highlight had already left, and the virtual keyboard
            // (if open for it) stayed open pointing at a field that no longer looked selected.
            ReleaseConsoleTopBarTextFocus();
            // Moving off a dropdown that is still hanging open would leave its list floating
            // over the window with the highlight already somewhere else.
            if (consoleDropdownOpen) CloseConsoleDropdown(true);

            consoleTopBarIndex = newIndex;
            RefreshConsoleTopBarHighlight();
        }

        // If the currently-highlighted top-bar control is a textbox that holds real Windows
        // focus, hands focus back to the tile panel and closes the virtual keyboard that was
        // targeting it, so navigating away always fully releases it.
        private void ReleaseConsoleTopBarTextFocus()
        {
            if (consoleTopBarControls == null || consoleTopBarIndex < 0 || consoleTopBarIndex >= consoleTopBarControls.Length) return;
            Control current = consoleTopBarControls[consoleTopBarIndex];
            // Was "is TextBox" only, so moving off a focused dropdown field left real Windows
            // focus (and therefore its own outline) behind on it.
            if (current != null && current.Focused)
            {
                if (pnlConsoleTiles != null) pnlConsoleTiles.Focus();
                if (frmVirtualKeyboard != null && frmVirtualKeyboard.Visible) HideVirtualKeyboard();
            }

            HideFieldFocusRings();
        }

        // Drops every per-field outline at once. Console Mode draws exactly one ring, the
        // shared one that follows the D-pad, so anything else showing is a leftover.
        private void HideFieldFocusRings()
        {
            for (int i = 0; i < focusHighlightPanels.Count; i++)
            {
                if (focusHighlightPanels[i] != null) focusHighlightPanels[i].Visible = false;
            }
        }

        // The accent color at whatever brightness the pulse is currently at - shared by every
        // focus ring in the app so they all breathe together.
        private Color FocusRingColor()
        {
            return Color.FromArgb(focusRingAlpha, GetThemeColors(CurrentThemeName()).AccentColor);
        }

        private void FocusPulseTimer_Tick(object sender, EventArgs e)
        {
            bool anyVisible = (activeConsolePicker != null)
                || (pnlTopBarFocusHighlight != null && pnlTopBarFocusHighlight.Visible);

            for (int i = 0; i < focusHighlightPanels.Count && !anyVisible; i++)
            {
                if (focusHighlightPanels[i] != null && focusHighlightPanels[i].Visible) anyVisible = true;
            }

            // Nothing is outlined right now, so there is nothing to repaint - the timer keeps
            // running but costs nothing until a ring actually appears.
            if (!anyVisible) return;

            focusPulsePhase++;
            // A slow sine between roughly a third brightness and full, which is what reads as
            // "breathing" rather than as blinking.
            double wave = 0.5 + 0.5 * Math.Sin(focusPulsePhase * 0.115);
            focusRingAlpha = 95 + (int)(160.0 * wave);
            if (focusRingAlpha < 0) focusRingAlpha = 0;
            if (focusRingAlpha > 255) focusRingAlpha = 255;

            if (pnlTopBarFocusHighlight != null && pnlTopBarFocusHighlight.Visible) pnlTopBarFocusHighlight.Invalidate();
            for (int i = 0; i < focusHighlightPanels.Count; i++)
            {
                if (focusHighlightPanels[i] != null && focusHighlightPanels[i].Visible) focusHighlightPanels[i].Invalidate();
            }
            if (activeConsolePicker != null) activeConsolePicker.PulseRing();
        }

        // Puts the current selection's text on each custom dropdown field. The ComboBoxes
        // behind them are hidden, so this is the only thing that makes the selection visible.
        private void UpdateDropDownDisplays()
        {
            if (btnThemeDropDown != null)
            {
                btnThemeDropDown.Text = (cboThemeSelector.SelectedItem != null)
                    ? cboThemeSelector.SelectedItem.ToString()
                    : "Select a theme...";
            }

            if (btnServerDropDown != null)
            {
                if (cboServerDropdown.SelectedItem != null)
                {
                    btnServerDropDown.Text = cboServerDropdown.SelectedItem.ToString();
                }
                else
                {
                    btnServerDropDown.Text = (cboServerDropdown.Items.Count == 0)
                        ? "No servers yet - use Add Server"
                        : "Select a target server...";
                }
            }
        }

        // Maps a custom dropdown field back to the real ComboBox holding its data.
        private ComboBox ComboBehindDropDownField(Control field)
        {
            if (ReferenceEquals(field, btnThemeDropDown)) return cboThemeSelector;
            if (ReferenceEquals(field, btnServerDropDown)) return cboServerDropdown;
            return field as ComboBox;
        }

        // Left/Right on a focused dropdown cycles its selection directly - simpler and far
        // more controller-friendly than trying to drive the native open dropdown list (which
        // has no controller input wired to it at all) via D-pad. Text boxes ignore this.
        private void AdjustConsoleTopBarValue(int delta)
        {
            Control focused = consoleTopBarControls[consoleTopBarIndex];
            // Resolves the custom dropdown field back to the ComboBox it stands in for, so
            // Left/Right still nudges the value without opening anything.
            ComboBox combo = ComboBehindDropDownField(focused);
            if (combo == null || combo.Items.Count == 0) return;

            int newIndex = Math.Max(0, Math.Min(combo.Items.Count - 1, combo.SelectedIndex + delta));
            if (newIndex != combo.SelectedIndex) combo.SelectedIndex = newIndex;
        }

        // A on a text box opens the virtual keyboard targeting it (the only way a
        // controller-only session can type at all); A on a dropdown opens/commits the real
        // dropdown list - see the OpenConsoleDropdown/CloseConsoleDropdown pair above.
        private void ActivateConsoleTopBarSelection()
        {
            Control focused = consoleTopBarControls[consoleTopBarIndex];

            // The custom dropdown fields are Buttons, not ComboBoxes, so they are matched
            // before either of the type checks below.
            if (ReferenceEquals(focused, btnThemeDropDown)) { OpenConsoleThemePicker(); return; }
            if (ReferenceEquals(focused, btnServerDropDown)) { OpenConsoleServerPicker(); return; }

            TextBox tb = focused as TextBox;
            if (tb != null)
            {
                // The mod search field opens the themed search popup - a full-size search row
                // with the matching mods laid out as big tiles underneath it, filtering as you
                // type - instead of dropping a caret into a 160px box that the on-screen
                // keyboard then covers up, with the results landing in a list the controller
                // could not reach anyway.
                if (ReferenceEquals(tb, txtModSearchBox)) { OpenConsoleModSearchPicker(); return; }
                // Browse.../Open Folder are hidden in Console Mode (they used to sit to the
                // RIGHT of this box, which is the one thing the top row could not be stacked
                // around), so A here offers those two actions plus typing, rather than
                // silently dropping one of the three.
                if (ReferenceEquals(tb, txtGamePath)) { OpenConsolePathPicker(); return; }
                tb.Focus();
                ShowVirtualKeyboard(tb);
                return;
            }

            ComboBox combo = focused as ComboBox;
            if (combo != null)
            {
                if (consoleDropdownOpen) CloseConsoleDropdown(true);
                else OpenConsoleDropdown(combo);
                return;
            }

            focused.Focus();
        }

        // Moves the shared outline (see its field comment) to wrap whichever control is
        // currently focused in the top bar zone.
        private void RefreshConsoleTopBarHighlight()
        {
            if (pnlTopBarFocusHighlight == null || consoleTopBarControls == null) return;
            if (!consoleTopBarActive || consoleTopBarIndex < 0 || consoleTopBarIndex >= consoleTopBarControls.Length)
            {
                pnlTopBarFocusHighlight.Visible = false;
                return;
            }

            // Exactly one outline is allowed on screen in Console Mode. Anything a stray
            // GotFocus managed to light up gets dropped here, which is the backstop for the
            // Theme field staying ringed after the cursor had moved to Target Server.
            HideFieldFocusRings();

            Control target = consoleTopBarControls[consoleTopBarIndex];
            pnlTopBarFocusHighlight.Location = new Point(target.Left - 5, target.Top - 5);
            pnlTopBarFocusHighlight.Size = new Size(target.Width + 10, target.Height + 10);
            pnlTopBarFocusHighlight.Invalidate();
            pnlTopBarFocusHighlight.Visible = true;
            // Sent to the BACK, not the front - it's sized a few pixels larger than the
            // control it's highlighting on every side, so as long as it sits behind that
            // control (and behind the light-mode border panel drawn over it - see
            // WrapControlWithLightModeBorder), only the extra margin peeks out as a ring around
            // it. Bringing it to the front instead would sit on top of the real control and
            // swallow every mouse click meant for it.
            pnlTopBarFocusHighlight.SendToBack();
        }

        private void ActivateConsoleSelection()
        {
            if (consoleSidebarFocused)
            {
                ActivateConsoleSidebarSelection();
            }
            else if (consoleResizeFocused)
            {
                btnResizeModList.PerformClick();
            }
            else if (consoleLaunchFocused)
            {
                btnConsoleLaunchGame.PerformClick();
            }
            else if (selectedConsoleTileIndex >= 0 && selectedConsoleTileIndex < consoleTileButtons.Count)
            {
                consoleTileButtons[selectedConsoleTileIndex].PerformClick();
            }
        }

        // Re-colors the sidebar, content tiles, and Launch Game button from the current theme,
        // with whichever one is presently selected drawn in the accent color.
        private void RefreshConsoleHighlights()
        {
            if (pnlConsoleTiles == null) return;

            ThemeColors t = GetThemeColors(CurrentThemeName());

            // Three distinct sidebar states now, not two: the tab the D-pad is currently
            // sitting on (full accent), the category actually being shown (a muted accent, so
            // you can still see where you came from while browsing), and everything else.
            for (int i = 0; i < consoleCategoryButtons.Count; i++)
            {
                bool cursorHere = (consoleSidebarFocused && !consoleTopBarActive && i == consoleSidebarIndex);
                bool isOpenCategory = (i == selectedConsoleCategoryIndex);

                if (cursorHere)
                {
                    consoleCategoryButtons[i].BackColor = t.AccentColor;
                    consoleCategoryButtons[i].ForeColor = Color.White;
                }
                else if (isOpenCategory)
                {
                    consoleCategoryButtons[i].BackColor = BlendColors(t.AccentColor, t.ButtonBg, 0.45f);
                    consoleCategoryButtons[i].ForeColor = t.IsLightBase ? Color.Black : Color.White;
                }
                else
                {
                    consoleCategoryButtons[i].BackColor = t.ButtonBg;
                    consoleCategoryButtons[i].ForeColor = t.ButtonFg;
                }
            }

            // While the top bar (search boxes/dropdowns above the tile overlay) has focus,
            // nothing in the tile grid itself should still be drawn as selected.
            for (int i = 0; i < consoleTileButtons.Count; i++)
            {
                bool selected = (!consoleTopBarActive && !consoleSidebarFocused && !consoleLaunchFocused && !consoleResizeFocused && i == selectedConsoleTileIndex);
                consoleTileButtons[i].BackColor = selected ? t.AccentColor : t.ButtonBg;
                consoleTileButtons[i].ForeColor = selected ? Color.White : t.ButtonFg;
            }

            RefreshResizeModListButton(t);

            if (btnConsoleLaunchGame != null)
            {
                btnConsoleLaunchGame.BackColor = (consoleLaunchFocused && !consoleTopBarActive && !consoleSidebarFocused) ? t.AccentColor : Color.FromArgb(40, 140, 60);
                btnConsoleLaunchGame.ForeColor = Color.White;
            }
        }

        // Keeps the permanent "Resize Mod List" button (directly under the mod list, in both
        // desktop and Console Mode) in sync with whether resize mode is currently active -
        // called from RefreshConsoleHighlights, which already runs on every theme change and
        // on every toggle of the flag itself, so this needed no separate call sites of its own.
        private void RefreshResizeModListButton(ThemeColors t)
        {
            if (btnResizeModList == null) return;

            if (listResizeModeActive)
            {
                btnResizeModList.Text = "Resize Mod List - ADJUSTING  (Down = grow, Up = shrink, Enter/Esc to stop)";
                btnResizeModList.BackColor = t.AccentColor;
                btnResizeModList.ForeColor = Color.White;
            }
            else if (consoleResizeFocused)
            {
                // D-pad/keyboard cursor is parked here (but A/Enter hasn't been pressed yet) -
                // same accent highlight every other focused Console Mode control gets.
                btnResizeModList.Text = "Resize Mod List";
                btnResizeModList.BackColor = t.AccentColor;
                btnResizeModList.ForeColor = Color.White;
            }
            else
            {
                btnResizeModList.Text = "Resize Mod List";
                btnResizeModList.BackColor = t.ButtonBg;
                btnResizeModList.ForeColor = t.ButtonFg;
            }
        }

        // Mixes two colors - used for the "this category is open but the cursor has moved
        // elsewhere" sidebar shade, so that state is visibly between selected and unselected
        // rather than needing a third hardcoded color per theme.
        private static Color BlendColors(Color a, Color b, float amountOfA)
        {
            float k = amountOfA < 0f ? 0f : (amountOfA > 1f ? 1f : amountOfA);
            return Color.FromArgb(
                (int)(a.R * k + b.R * (1f - k)),
                (int)(a.G * k + b.G * (1f - k)),
                (int)(a.B * k + b.B * (1f - k)));
        }

        // Drag-and-drop isn't reachable with a controller, so this gives Console Mode's Mods
        // category an equivalent: pick files, then hand them to the exact same import pipeline
        // a real drop uses (zip extraction, readme handling, smart version matching, engine.ini
        // merging) by simulating a drop with the picked paths, rather than reimplementing any
        // of that logic a second time.
        private void OnConsoleAddModClicked(object sender, EventArgs e)
        {
            using (OpenFileDialog dlg = new OpenFileDialog())
            {
                dlg.Title = "Select Mod Files";
                dlg.Filter = "Mod Files (*.pak;*.zip)|*.pak;*.zip|All Files (*.*)|*.*";
                dlg.Multiselect = true;

                if (dlg.ShowDialog(this) == DialogResult.OK && dlg.FileNames.Length > 0)
                {
                    DataObject fakeDropData = new DataObject(DataFormats.FileDrop, dlg.FileNames);
                    DragEventArgs fakeDropArgs = new DragEventArgs(fakeDropData, 0, 0, 0, DragDropEffects.Copy, DragDropEffects.Copy);
                    OnPanelDragDrop(this, fakeDropArgs);
                }
            }
        }

        // Toggles "adjust mode" for the mod list's height, via the "Resize Mod List" button
        // that sits directly under the list in both desktop and Console Mode. While active,
        // Up/Down (real arrow keys, or D-pad/physical arrows in Console Mode) resize the list
        // instead of their normal meaning - see ProcessCmdKey and FireDirectionalMove.
        private void OnToggleListResizeModeClicked(object sender, EventArgs e)
        {
            listResizeModeActive = !listResizeModeActive;
            RefreshConsoleHighlights();
        }

        // --- Console Mode themed pickers (top row only) ---------------------------------
        // The top row's dropdowns and search boxes were the last parts of the window that
        // assumed a mouse and a keyboard: a native ComboBox list has no controller input
        // wired to it at all and draws rows too small to read at arm's length, and a 160px
        // TextBox needs a caret in it before it does anything and then gets covered by the
        // on-screen keyboard anyway. A picker is a themed modal window instead: an optional
        // search row across the top that filters as you type, and the matches laid out below
        // it as big tiles you walk with the D-pad.
        //
        // Input is driven by the main window's existing poll timer (ControllerPollTimer_Tick
        // branches to activeConsolePicker first, and FireDirectionalMove hands it every
        // direction) rather than a second XInput poll of its own - a WinForms Timer keeps
        // ticking inside a modal dialog's nested message loop, so there is still exactly one
        // place in the app reading the controller.
        private string ShowConsolePicker(string title, string searchPlaceholder, string currentValue, Func<string, List<string>> itemProvider)
        {
            ConsolePickerForm picker = new ConsolePickerForm();
            picker.Host = this;
            picker.TitleText = title;
            picker.SearchPlaceholder = searchPlaceholder;
            picker.SearchEnabled = !string.IsNullOrEmpty(searchPlaceholder);
            picker.ItemProvider = itemProvider;
            picker.InitialValue = currentValue;

            ConsolePickerForm previous = activeConsolePicker;
            activeConsolePicker = picker;
            string chosen = null;
            try
            {
                picker.BuildAndShow(this);
                chosen = picker.SelectedValue;
                lastPickerQuery = picker.CurrentQuery;
            }
            finally
            {
                activeConsolePicker = previous;
                picker.Dispose();
            }

            return chosen;
        }

        // Four options, no search row needed - the picker in its simplest form.
        private void OpenConsoleThemePicker()
        {
            List<string> themes = new List<string>();
            foreach (object item in cboThemeSelector.Items) themes.Add(item.ToString());

            string chosen = ShowConsolePicker("SELECT THEME", "", CurrentThemeName(),
                delegate(string query) { return themes; });

            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(chosen)) cboThemeSelector.SelectedItem = chosen;
            RefreshConsoleTopBarHighlight();
        }

        // Search row plus grid: what used to be two separate top-row controls sitting side by
        // side (a search box to the LEFT of the dropdown it filtered) is one stop now, and the
        // filtering and the picking happen in the same window instead of one field feeding
        // another one next to it.
        private void OpenConsoleServerPicker()
        {
            string current = (cboServerDropdown.SelectedItem != null) ? cboServerDropdown.SelectedItem.ToString() : null;

            string chosen = ShowConsolePicker("SELECT TARGET SERVER", "SEARCH SERVERS   (Y TO TYPE)...", current,
                delegate(string query)
                {
                    // Reuses the exact filter the desktop search box drives, so the dropdown
                    // underneath is always already holding whatever the picker is showing and
                    // nothing about how server filtering works is duplicated here.
                    FilterServers(query);
                    List<string> results = new List<string>();
                    foreach (object item in cboServerDropdown.Items) results.Add(item.ToString());
                    return results;
                });

            // Keep the desktop search box (hidden while Console Mode is on) in step with what
            // was typed, so switching Console Mode back off never reveals a search box whose
            // text has nothing to do with the list beside it.
            suppressServerSearchEvent = true;
            try { txtServerSearchBox.Text = lastPickerQuery; }
            finally { suppressServerSearchEvent = false; }

            FilterServers(lastPickerQuery);

            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(chosen))
            {
                int idx = cboServerDropdown.Items.IndexOf(chosen);
                if (idx >= 0) cboServerDropdown.SelectedIndex = idx;
            }
            else if (cboServerDropdown.Items.Count > 0 && cboServerDropdown.SelectedIndex < 0)
            {
                cboServerDropdown.SelectedIndex = 0;
            }

            RefreshConsoleTopBarHighlight();
        }

        // The mod list itself is still the thing being filtered - this just gives the filtering
        // somewhere controller-sized to happen, and lets A on a result jump the mod list's
        // selection straight to that mod instead of leaving you to find it by hand afterwards.
        private void OpenConsoleModSearchPicker()
        {
            string chosen = ShowConsolePicker("SEARCH MODS", "SEARCH MODS   (Y TO TYPE)...", null,
                delegate(string query)
                {
                    FilterMods(query);
                    List<string> results = new List<string>();
                    foreach (object item in lstServerPaks.Items) results.Add(item.ToString());
                    return results;
                });

            suppressModSearchEvent = true;
            try { txtModSearchBox.Text = lastPickerQuery; }
            finally { suppressModSearchEvent = false; }

            FilterMods(lastPickerQuery);

            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(chosen))
            {
                int idx = lstServerPaks.Items.IndexOf(chosen);
                if (idx >= 0) lstServerPaks.SelectedIndex = idx;
            }

            RefreshConsoleTopBarHighlight();
        }

        // Stands in for the Browse.../Open Folder buttons that Console Mode hides, plus the
        // plain "type it myself" route the field had before.
        private const string ConsolePathActionBrowse = "Browse For Folder...";
        private const string ConsolePathActionOpen = "Open Folder In Explorer";
        private const string ConsolePathActionType = "Type The Path";
        // A controller-only session has no equivalent of clearing a text box and retyping the
        // built-in default from scratch - this gives it an explicit, single-press way back to
        // DefaultGamePath instead. Desktop mode still has Browse.../typing directly to get back
        // to any path (including the default) with a mouse or keyboard, so this entry is
        // console-only rather than adding a fourth button to the already-tight desktop row.
        private const string ConsolePathActionResetDefault = "Reset To Default Path";

        private void OpenConsolePathPicker()
        {
            List<string> actions = new List<string>();
            actions.Add(ConsolePathActionBrowse);
            actions.Add(ConsolePathActionOpen);
            actions.Add(ConsolePathActionType);
            actions.Add(ConsolePathActionResetDefault);

            string chosen = ShowConsolePicker("GAME PAKS DIRECTORY", "", null,
                delegate(string query) { return actions; });

            if (chosen == ConsolePathActionBrowse)
            {
                OnBrowsePathClicked(this, EventArgs.Empty);
            }
            else if (chosen == ConsolePathActionOpen)
            {
                OnOpenDirectoryClicked(this, EventArgs.Empty);
            }
            else if (chosen == ConsolePathActionType)
            {
                txtGamePath.Focus();
                ShowVirtualKeyboard(txtGamePath);
            }
            else if (chosen == ConsolePathActionResetDefault)
            {
                ResetGamePathToDefault();
            }

            RefreshConsoleTopBarHighlight();
        }

        // Backs the console picker's "Reset To Default Path" entry - restores DefaultGamePath
        // and persists it immediately, the same as any other path change, rather than leaving
        // the reset sitting unsaved until something else happens to trigger a save.
        private void ResetGamePathToDefault()
        {
            txtGamePath.Text = DefaultGamePath;
            PersistConfigPath(DefaultGamePath);
        }

        // Console Mode restacks the TOP ROW into a single full-width column. On the desktop
        // layout the paks path shares its row with Browse.../Open Folder, and the server
        // search box sits to the LEFT of the server dropdown it filters - both fine with a
        // mouse, both a sideways detour with a D-pad. So those three move out of the way
        // (Browse/Open Folder into the paks-path picker, the search box into the server
        // picker's own search row) and what is left is one control per row: path, theme,
        // server, mods. Everything below the mod list is untouched.
        private void ApplyConsoleTopBarLayout(bool consoleOn)
        {
            if (txtGamePath == null || btnServerDropDown == null || txtModSearchBox == null) return;

            int fullWidth = Math.Max(200, ClientSize.Width - 30);

            btnBrowsePath.Visible = !consoleOn;
            btnOpenDirectory.Visible = !consoleOn;
            txtServerSearchBox.Visible = !consoleOn;

            if (consoleOn)
            {
                lblServerHeader.Text = "Target Server:";

                txtGamePath.Width = fullWidth;

                btnServerDropDown.Location = new Point(15, 145);
                btnServerDropDown.Width = fullWidth;

                txtModSearchBox.Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left | AnchorStyles.Right;
                txtModSearchBox.Location = new Point(15, 200);
                txtModSearchBox.Width = fullWidth;
            }
            else
            {
                lblServerHeader.Text = "Select / Search Target Server:";

                // Back to sharing its row with Browse.../Open Folder, which anchor to the
                // window's right edge - so the path box has to stop short of them rather than
                // running the full width.
                txtGamePath.Width = Math.Max(120, fullWidth - 195);

                btnServerDropDown.Location = new Point(180, 145);
                btnServerDropDown.Width = Math.Max(120, fullWidth - 165);

                txtModSearchBox.Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left;
                txtModSearchBox.Location = new Point(15, 200);
                txtModSearchBox.Width = 160;
            }

            SyncLightModeBorder(txtGamePath);
            SyncLightModeBorder(txtModSearchBox);
            SyncLightModeBorder(txtServerSearchBox);
            RefreshConsoleTopBarHighlight();
        }

        // A field's Light Mode outline is a separate sibling panel rather than a real border
        // (see WrapControlWithLightModeBorder), so anything that moves or resizes one of those
        // fields has to move its outline as well or the frame is simply left behind.
        private void SyncLightModeBorder(Control inner)
        {
            Panel borderPanel;
            if (inner == null || !lightModeBorderPanels.TryGetValue(inner, out borderPanel)) return;

            borderPanel.Visible = inner.Visible;
            borderPanel.Anchor = inner.Anchor;
            borderPanel.Location = new Point(inner.Left - 1, inner.Top - 1);
            borderPanel.Size = new Size(inner.Width + 2, inner.Height + 2);
            borderPanel.Invalidate();
        }

        // The picker window itself. Borderless and painted from the current theme, so it reads
        // as part of the app rather than as a system dialog dropped on top of it.
        private class ConsolePickerForm : Form
        {
            // Forces real OS foreground activation on Shown (see the comment there) - this
            // picker is opened by A on a controller via a System.Windows.Forms.Timer tick, and
            // Windows' foreground-lock heuristic can otherwise refuse to hand a brand-new
            // window real activation when it's requested from something other than a genuine
            // user input message, silently leaving the OWNER as the actual foreground window.
            [DllImport("user32.dll")]
            private static extern bool SetForegroundWindow(IntPtr hWnd);

            public ModManagerForm Host;
            public string TitleText = "SELECT";
            public string SearchPlaceholder = "";
            public bool SearchEnabled = false;
            public string InitialValue;
            // Called once up front and again on every keystroke in the search row; whatever it
            // returns is what the grid shows. Keeping it a delegate is what lets the server
            // picker and the mod picker reuse the app's real FilterServers/FilterMods instead
            // of reimplementing filtering in here.
            public Func<string, List<string>> ItemProvider;

            public string SelectedValue;
            public string CurrentQuery = "";

            private readonly List<string> items = new List<string>();
            private readonly List<ShinyButton> tiles = new List<ShinyButton>();

            private Label lblTitle;
            // A real, dedicated Back button sitting above the search/results controls (in the
            // title row, to the title's left) instead of the picker's only way out being the
            // footer hint bar below everything else - the same "< Back" placement a title bar
            // would normally use, so it reads as its own clear affordance rather than
            // something you have to notice is also clickable.
            private ShinyButton btnBack;
            // A full-width clickable bar instead of a plain caption label - the whole strip
            // is a button now, so closing the picker no longer requires a controller's B or a
            // keyboard's Escape; a mouse/touch tap across the entire bottom edge does the same
            // thing CancelPicker always did. Kept as a secondary way out (and as the nav-hint
            // display) alongside the dedicated btnBack above.
            private ShinyButton btnFooterBack;
            private Label lblEmpty;
            private Label lblPlaceholder;
            private Panel pnlSearchRow;
            private Panel pnlResults;
            private Panel pnlRing;
            private TextBox txtSearch;

            private ThemeColors theme;
            private int selIndex = 0;
            private int columns = 3;
            private bool searchRowFocused = false;

            // See the Deactivate/Shown comments in BuildAndShow: Deactivate is ignored until
            // this flips true, which happens once shortly after Shown rather than immediately,
            // so the foreground-activation race can't masquerade as "the user clicked away."
            private const int DeactivateGuardDelayMs = 350;
            private bool deactivateGuardArmed = false;
            private Timer deactivateGuardTimer;

            public void BuildAndShow(ModManagerForm host)
            {
                theme = Host.GetThemeColors(Host.CurrentThemeName());

                FormBorderStyle = FormBorderStyle.None;
                ShowInTaskbar = false;
                StartPosition = FormStartPosition.CenterParent;
                KeyPreview = true;
                BackColor = theme.WindowBg;
                ForeColor = theme.TextColor;
                // The 420x320 floor guarantees room for the title/back button/footer even
                // against a tiny host window - but flooring it unconditionally used to let this
                // picker end up WIDER/TALLER than a genuinely small host, and since it's
                // centered ON that host (StartPosition.CenterParent) rather than on the screen,
                // a picker bigger than its host could spill straight past the edge of the
                // physical display with no way to scroll or drag it back - exactly the "buttons
                // running off the screen" a Steam Deck-sized window would hit. The working
                // area's own size is now folded into every clamp below, so the floor only wins
                // when the SCREEN actually has room for it; ClampToScreen (called from Shown)
                // is the second half of this fix, nudging the whole window back on screen for
                // the rarer case where CenterParent itself lands it partly off-screen.
                Rectangle workArea = Screen.FromControl(host).WorkingArea;
                ClientSize = new Size(
                    Math.Min(Math.Min(620, workArea.Width - 24), Math.Max(Math.Min(420, workArea.Width - 24), host.ClientSize.Width - 40)),
                    Math.Min(Math.Min(540, workArea.Height - 24), Math.Max(Math.Min(320, workArea.Height - 24), host.ClientSize.Height - 90)));

                lblTitle = new Label
                {
                    Text = TitleText,
                    TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleCenter,
                    Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 12f, FontStyle.Bold),
                    BackColor = BlendColors(theme.AccentColor, theme.WindowBg, 0.30f),
                    ForeColor = theme.IsLightBase ? Color.Black : Color.White
                };
                Controls.Add(lblTitle);

                btnBack = new ShinyButton
                {
                    Text = "\u2190 Back",
                    Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9f, FontStyle.Bold),
                    FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
                    BackColor = theme.ButtonBg,
                    ForeColor = theme.ButtonFg
                };
                btnBack.Click += delegate { CancelPicker(); };
                Controls.Add(btnBack);
                btnBack.BringToFront();

                pnlSearchRow = new Panel { BackColor = theme.WindowBg, Visible = SearchEnabled };
                Controls.Add(pnlSearchRow);

                txtSearch = new TextBox
                {
                    BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle,
                    Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 11f, FontStyle.Regular),
                    BackColor = theme.ControlBg,
                    ForeColor = theme.TextColor
                };
                txtSearch.TextChanged += delegate { ApplyQuery(); };
                pnlSearchRow.Controls.Add(txtSearch);

                // Placeholder text drawn as a child label rather than as real text in the box,
                // so the query never has to be told apart from the prompt.
                lblPlaceholder = new Label
                {
                    Text = SearchPlaceholder,
                    AutoSize = false,
                    TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleLeft,
                    BackColor = Color.Transparent,
                    ForeColor = BlendColors(theme.TextColor, theme.ControlBg, 0.40f),
                    Font = txtSearch.Font
                };
                lblPlaceholder.Click += delegate { BeginTyping(); };
                txtSearch.Controls.Add(lblPlaceholder);

                pnlResults = new Panel { BackColor = theme.WindowBg, AutoScroll = true };
                Controls.Add(pnlResults);

                pnlRing = new DoubleBufferedPanel { BackColor = Color.Transparent, Enabled = false, Visible = false };
                pnlRing.Paint += delegate(object s, PaintEventArgs pe)
                {
                    pe.Graphics.SmoothingMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.SmoothingMode.AntiAlias;
                    using (Pen pen = new Pen(Host.FocusRingColor(), 3f))
                    {
                        pe.Graphics.DrawRectangle(pen, 2, 2, pnlRing.Width - 5, pnlRing.Height - 5);
                    }
                };
                pnlResults.Controls.Add(pnlRing);

                lblEmpty = new Label
                {
                    Text = "No matches.",
                    AutoSize = false,
                    TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleLeft,
                    ForeColor = theme.TextColor,
                    BackColor = Color.Transparent,
                    Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 10f, FontStyle.Regular),
                    Visible = false
                };
                pnlResults.Controls.Add(lblEmpty);

                btnFooterBack = new ShinyButton
                {
                    Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9f, FontStyle.Bold),
                    FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat,
                    BackColor = theme.ButtonBg,
                    ForeColor = theme.ButtonFg
                };
                btnFooterBack.Click += delegate { CancelPicker(); };
                Controls.Add(btnFooterBack);

                KeyUp += Host.OnConsoleModeKeyUp;

                // Clicking anywhere outside this window - back on the main window, another
                // app, the taskbar - deactivates it. Previously the only way out was B/Escape
                // or a tile click; now stepping away from the popup closes it the same way
                // clicking outside a native dropdown's open list would.
                //
                // This used to call CancelPicker() the instant Deactivate fired at all, which
                // is exactly what made a picker opened by A on a controller "flash and
