            float sat = c.GetSaturation();
            // Grays / near-black / near-white have no meaningful hue to confuse with
            // anything else - leave them completely alone so plain neutral surfaces never
            // pick up an unwanted tint.
            if (sat < 0.10f) return c;

            float hue = c.GetHue();
            float safeHue = MapHueForColorBlindMode(hue);
            if (Math.Abs(safeHue - hue) < 0.01f) return c;

            float lightness = c.GetBrightness();
            return ColorFromHsl(safeHue, sat, lightness, c.A);
        }

        // Which hue (in degrees) a given original hue should be rotated to for the current
        // colorBlindMode, following the same red/green (Prot/Deuter) vs. blue/violet (Trit)
        // confusion pairs the fixed SemanticColorRole mapping above already targets. Hues
        // outside the confusable bands for that mode pass straight through unchanged.
        private float MapHueForColorBlindMode(float hue)
        {
            bool isRed = hue < 20f || hue >= 345f;
            bool isOrange = hue >= 20f && hue < 50f;
            bool isYellow = hue >= 50f && hue < 70f;
            bool isGreen = hue >= 70f && hue < 170f;
            bool isCyan = hue >= 170f && hue < 195f;
            bool isBlue = hue >= 195f && hue < 250f;
            bool isPurple = hue >= 250f && hue < 290f;

            switch (colorBlindMode)
            {
                case "Protanopia":
                case "Deuteranopia":
                    // Red vs. green is the hard pair for both of these - orange is left alone
                    // since it still reads as clearly "warm" rather than collapsing into red.
                    if (isRed) return 24f;    // vermillion
                    if (isGreen) return 202f; // blue
                    return hue;
                case "Tritanopia":
                    // Blue/cyan vs. violet (and yellow sliding toward pale blue) is the hard
                    // pair here instead.
                    if (isBlue) return 165f;   // bluish green
                    if (isCyan) return 165f;   // bluish green
                    if (isPurple) return 328f; // reddish purple
                    if (isYellow) return 50f;  // keep a clean yellow
                    return hue;
                default:
                    return hue;
            }
        }

        // Rebuilds an RGB Color from HSL, matching the model Color.GetHue/GetSaturation/
        // GetBrightness already use - so a color that goes through GetHue()/GetSaturation()/
        // GetBrightness() and straight back through here round-trips exactly, and only the
        // hue actually changes when the caller passes in a different one.
        private static Color ColorFromHsl(float h, float s, float l, int alpha)
        {
            if (s <= 0f)
            {
                int gray = (int)Math.Round(l * 255f);
                gray = Math.Max(0, Math.Min(255, gray));
                return Color.FromArgb(alpha, gray, gray, gray);
            }

            float chroma = (1f - Math.Abs(2f * l - 1f)) * s;
            float hp = h / 60f;
            float x = chroma * (1f - Math.Abs(hp % 2f - 1f));
            float r1, g1, b1;
            if (hp < 1f) { r1 = chroma; g1 = x; b1 = 0f; }
            else if (hp < 2f) { r1 = x; g1 = chroma; b1 = 0f; }
            else if (hp < 3f) { r1 = 0f; g1 = chroma; b1 = x; }
            else if (hp < 4f) { r1 = 0f; g1 = x; b1 = chroma; }
            else if (hp < 5f) { r1 = x; g1 = 0f; b1 = chroma; }
            else { r1 = chroma; g1 = 0f; b1 = x; }

            float m = l - chroma / 2f;
            int r = (int)Math.Round((r1 + m) * 255f);
            int g = (int)Math.Round((g1 + m) * 255f);
            int b = (int)Math.Round((b1 + m) * 255f);
            r = Math.Max(0, Math.Min(255, r));
            g = Math.Max(0, Math.Min(255, g));
            b = Math.Max(0, Math.Min(255, b));
            return Color.FromArgb(alpha, r, g, b);
        }

        private ThemeColors GetBaseThemeColors(string themeName)
        {
            switch (themeName)
            {
                case "Light Mode":
                    // Fix: ButtonBg and AccentColor were BOTH SystemColors.ControlLight, which
                    // is only a few shades off SystemColors.Control (the window background).
                    // That single collision caused most of Light Mode's visual problems at
                    // once: buttons blended into the background, a "selected" console tile or
                    // virtual-keyboard key was drawn in exactly the same color as an
                    // unselected one (and then had white text put on it, so its label
                    // vanished), and the controller focus ring - which paints in AccentColor -
                    // was invisible against the very surface it was outlining. Light Mode now
                    // gets a genuinely distinct button gray and a real accent blue, so every
                    // "this is selected / this is focused" cue has something to contrast with.
                    return new ThemeColors
                    {
                        WindowBg = SystemColors.Control,
                        ControlBg = SystemColors.Window,
                        TextColor = SystemColors.WindowText,
                        HeaderColor = SystemColors.ControlText,
                        ButtonBg = Color.FromArgb(214, 216, 220),
                        ButtonFg = Color.FromArgb(20, 20, 20),
                        AccentColor = Color.FromArgb(0, 102, 194),
                        IsLightBase = true,
                        UseBlackBorder = true,
                        UseDarkScrollbar = false,
                        DarkTitleBar = false,
                        TitleBarColor = SystemColors.Control,
                        TitleBarTextColor = SystemColors.ControlText
                    };
                case "Cerulean Blue":
                    return new ThemeColors
                    {
                        WindowBg = Color.FromArgb(16, 40, 61),
                        ControlBg = Color.FromArgb(24, 56, 82),
                        TextColor = Color.FromArgb(228, 242, 250),
                        HeaderColor = Color.FromArgb(120, 202, 255),
                        ButtonBg = Color.FromArgb(24, 56, 82),
                        ButtonFg = Color.FromArgb(228, 242, 250),
                        AccentColor = Color.FromArgb(0, 149, 217),
                        IsLightBase = false,
                        UseBlackBorder = false,
                        UseDarkScrollbar = true,
                        DarkTitleBar = true,
                        TitleBarColor = Color.FromArgb(16, 40, 61),
                        TitleBarTextColor = Color.FromArgb(228, 242, 250)
                    };
                case "Amethyst Purple":
                    return new ThemeColors
                    {
                        WindowBg = Color.FromArgb(36, 22, 54),
                        ControlBg = Color.FromArgb(52, 34, 76),
                        TextColor = Color.FromArgb(238, 228, 248),
                        HeaderColor = Color.FromArgb(198, 155, 240),
                        ButtonBg = Color.FromArgb(52, 34, 76),
                        ButtonFg = Color.FromArgb(238, 228, 248),
                        AccentColor = Color.FromArgb(153, 102, 204),
                        IsLightBase = false,
                        UseBlackBorder = false,
                        UseDarkScrollbar = true,
                        DarkTitleBar = true,
                        TitleBarColor = Color.FromArgb(36, 22, 54),
                        TitleBarTextColor = Color.FromArgb(238, 228, 248)
                    };
                default: // "Dark Mode"
                    return new ThemeColors
                    {
                        WindowBg = ThemeDarkBg,
                        ControlBg = ThemeControlDark,
                        TextColor = TextLight,
                        HeaderColor = AccentYellow,
                        ButtonBg = ThemeControlDark,
                        ButtonFg = TextLight,
                        AccentColor = AccentOrange,
                        IsLightBase = false,
                        UseBlackBorder = false,
                        UseDarkScrollbar = true,
                        DarkTitleBar = true,
                        TitleBarColor = ThemeDarkBg,
                        TitleBarTextColor = TextLight
                    };
            }
        }

        private bool IsLightTheme()
        {
            return CurrentThemeName() == "Light Mode";
        }

        // Draws a thick accent-colored ring around a control whenever it has keyboard focus.
        // The top row's fields previously relied on nothing but their own 1px FixedSingle
        // border, which gave no focus feedback at all with a mouse and - in Light Mode, where
        // the accent used to be the same near-white as the background - gave none with a
        // controller either. Built the same way as WrapControlWithLightModeBorder: a separate
        // SIBLING panel sized a few pixels larger and sent to the back, so only the margin
        // shows as a ring. The control itself is never reparented (doing that to an edit
        // control breaks its caret rendering) and the ring is Enabled=false so it can never
        // intercept a click meant for the field.
        private void AttachFocusHighlight(Control inner)
        {
            const int ringMargin = 4;

            Panel ring = new DoubleBufferedPanel
            {
                Location = new Point(inner.Left - ringMargin, inner.Top - ringMargin),
                Size = new Size(inner.Width + ringMargin * 2, inner.Height + ringMargin * 2),
                Anchor = inner.Anchor,
                BackColor = Color.Transparent,
                Enabled = false,
                Visible = false
            };

            ring.Paint += delegate(object s, PaintEventArgs pe)
            {
                pe.Graphics.SmoothingMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.SmoothingMode.AntiAlias;
                using (Pen pen = new Pen(FocusRingColor(), 3f))
                {
                    pe.Graphics.DrawRectangle(pen, 2, 2, ring.Width - 5, ring.Height - 5);
                }
            };

            inner.Parent.Controls.Add(ring);
            ring.SendToBack();
            focusHighlightPanels.Add(ring);

            inner.GotFocus += delegate
            {
                // Console Mode has one shared ring of its own that follows D-pad navigation
                // (pnlTopBarFocusHighlight). Letting these per-field rings show as well is
                // what left the Theme field still outlined after the cursor had moved on to
                // Target Server - real Windows focus was still sitting on the field the D-pad
                // had visibly left. In Console Mode this ring stays down entirely.
                if (chkConsoleMode != null && chkConsoleMode.Checked) { ring.Visible = false; return; }

                ring.Location = new Point(inner.Left - ringMargin, inner.Top - ringMargin);
                ring.Size = new Size(inner.Width + ringMargin * 2, inner.Height + ringMargin * 2);
                ring.Visible = true;
                ring.SendToBack();
                ring.Invalidate();
            };
            inner.LostFocus += delegate { ring.Visible = false; };
        }

        // ComboBox and TextBox don't expose a reliable way to force a specific border color -
        // their default border can look nearly invisible against a light background. This
        // draws a crisp black frame using a SEPARATE sibling panel positioned just outside the
        // control's existing bounds - deliberately NOT by reparenting/docking the control
        // itself into a container, since doing that to an edit control can silently break its
        // own text/caret rendering (exactly what happened to the mod search box previously).
        // The original control is never touched: same parent, same position, same everything.
        private void WrapControlWithLightModeBorder(Control inner)
        {
            Panel borderPanel = new DoubleBufferedPanel
            {
                Location = new Point(inner.Left - 1, inner.Top - 1),
                Size = new Size(inner.Width + 2, inner.Height + 2),
                Anchor = inner.Anchor
            };

            borderPanel.Paint += delegate(object s, PaintEventArgs pe)
            {
                if (IsLightTheme())
                {
                    using (Pen borderPen = new Pen(Color.Black, 1f))
                    {
                        pe.Graphics.DrawRectangle(borderPen, 0, 0, borderPanel.Width - 1, borderPanel.Height - 1);
                    }
                }
            };

            inner.Parent.Controls.Add(borderPanel);
            // Remembered so Console Mode's top-row restack (ApplyConsoleTopBarLayout) can move
            // each outline along with the field it belongs to - it is a sibling panel, not a
            // real border, so it does not follow the control on its own.
            lightModeBorderPanels[inner] = borderPanel;
        }

        // Setting ComboBox.BackColor/ForeColor alone only reliably recolors the closed box -
        // the open dropdown list often still renders with the system's default white
        // background on Windows regardless of those properties. Owner-drawing every item
        // guarantees the dropdown itself matches the current theme too.
        private void ThemedComboBox_DrawItem(object sender, DrawItemEventArgs e)
        {
            ComboBox combo = sender as ComboBox;
            if (combo == null || e.Index < 0) return;

            ThemeColors t = GetThemeColors(CurrentThemeName());
            bool isSelected = (e.State & DrawItemState.Selected) == DrawItemState.Selected;

            Color backColor = isSelected
                ? (t.IsLightBase ? SystemColors.Highlight : t.AccentColor)
                : (t.IsLightBase ? SystemColors.Window : t.ControlBg);
            Color foreColor = isSelected
                ? (t.IsLightBase ? SystemColors.HighlightText : Color.Black)
                : (t.IsLightBase ? SystemColors.WindowText : t.TextColor);

            using (SolidBrush backBrush = new SolidBrush(backColor))
            {
                e.Graphics.FillRectangle(backBrush, e.Bounds);
            }

            string text = combo.Items[e.Index].ToString();
            TextRenderer.DrawText(e.Graphics, text, combo.Font, e.Bounds, foreColor, TextFormatFlags.VerticalCenter | TextFormatFlags.Left);
        }

        // Desktop-mode replacement for opening the full Console Mode picker window just to
        // pick a Theme or a Server with a mouse. A borderless popup that drops open directly
        // under the field, lists each choice as one themed row, and closes itself the instant
        // something is clicked or focus moves elsewhere - i.e. exactly how a native ComboBox's
        // own drop-down list already behaves, just painted in this app's own theme colors
        // instead of the OS's stock white list.
        private void ShowThemedDropdown(Control anchor, List<string> items, string currentValue, Action<string> onSelect)
        {
            if (activeDesktopDropdown != null)
            {
                Form prior = activeDesktopDropdown;
                activeDesktopDropdown = null;
                prior.Close();
            }

            ThemeColors t = GetThemeColors(CurrentThemeName());
            const int rowHeight = 26;
            const int maxVisibleRows = 8;
            int width = Math.Max(anchor.Width, 160);

            Form popup = new Form
            {
                FormBorderStyle = FormBorderStyle.None,
                ShowInTaskbar = false,
                StartPosition = FormStartPosition.Manual,
                // Doubles as the popup's 1px frame: the inner list panel is inset by exactly
                // one pixel (below), so whatever color shows through that gap is the "border" -
                // the same trick WrapControlWithLightModeBorder uses elsewhere in this file for
                // controls that need an outline WinForms doesn't otherwise let you paint.
                BackColor = t.AccentColor
            };

            Panel list = new Panel
            {
                Location = new Point(1, 1),
                BackColor = t.ControlBg,
                AutoScroll = true
            };
            popup.Controls.Add(list);

            int y = 0;
            foreach (string rawItem in items)
            {
                string captured = rawItem;
                bool isCurrent = string.Equals(rawItem, currentValue, StringComparison.Ordinal);

                Label row = new Label
                {
                    Text = rawItem,
                    AutoSize = false,
                    Location = new Point(0, y),
                    Size = new Size(width - 2, rowHeight),
                    TextAlign = ContentAlignment.MiddleLeft,
                    Padding = new Padding(10, 0, 0, 0),
                    Font = anchor.Font,
                    Cursor = Cursors.Hand,
                    BackColor = isCurrent ? t.AccentColor : t.ControlBg,
                    ForeColor = isCurrent ? (t.IsLightBase ? Color.White : Color.Black) : t.TextColor
                };
                row.Click += delegate
                {
                    onSelect(captured);
                    popup.Close();
                };
                // Hover highlight - the same accent-fill/contrasting-text swap the console
                // picker's tiles and this file's other themed lists already use for "this is
                // what you're about to pick."
                row.MouseEnter += delegate
                {
                    row.BackColor = t.AccentColor;
                    row.ForeColor = t.IsLightBase ? Color.White : Color.Black;
                };
                row.MouseLeave += delegate
                {
                    bool stillCurrent = string.Equals(captured, currentValue, StringComparison.Ordinal);
                    row.BackColor = stillCurrent ? t.AccentColor : t.ControlBg;
                    row.ForeColor = stillCurrent ? (t.IsLightBase ? Color.White : Color.Black) : t.TextColor;
                };
                list.Controls.Add(row);
                y += rowHeight;
            }

            int visibleRows = Math.Max(1, Math.Min(maxVisibleRows, items.Count));
            list.Size = new Size(width - 2, visibleRows * rowHeight);
            popup.ClientSize = new Size(width, list.Height + 2);

            Point openAt = anchor.PointToScreen(new Point(0, anchor.Height));
            Screen scr = Screen.FromControl(anchor);
            // Open upward instead of off the bottom of the monitor when the field sits near
            // the taskbar - the same "keep it fully visible" behavior a native drop-down gets
            // for free from Windows.
            if (openAt.Y + popup.Height > scr.WorkingArea.Bottom)
            {
                openAt = anchor.PointToScreen(new Point(0, -popup.Height));
            }
            popup.Location = openAt;

            popup.Deactivate += delegate { popup.Close(); };
            popup.FormClosed += delegate
            {
                if (ReferenceEquals(activeDesktopDropdown, popup)) activeDesktopDropdown = null;
            };

            activeDesktopDropdown = popup;
            popup.Show(this);
        }

        // Recolors an entire dialog (and every control on it) to match whichever theme is
        // currently selected in the main window, instead of the default light/white system
        // colors WinForms dialogs get otherwise. Call this once, after all of a dialog's
        // controls have been added, right before ShowDialog().
        private void ApplyDialogTheme(Form dlg)
        {
            ThemeColors t = GetThemeColors(CurrentThemeName());

            dlg.BackColor = t.WindowBg;
            dlg.ForeColor = t.TextColor;

            ApplyDialogThemeToControls(dlg.Controls, t);

            try
            {
                int useDark = t.DarkTitleBar ? 1 : 0;
                DwmSetWindowAttribute(dlg.Handle, DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE, ref useDark, sizeof(int));
                int captionColorRef = ColorToColorRef(t.TitleBarColor);
                DwmSetWindowAttribute(dlg.Handle, DWMWA_CAPTION_COLOR, ref captionColorRef, sizeof(int));
                int textColorRef = ColorToColorRef(t.TitleBarTextColor);
                DwmSetWindowAttribute(dlg.Handle, DWMWA_TEXT_COLOR, ref textColorRef, sizeof(int));
            }
            catch { }
        }

        private void ApplyDialogThemeToControls(Control.ControlCollection controls, ThemeColors t)
        {
            foreach (Control child in controls)
            {
                if (child is ShinyButton || child is Button)
                {
                    child.BackColor = t.ButtonBg;
                    child.ForeColor = t.ButtonFg;
                }
                else if (child is TextBox || child is ComboBox || child is ListBox || child is CheckedListBox)
                {
                    child.BackColor = t.ControlBg;
                    child.ForeColor = t.TextColor;
                }
                else if (child is Label || child is CheckBox || child is RadioButton)
                {
                    child.ForeColor = t.TextColor;
                    child.BackColor = Color.Transparent;
                }
                else if (child is Panel || child is GroupBox || child is TableLayoutPanel || child is FlowLayoutPanel)
                {
                    child.BackColor = t.WindowBg;
                }

                if (child.Controls.Count > 0)
                {
                    ApplyDialogThemeToControls(child.Controls, t);
                }
            }
        }

        private void ApplyTheme(string themeName)
        {
            ThemeColors t = GetThemeColors(themeName);
            bool isDarkModeSpecifically = (themeName == "Dark Mode");

            BackgroundImage = null;
            BackColor = t.WindowBg;

            lblPathHeader.ForeColor = t.HeaderColor;
            lblServerHeader.ForeColor = t.HeaderColor;
            lblThemeHeader.ForeColor = t.HeaderColor;
            lblModSearchHeader.ForeColor = t.HeaderColor;
            lblEditorHeader.ForeColor = t.HeaderColor;
            lblPathHeader.BackColor = Color.Transparent;
            lblServerHeader.BackColor = Color.Transparent;
            lblThemeHeader.BackColor = Color.Transparent;
            lblModSearchHeader.BackColor = Color.Transparent;
            lblEditorHeader.BackColor = Color.Transparent;

            foreach (var ctrl in new Control[] { txtGamePath, txtServerSearchBox, cboServerDropdown, cboThemeSelector, cboEditorSelector, txtModSearchBox, lstServerPaks })
            {
                ctrl.BackColor = t.ControlBg;
                ctrl.ForeColor = t.TextColor;
            }

            foreach (var btn in new Button[] { btnBrowsePath, btnOpenDirectory, btnBackupPaks, btnRestoreBackup, btnBackupSaves, btnManageSaves })
            {
                btn.BackColor = t.ButtonBg;
                btn.ForeColor = t.ButtonFg;
                // Always Flat: ShinyButton sets ControlStyles.UserPaint and draws its own
                // gradient/border in OnPaint, so the old FlatStyle.Standard branch for light
                // themes just asked Windows for a native button look that never actually got
                // painted - it contributed nothing except hiding the custom border.
                btn.FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat;
            }

            // "Green like Launch Game, but only in Dark Mode" - normal theme-matching color
            // everywhere else (Light Mode, and the new Cerulean/Amethyst themes).
            Color addMergeColor = isDarkModeSpecifically ? AdjustForColorBlindness(Color.FromArgb(40, 140, 60), SemanticColorRole.Success) : t.ButtonBg;
            btnAddServerFolder.BackColor = addMergeColor;
            btnAddServerFolder.ForeColor = t.ButtonFg;
            btnAddServerFolder.FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat;

            btnMergeServerMods.BackColor = addMergeColor;
            btnMergeServerMods.ForeColor = t.ButtonFg;
            btnMergeServerMods.FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat;

            // Light Mode used to flatten every one of these into SystemColors.ControlLight,
            // so Delete / Undo / Deploy / Remove All ended up identical to each other AND to
            // the plain background - the whole button column read as blank rectangles. They
            // now keep their meaning-carrying colors in Light Mode too, just in lighter-base
            // shades picked to stay readable with white text.
            Color deleteColor = AdjustForColorBlindness(t.IsLightBase ? Color.FromArgb(196, 62, 62) : Color.FromArgb(160, 35, 35), SemanticColorRole.Danger);
            btnDeleteServerFolder.BackColor = deleteColor;
            btnDeleteServerFolder.ForeColor = t.IsLightBase ? Color.White : t.ButtonFg;
            btnDeleteServerFolder.FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat;

            btnDeleteSelectedPak.BackColor = deleteColor;
            btnDeleteSelectedPak.ForeColor = t.IsLightBase ? Color.White : t.ButtonFg;
            btnDeleteSelectedPak.FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat;

            btnUndoLastAction.BackColor = AdjustForColorBlindness(t.IsLightBase ? Color.FromArgb(56, 110, 180) : Color.FromArgb(40, 90, 150), SemanticColorRole.Info);
            btnUndoLastAction.ForeColor = t.IsLightBase ? Color.White : t.ButtonFg;
            btnUndoLastAction.FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat;

            btnDeployMods.BackColor = t.AccentColor;
            btnDeployMods.ForeColor = t.IsLightBase ? Color.White : Color.Black;
            btnDeployMods.FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat;

            // Was a hardcoded orange regardless of theme - now follows the same
            // theme-accent pattern as btnDeployMods so it matches whatever theme (Amethyst
            // Purple, Ocean Blue, etc.) is currently selected instead of always being orange.
            btnRevertVanilla.BackColor = t.AccentColor;
            btnRevertVanilla.ForeColor = t.IsLightBase ? Color.White : Color.Black;
            btnRevertVanilla.FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat;

            btnOpenEngineIni.BackColor = t.ButtonBg;
            btnOpenEngineIni.ForeColor = t.ButtonFg;
            btnOpenEngineIni.FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat;

            btnOpenSaveDirectory.BackColor = t.ButtonBg;
            btnOpenSaveDirectory.ForeColor = t.ButtonFg;
            btnOpenSaveDirectory.FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat;

            // The two custom dropdown fields take the CONTROL background rather than the
            // button one, so they still read as fields you open rather than as actions you
            // press - same distinction the native ComboBoxes used to carry.
            foreach (var dropField in new ShinyButton[] { btnThemeDropDown, btnServerDropDown })
            {
                if (dropField == null) continue;
                dropField.BackColor = t.ControlBg;
                dropField.ForeColor = t.TextColor;
                dropField.FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat;
                dropField.Invalidate();
            }

            // Launch Game stays green in every theme, always - it's never swept into the
            // generic per-theme button coloring above. Still runs through the colorblind
            // adjuster so "green = go" stays readable as its own distinct hue instead of
            // risking a green/red mixup with the Delete buttons above.
            btnLaunchGame.BackColor = AdjustForColorBlindness(Color.FromArgb(40, 140, 60), SemanticColorRole.Success);
            btnLaunchGame.ForeColor = Color.White;
            btnLaunchGame.FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat;

            chkSmartMatching.ForeColor = t.TextColor;
            chkSmartMatching.BackColor = Color.Transparent;

            chkAutoEngineIni.ForeColor = t.TextColor;
            chkAutoEngineIni.BackColor = Color.Transparent;

            // chkConsoleMode is themed by ApplyDialogTheme instead, whenever the Settings
            // dialog that now holds it is opened - it isn't a permanent child of this Form
            // anymore, so there's nothing to theme here directly.

            if (pnlConsoleTiles != null)
            {
                pnlConsoleTiles.BackColor = t.WindowBg;
                lblConsoleControlHint.BackColor = Color.Transparent;
                lblConsoleControlHint.ForeColor = t.IsLightBase ? SystemColors.GrayText : TextMuted;
                RefreshConsoleHighlights();
                RefreshConsoleTopBarHighlight();
            }

            // Also unparented like chkConsoleMode - only themed here if it happens to be open
            // right now, since it's its own independent Form rather than a child of this one.
            if (frmVirtualKeyboard != null && frmVirtualKeyboard.Visible)
            {
                ThemeVirtualKeyboard();
            }

            pnlDropTarget.BackColor = t.ControlBg;
            lblDropInstruction.ForeColor = t.IsLightBase ? SystemColors.GrayText : TextMuted;

            txtServerSearchBox.Invalidate();
            txtModSearchBox.Invalidate();

            // The focus rings paint in the theme's accent color at paint time, so they have to
            // be told to repaint or a ring that is visible right now keeps the old accent.
            foreach (Panel ring in focusHighlightPanels) ring.Invalidate();

            ApplyListBoxScrollbarTheme(t.UseDarkScrollbar);
            ApplyTitleBarTheme(t);

            // Refresh everything so the light-mode border wrappers (which check the theme at
            // paint time) show or hide immediately instead of waiting for some unrelated
            // repaint to happen to notice the theme changed.
            Invalidate(true);
        }

        private void ApplyListBoxScrollbarTheme(bool useDark)
        {
            ApplyNativeScrollbarTheme(lstServerPaks, useDark);
        }

        // Generic helper for theming any native scrollbar (ListBox, CheckedListBox, or a
        // multiline TextBox) so it matches the app theme instead of staying the stock white
        // Windows scrollbar. Every scrollable control created in every dialog/subwindow -
        // main window and popups alike - should be run through this right after it's created.
        private static void ApplyNativeScrollbarTheme(Control ctrl, bool useDark)
        {
            try
            {
                SetWindowTheme(ctrl.Handle, useDark ? "DarkMode_Explorer" : "Explorer", null);
            }
            catch { }
        }

        private void ApplyTitleBarTheme(ThemeColors t)
        {
            try
            {
                int useDark = t.DarkTitleBar ? 1 : 0;
                DwmSetWindowAttribute(Handle, DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE, ref useDark, sizeof(int));
            }
            catch { }

            try
            {
                int captionColorRef = ColorToColorRef(t.TitleBarColor);
                DwmSetWindowAttribute(Handle, DWMWA_CAPTION_COLOR, ref captionColorRef, sizeof(int));

                int textColorRef = ColorToColorRef(t.TitleBarTextColor);
                DwmSetWindowAttribute(Handle, DWMWA_TEXT_COLOR, ref textColorRef, sizeof(int));
            }
            catch { }
            // Both calls above are wrapped separately and swallow failures individually - on
            // Windows versions that don't support DWMWA_CAPTION_COLOR (pre-Windows 11), the
            // title bar still gets the dark/light toggle from the first call even though the
            // custom-color call fails.
        }

        private static int ColorToColorRef(Color c)
        {
            return c.R | (c.G << 8) | (c.B << 16);
        }

        private void UpdateIcon_Paint(object sender, PaintEventArgs pe)
        {
            ThemeColors t = GetThemeColors(CurrentThemeName());
            pe.Graphics.SmoothingMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.SmoothingMode.AntiAlias;

            using (SolidBrush circleBrush = new SolidBrush(t.AccentColor))
            {
                pe.Graphics.FillEllipse(circleBrush, 0, 0, 23, 23);
            }

            Color arrowColor = t.IsLightBase ? Color.White : Color.Black;
            using (Pen arrowPen = new Pen(arrowColor, 2.2f) { StartCap = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.LineCap.Round, EndCap = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.LineCap.Round })
            {
                pe.Graphics.DrawLine(arrowPen, 12, 17, 12, 7);
                pe.Graphics.DrawLine(arrowPen, 12, 7, 7, 12);
                pe.Graphics.DrawLine(arrowPen, 12, 7, 17, 12);
            }

            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(pendingUpdateVersion))
            {
                using (SolidBrush redBrush = new SolidBrush(Color.FromArgb(235, 40, 40)))
                {
                    pe.Graphics.FillEllipse(redBrush, 15, 0, 9, 9);
                }
                using (Pen ringPen = new Pen(t.WindowBg, 1.5f))
                {
                    pe.Graphics.DrawEllipse(ringPen, 15, 0, 9, 9);
                }
            }
        }

        private void ShowUpdateIcon(bool show)
        {
            if (btnUpdateIcon == null) return;
            btnUpdateIcon.Visible = show;
            btnUpdateIcon.Invalidate();
            RepositionSettingsGear();
        }

        // Lays out the top-right corner icon group, right to left: Settings gear (always the
        // rightmost permanent icon), the Redo icon immediately to its left, the Undo icon to
        // Redo's left, the Discord icon to Undo's left, and the Update icon (only shown when
        // an update is available) to the left of all four. When the update icon isn't showing,
        // the rest slide right together to close the gap instead of leaving an empty slot
        // where it would have been.
        private void RepositionSettingsGear()
        {
            if (btnSettingsGear == null) return;
            const int slot = 24 + 6;
            bool updateIconShowing = (btnUpdateIcon != null && btnUpdateIcon.Visible);

            // Was a flat constant (501) picked to match this window's ORIGINAL default
            // width - it never moved when EnsureActionRowMinimumWidth grew the window wider
            // to fit the "Add Server / Delete Server / Delete Mod / Undo / Merge Servers" row,
            // or when the user resized it by hand, so the whole icon group sat stranded well
            // left of the actual right edge instead of hugging it like every other
            // right-anchored control on this row does. Deriving it from ClientSize.Width
            // instead keeps the same ~19px margin from the true edge the original constant
            // was calibrated for, but now it tracks the window's real width.
            int rightEdge = ClientSize.Width - 43;

            // Update (when visible) always claims the outermost spot; Settings, Redo, Undo,
            // and Discord then slide one slot left to make room for it, or sit flush against
            // the edge together when it's hidden.
            int settingsX = updateIconShowing ? (rightEdge - slot) : rightEdge;
            if (btnUpdateIcon != null) btnUpdateIcon.Location = new Point(rightEdge, 6);
            btnSettingsGear.Location = new Point(settingsX, 6);
            if (btnRedoIcon != null) btnRedoIcon.Location = new Point(settingsX - slot, 6);
            if (btnUndoIcon != null) btnUndoIcon.Location = new Point(settingsX - slot * 2, 6);
            if (btnDiscordIcon != null) btnDiscordIcon.Location = new Point(settingsX - slot * 3, 6);
        }

        private void SettingsGear_Paint(object sender, PaintEventArgs pe)
        {
            // Delegates to the same gear renderer Console Mode's tiles use (ConsoleIcons.Paint)
            // instead of a separate hand-rolled copy, so this corner icon and the Utility tab's
            // Settings tile are always the same shape and get fixed together.
            PaintCornerIcon(pe, ConsoleIconKind.Gear);
        }

        // Shared renderer for the top-right corner icon group (Undo / Redo / Settings, and the
        // Update icon's own body in UpdateIcon_Paint): a filled accent-colored disc with the
        // glyph punched out of it in a contrasting color. Previously only the update icon
        // looked like this and the other three were flat orange/gray outlines drawn straight
        // onto the window background, which looked like a different control family entirely
        // and was close to unreadable against Light Mode's pale background.
        private void PaintCornerIcon(PaintEventArgs pe, ConsoleIconKind kind)
        {
            ThemeColors t = GetThemeColors(CurrentThemeName());
            pe.Graphics.SmoothingMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.SmoothingMode.AntiAlias;

            using (SolidBrush circleBrush = new SolidBrush(t.AccentColor))
            {
                pe.Graphics.FillEllipse(circleBrush, 0, 0, 23, 23);
            }

            Color glyphColor = t.IsLightBase ? Color.White : Color.Black;
            ConsoleIcons.Paint(kind, pe.Graphics, new RectangleF(5f, 5f, 14f, 14f), glyphColor);
        }

        // Height a block of text actually needs once it has wrapped to the given width - the
        // Settings dialog stacks its rows from these rather than from guessed pixel values.
        private int MeasureDialogText(string text, Font font, int width)
        {
            Size measured = TextRenderer.MeasureText(text, font, new Size(width, 0), TextFormatFlags.WordBreak);
            return Math.Max(18, measured.Height + 4);
        }

        private void ShowSettingsDialog()
        {
            // Console Mode gets its own controller-navigable, big-row settings menu instead
            // of this mouse-oriented dialog - see ShowConsoleSettingsMenu. A FixedDialog Form
            // with a plain OK-button-to-close flow and no D-pad wiring at all isn't reachable
            // with just a controller, which defeats the point of Console Mode existing.
            if (chkConsoleMode != null && chkConsoleMode.Checked)
            {
                ShowConsoleSettingsMenu();
                // ShowConsoleSettingsMenu's own "Console Mode: ON" entry can flip the
                // checkbox off and break out of its loop - previously that just returned
                // here, leaving Settings closed entirely until the person reopened it by
                // hand to see the desktop version. Falling through to the desktop dialog
                // below instead of returning makes that switch immediate, mirroring what
                // closeOnConsoleModeToggle already does for the opposite direction.
                if (chkConsoleMode.Checked) return;
            }

            // Everything in here used to be positioned with hardcoded pixel values against a
            // fixed 360px dialog - so the longest checkbox label ran off the right edge, and
            // any hint that wrapped to more lines than its hardcoded Size allowed was simply
            // clipped. The dialog is wider now, and every row is measured and stacked instead.
            const int margin = 20;
            const int contentWidth = 400;
            const int rowGap = 8;
            const int blockGap = 18;

            Form dlg = new Form
            {
                Text = "Settings",
                FormBorderStyle = FormBorderStyle.FixedDialog,
                StartPosition = FormStartPosition.CenterParent,
                MaximizeBox = false,
                MinimizeBox = false
            };

            int y = margin;

            // AutoSize on a CheckBox lets its label run to whatever width the text needs,
            // which is exactly how it ended up past the edge of the window. Fixed width plus
            // its own measured height keeps it inside instead.
            chkConsoleMode.AutoSize = false;
            chkConsoleMode.Size = new Size(contentWidth, MeasureDialogText(chkConsoleMode.Text, chkConsoleMode.Font, contentWidth - 24) + 6);
            chkConsoleMode.Location = new Point(margin, y);
            dlg.Controls.Add(chkConsoleMode);
            y += chkConsoleMode.Height + rowGap;

            string consoleHintText = "Replaces the action buttons with a big-tile, controller-navigable menu grouped into Mods / Servers / Backups / Utility. D-pad or arrow keys to move, A/Enter to select, B/Escape to exit.";
            Label lblHint = new Label
            {
                Text = consoleHintText,
                Location = new Point(margin, y),
                Size = new Size(contentWidth, MeasureDialogText(consoleHintText, Font, contentWidth)),
                AutoSize = false
            };
            dlg.Controls.Add(lblHint);
            y += lblHint.Height + blockGap;

            chkVirtualKeyboard.AutoSize = false;
            chkVirtualKeyboard.Size = new Size(contentWidth, MeasureDialogText(chkVirtualKeyboard.Text, chkVirtualKeyboard.Font, contentWidth - 24) + 6);
            chkVirtualKeyboard.Location = new Point(margin, y);
            dlg.Controls.Add(chkVirtualKeyboard);
            y += chkVirtualKeyboard.Height + rowGap;

            string keyboardHintText = "Pops up a themed on-screen keyboard whenever a text box is focused. In Console Mode, the search boxes and dropdowns above the tile menu also become reachable by D-pad/controller - Up from Launch Game enters them, A opens the keyboard or the themed picker, B/Escape backs out. A Close button sits above the keyboard itself for controller users.";
            Label lblKeyboardHint = new Label
            {
                Text = keyboardHintText,
                Location = new Point(margin, y),
                Size = new Size(contentWidth, MeasureDialogText(keyboardHintText, Font, contentWidth)),
                AutoSize = false
            };
            dlg.Controls.Add(lblKeyboardHint);
            y += lblKeyboardHint.Height + blockGap;

            // Custom themed drop-down (owner-drawn via ThemedComboBox_DrawItem, same as the
            // Theme/Editor selectors) rather than a stock combo box - adjusts every red/
            // green/blue "meaning" color in the app (Delete = red, Add/Launch = green, Undo =
            // blue, plus the general accent) for the selected type of color vision deficiency.
            lblColorBlindHeader.Location = new Point(margin, y);
            dlg.Controls.Add(lblColorBlindHeader);
            y += lblColorBlindHeader.Height + 4;

            cboColorBlindMode.Location = new Point(margin, y);
            cboColorBlindMode.Width = contentWidth;
            dlg.Controls.Add(cboColorBlindMode);
            y += cboColorBlindMode.Height + rowGap;

            string colorBlindHintText = "Remaps Delete/Add/Launch/Undo and the accent color to a palette that stays distinguishable under the selected type of color blindness.";
            Label lblColorBlindHint = new Label
            {
                Text = colorBlindHintText,
                Location = new Point(margin, y),
                Size = new Size(contentWidth, MeasureDialogText(colorBlindHintText, Font, contentWidth)),
                AutoSize = false
            };
            dlg.Controls.Add(lblColorBlindHint);
            y += lblColorBlindHint.Height + blockGap;

            ShinyButton btnClose = new ShinyButton { Text = "Close", DialogResult = DialogResult.OK, Width = 100, Height = 30 };
            btnClose.Location = new Point(margin + (contentWidth - btnClose.Width) / 2, y);
            dlg.Controls.Add(btnClose);
            dlg.AcceptButton = btnClose;

            dlg.ClientSize = new Size(contentWidth + margin * 2, y + btnClose.Height + margin);

            // Checking "Console Mode" while this mouse-oriented dialog is open used to just
            // sit there looking unchanged until the person closed it and reopened Settings
            // from the gear icon - only then did the check at the top of this method see
            // Checked=true and redirect. Closing this dialog itself the instant the checkbox
            // flips, and immediately reopening Settings right after ShowDialog returns, makes
            // that switch happen live instead of needing a manual close/reopen.
            EventHandler closeOnConsoleModeToggle = delegate { dlg.Close(); };
            chkConsoleMode.CheckedChanged += closeOnConsoleModeToggle;

            ApplyDialogTheme(dlg);
            dlg.ShowDialog(this);

            chkConsoleMode.CheckedChanged -= closeOnConsoleModeToggle;

            // chkConsoleMode/chkVirtualKeyboard/cboColorBlindMode have to keep existing (and
            // keep their event wiring intact) for the rest of the app's lifetime, so they're
            // detached from the dialog before this Form object is left for the GC to collect,
            // rather than letting them go down with it.
            dlg.Controls.Remove(chkConsoleMode);
            dlg.Controls.Remove(chkVirtualKeyboard);
            dlg.Controls.Remove(lblColorBlindHeader);
            dlg.Controls.Remove(cboColorBlindMode);

            // Now that the mouse dialog is fully torn down, reopen Settings so the person
            // lands straight on whichever version now matches the checkbox they just flipped -
            // ShowSettingsDialog's own guard at the top sends them to the console menu instead
            // of back here if it's now checked.
            //
            // Deferred one message-loop turn (BeginInvoke) rather than called straight away:
            // calling it inline here still runs inside the same call stack as the checkbox's
            // own CheckedChanged (which is itself still unwinding out of dlg's just-closed
            // modal loop), and opening the console picker's borderless Form from that half-
            // settled a context risks the exact same foreground-activation race that made the
            // picker itself flash and vanish (see ConsolePickerForm's Deactivate/Shown
            // comments) - it would appear and immediately look like nothing happened, which
            // reads to the person as "still requires a manual close/reopen" even though this
            // code did technically run. Posting it to the next message instead lets dlg finish
            // closing completely first, so the console menu opens from a clean, fully-idle
            // message loop the same way it does when opened fresh from the gear icon.
            if (chkConsoleMode.Checked)
            {
                BeginInvoke(new MethodInvoker(delegate { ShowSettingsDialog(); }));
            }
        }

        // --- Console Mode Settings menu ---
        // A controller-accessible replacement for ShowSettingsDialog's mouse-oriented layout:
        // reuses ShowConsolePicker (the same borderless, D-pad-navigable, themed list every
        // other Console Mode picker - Theme, Target Server, Mod Search, Paks Directory - is
        // built from) instead of a FixedDialog full of checkboxes a controller can't reach.
        // Loops so picking a toggle flips it and reopens the same menu, rather than forcing a
        // full menu exit/re-enter for every single setting change.
        private void ShowConsoleSettingsMenu()
        {
            // An action label instead of a state readout - this menu is only ever reachable
            // while Console Mode is already on (ShowSettingsDialog redirects here specifically
            // because chkConsoleMode.Checked is true), so "Console Mode (Steam Deck):  ON"
            // was telling the person a fact they already knew just by being here. What they
            // actually want from this row is a way back OUT, so it now reads as the action
            // picking it performs - matching the desktop dialog's own checkbox, which always
            // reads "Console Mode (Steam Deck)" since desktop is the state IT is only ever
            // shown from.
            const string optConsoleMode = "Switch To Desktop Mode";
            const string optVirtualKeyboard = "On-Screen Virtual Keyboard";
            const string optColorBlind = "Colorblind Options >";
            const string optClose = "Close Settings";

            while (true)
            {
                List<string> entries = new List<string>();
                entries.Add(optConsoleMode);
                entries.Add(optVirtualKeyboard + ":  " + (chkVirtualKeyboard.Checked ? "ON" : "OFF"));
                entries.Add(optColorBlind + "  [" + colorBlindMode + "]");
                entries.Add(optClose);

                string chosen = ShowConsolePicker("SETTINGS", "", null, delegate(string query) { return entries; });
                if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(chosen) || chosen == optClose) break;

                if (chosen == optConsoleMode)
                {
                    // Turning Console Mode off mid-menu means this very menu is no longer
                    // reachable by controller-only navigation - close it immediately and let
                    // ShowSettingsDialog's own fallback-through (see its comment) bring up the
                    // desktop dialog right away instead of looping back into a picker the
                    // person just asked to leave.
                    chkConsoleMode.Checked = false;
                    break;
                }
                else if (chosen.StartsWith(optVirtualKeyboard, StringComparison.Ordinal))
                {
                    chkVirtualKeyboard.Checked = !chkVirtualKeyboard.Checked;
                }
                else if (chosen.StartsWith(optColorBlind, StringComparison.Ordinal))
                {
                    ShowConsoleColorBlindMenu();
                }
            }
        }

        // Submenu-inside-a-menu for Console Mode's colorblindness picker, per the requested
        // Settings -> Colorblind Options -> [type] flow - Off/Protanopia/Deuteranopia/
        // Tritanopia, reusing the exact same picker chrome as every other Console Mode list.
        private void ShowConsoleColorBlindMenu()
        {
            List<string> entries = new List<string>();
            foreach (string opt in ColorBlindModeOptions)
            {
                entries.Add(opt + (opt == colorBlindMode ? "  (current)" : ""));
            }

            string chosen = ShowConsolePicker("COLORBLIND OPTIONS", "", colorBlindMode, delegate(string query) { return entries; });
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(chosen)) return;

            foreach (string opt in ColorBlindModeOptions)
            {
                if (chosen.StartsWith(opt, StringComparison.Ordinal))
                {
                    colorBlindMode = opt;
                    if (cboColorBlindMode != null) cboColorBlindMode.SelectedItem = opt;
                    SaveCheckboxSettings();
                    ApplyTheme(CurrentThemeName());
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        private static bool IsRemoteVersionNewer(string remoteVersion, string localVersion)
        {
            Version remoteParsed, localParsed;
            if (Version.TryParse(NormalizeVersionString(remoteVersion), out remoteParsed) &&
                Version.TryParse(NormalizeVersionString(localVersion), out localParsed))
            {
                return remoteParsed > localParsed;
            }
            return !string.Equals(remoteVersion, localVersion, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
        }

        private static string NormalizeVersionString(string v)
        {
            v = v.Trim();
            if (v.StartsWith("V", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) v = v.Substring(1);
            // System.Version needs at least a major.minor pair - pad a bare "4" to "4.0".
            return Regex.IsMatch(v, "^\\d+$") ? v + ".0" : v;
        }

        // Fix: HttpClient's GetStringAsync decodes the response bytes with Encoding.GetString
        // directly, which does NOT strip a leading UTF-8 byte-order-mark the way StreamReader
        // normally would - so if version.txt was ever saved with a BOM (Windows Notepad does
        // this by default, and it's one of the editor options this very app offers), the
        // fetched content starts with an invisible U+FEFF character that string.Trim() does
        // NOT remove (it isn't classified as whitespace). That silently turned "0.3" into
        // "\uFEFF0.3" after Trim(), which never equals the locally normalized "0.3" no matter
        // how carefully the file's visible text was checked on GitHub - hence the version
        // check failing and falling back to the "couldn't be retrieved" message even though
        // the file's contents looked completely correct.
        private static string StripBom(string s)
        {
            return (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(s) && s[0] == '\uFEFF') ? s.Substring(1) : s;
        }

        private async void CheckForUpdatesAsync()
        {
            // Fix: the first-launch changelog used to fire only when a freshly fetched
            // version.txt happened to report a version EQUAL to AppVersion. GitHub's raw
            // content origin is eventually consistent for a window after every push - not
            // just its Fastly edge cache (which the cache-busting query string below does
            // defeat) - so two boots seconds apart can land on different backend replicas and
            // get genuinely different answers for the exact same URL+query. That's what was
            // making the dialog flicker on and off across launches instead of firing once and
            // staying off: the trigger itself depended on unstable remote data. Now the
            // trigger is purely local - it only depends on lastSeenChangelogVersion, a value
            // that changes exclusively when the .exe is rebuilt with a bumped AppVersion - so
            // once it fires for a given AppVersion, no amount of remote flakiness can make it
            // fire again for that same build. The remote fetch is still used, opportunistically,
            // to supply live display text for that one-time dialog.
            if (!string.Equals(lastSeenChangelogVersion, AppVersion, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
            {
                string firstLaunchText = null;
                try
                {
                    string primerUrl = GitHubVersionUrl + "?nocache=" + DateTime.UtcNow.Ticks + "-fl";
                    string primerContent = StripBom(await updateHttpClient.GetStringAsync(primerUrl));
                    if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(primerContent))
                    {
                        string[] primerLines = primerContent.Replace("\r\n", "\n").Split('\n');
                        string primerVersion = primerLines[0].Trim();
                        if (string.Equals(NormalizeVersionString(primerVersion), NormalizeVersionString(AppVersion), StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                        {
                            firstLaunchText = primerLines.Length > 1 ? string.Join("\n", primerLines, 1, primerLines.Length - 1).Trim() : "";
                        }
                    }
                }
                catch (Exception flEx)
                {
                    System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine("ModManager first-launch changelog fetch: " + flEx.GetType().Name + " - " + flEx.Message);
                }
                // Shown (and marked seen) unconditionally here even if the fetch above failed
                // or came back describing some other version - "first boot after installing
                // an update" shouldn't be held hostage to network timing, so a generic
                // fallback message is used when live text isn't available rather than
                // skipping the dialog and trying again next boot.
                ShowFirstLaunchChangelogIfNeeded(firstLaunchText);
            }

            try
            {
                // Fix: GitHub's raw.githubusercontent.com sits behind a CDN (Fastly) that
                // caches each URL's response for a few minutes per edge node, and it does NOT
                // honor the client's Cache-Control/Pragma "no-cache" request headers set in
                // CreateUpdateHttpClient above - those only ever affect caches that choose to
                // respect them, and Fastly's edge cache here doesn't. Appending a value that's
                // different on every single request (current UTC ticks) makes each request's
                // full URL unique, so this particular check can never be served out of a
                // previously cached edge entry - every boot always asks fresh whether a newer
                // version now exists, so a real update is never missed because of a stale
                // "no update available" result sitting in cache somewhere.
                string cacheBustedUrl = GitHubVersionUrl + "?nocache=" + DateTime.UtcNow.Ticks;
                string content = StripBom(await updateHttpClient.GetStringAsync(cacheBustedUrl));
                if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(content)) return;

                string[] lines = content.Replace("\r\n", "\n").Split('\n');
                string remoteVersionRaw = lines[0].Trim();
                string changelog = lines.Length > 1 ? string.Join("\n", lines, 1, lines.Length - 1).Trim() : "";

                if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(remoteVersionRaw)) return;
                
                bool isNewer = IsRemoteVersionNewer(NormalizeVersionString(remoteVersionRaw), AppVersion);
                System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine(string.Format("ModManager update check: Remote={0} ({1}), Local={2} ({3}), IsNewer={4}", remoteVersionRaw, NormalizeVersionString(remoteVersionRaw), AppVersion, NormalizeVersionString(AppVersion), isNewer));

                if (!isNewer) return;

                pendingUpdateVersion = remoteVersionRaw;
                pendingUpdateChangelog = changelog;
                ShowUpdateIcon(true);

                // Only skip the automatic popup for the exact version the user already chose
                // to skip - a newer version than that still gets the full popup.
                if (!string.Equals(skippedUpdateVersion, remoteVersionRaw, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                {
                    System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine("ModManager: Showing update dialog for " + remoteVersionRaw);
                    ShowUpdateChangelogDialog();
                }
                else
                {
                    System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine("ModManager: Skipped update for " + remoteVersionRaw + " (user previously skipped)");
                }
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                // Version.txt may not exist yet (expected on first setup), or there could be
                // a real network error. Errors are logged to Debug output so you can
                // troubleshoot, but don't interrupt startup with a dialog - this is a
                // convenience background check, not critical.
                System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine("ModManager update check: " + ex.GetType().Name + " - " + ex.Message);
            }
        }

        // Shows the "What's New" changelog for AppVersion exactly once - the first boot of a
        // build with this AppVersion, full stop. changelogText is live text CheckForUpdatesAsync
        // opportunistically pulled from GitHub's version.txt when it could confirm that file
        // currently describes this exact version; it may be null (fetch failed, offline, or
        // version.txt has already moved on to describing a newer release), in which case a
        // generic fallback message is shown instead - but the dialog still only ever fires
        // this once per AppVersion regardless of whether live text was available.
        private void ShowFirstLaunchChangelogIfNeeded(string changelogText)
        {
            if (string.Equals(lastSeenChangelogVersion, AppVersion, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                return;

            // CheckForUpdatesAsync runs on a background continuation after its await, so this
            // needs the same UI-thread marshaling ShowUpdateChangelogDialog uses below.
            if (InvokeRequired)
            {
                BeginInvoke(new Action(delegate { ShowFirstLaunchChangelogIfNeeded(changelogText); }));
                return;
            }

            Form dlg = new Form
            {
                Text = "What's New in v" + AppVersion,
                FormBorderStyle = FormBorderStyle.FixedDialog,
                StartPosition = FormStartPosition.CenterParent,
                MaximizeBox = false,
                MinimizeBox = false,
                ClientSize = new Size(420, 350)
            };

            Label lblHeader = new Label
            {
                Text = string.IsNullOrEmpty(lastSeenChangelogVersion)
                    ? "Welcome! Here's what ModManager v" + AppVersion + " can do:"
                    : "ModManager was updated to v" + AppVersion + ". Here's what's new:",
                Location = new Point(20, 15),
                Size = new Size(380, 40),
                Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9.5f, FontStyle.Bold)
            };
            dlg.Controls.Add(lblHeader);

            TextBox txtChangelog = new TextBox
            {
                Text = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(changelogText) ? "(Release notes couldn't be retrieved right now. Check the Discord or Nexus Mods page for details on this version.)" : changelogText.Replace("\n", "\r\n"),
                Location = new Point(20, 58),
                Size = new Size(380, 225),
                Multiline = true,
                ReadOnly = true,
                ScrollBars = ScrollBars.Vertical,
                BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle
            };
            dlg.Controls.Add(txtChangelog);

            ShinyButton btnGotIt = new ShinyButton { Text = "Got It", Location = new Point(153, 295), Width = 115, Height = 36, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold) };
            dlg.Controls.Add(btnGotIt);
            dlg.AcceptButton = btnGotIt;

            // Marked seen as soon as the dialog closes - by the "X" button or Got It alike -
            // so it never nags again on a later launch of this same version.
            dlg.FormClosed += delegate
            {
                lastSeenChangelogVersion = AppVersion;
                SaveCheckboxSettings();
            };
            btnGotIt.Click += delegate { dlg.Close(); };

            // Fix: TextBox controls in WinForms auto-select their entire contents the very
            // first time they receive focus programmatically (not just via user Tab/click) -
            // and since txtChangelog was the first focusable control added to this dialog, it
            // was grabbing that initial focus and showing up fully highlighted in blue the
            // instant the dialog opened. Explicitly handing initial focus to the button
            // instead avoids the textbox ever getting that "first focus" in the first place;
            // DeselectAll on Shown is a second safety net in case anything else focuses it.
            dlg.ActiveControl = btnGotIt;
            dlg.Shown += delegate { txtChangelog.DeselectAll(); };

            ApplyDialogTheme(dlg);
            ApplyNativeScrollbarTheme(txtChangelog, GetThemeColors(CurrentThemeName()).UseDarkScrollbar);
            dlg.ShowDialog(this);
        }

        private void ShowUpdateChangelogDialog()
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(pendingUpdateVersion)) return;

            // The async update check might be continuing on a background thread, but
            // ShowDialog must run on the UI thread. Invoke handles the marshaling.
            if (InvokeRequired)
            {
                BeginInvoke(new Action(ShowUpdateChangelogDialog));
                return;
            }

            Form dlg = new Form
            {
                Text = "Update Available",
                FormBorderStyle = FormBorderStyle.FixedDialog,
                StartPosition = FormStartPosition.CenterParent,
                MaximizeBox = false,
                MinimizeBox = false,
                ClientSize = new Size(420, 390)
            };

            Label lblHeader = new Label
            {
                Text = "A new version of ModManager is available: " + pendingUpdateVersion + "  (you have v" + AppVersion + ")",
                Location = new Point(20, 15),
                Size = new Size(380, 40),
                Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9.5f, FontStyle.Bold)
            };
            dlg.Controls.Add(lblHeader);

            Label lblChangelogHeader = new Label
            {
                Text = "What's new:",
                Location = new Point(20, 58),
                AutoSize = true,
                Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold)
            };
            dlg.Controls.Add(lblChangelogHeader);

            TextBox txtChangelog = new TextBox
            {
                Text = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(pendingUpdateChangelog) ? "(No changelog provided.)" : pendingUpdateChangelog.Replace("\n", "\r\n"),
                Location = new Point(20, 82),
                Size = new Size(380, 225),
                Multiline = true,
                ReadOnly = true,
                ScrollBars = ScrollBars.Vertical,
                BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle
            };
            dlg.Controls.Add(txtChangelog);

            ShinyButton btnUpdate = new ShinyButton { Text = "Update", Location = new Point(20, 325), Width = 115, Height = 36, Font = new Font(FontFamily.GenericSansSerif, 9, FontStyle.Bold) };
            ShinyButton btnMaybeLater = new ShinyButton { Text = "Maybe Later", Location = new Point(148, 325), Width = 115, Height = 36 };
            ShinyButton btnSkip = new ShinyButton { Text = "Skip This Version", Location = new Point(276, 325), Width = 124, Height = 36 };
            dlg.Controls.Add(btnUpdate);
            dlg.Controls.Add(btnMaybeLater);
            dlg.Controls.Add(btnSkip);
            dlg.AcceptButton = btnUpdate;

            btnUpdate.Click += delegate
            {
                try { Process.Start(NexusModPageUrl); }
                catch (Exception ex) { ShowError("Opening Nexus Mods Page", ex); }
                // Intentionally NOT clearing pendingUpdateVersion or hiding the corner icon
                // here - clicking Update only opens the download page, it doesn't guarantee
                // the user actually installs it. The icon stays put so they can get back to
                // this dialog if they change their mind or need it again.
                dlg.Close();
            };

            btnMaybeLater.Click += delegate
            {
                // Nothing persisted here on purpose - since skippedUpdateVersion isn't set,
                // the next launch's check will find the same version newer and show this
                // popup again automatically, exactly like asking again "next time."
                dlg.Close();
            };

            btnSkip.Click += delegate
            {
                skippedUpdateVersion = pendingUpdateVersion;
                SaveCheckboxSettings();
                dlg.Close();
            };

            // Same fix as ShowFirstLaunchChangelogIfNeeded - hand initial focus to a button
            // instead of letting txtChangelog grab it and auto-highlight all its text blue.
            dlg.ActiveControl = btnUpdate;
            dlg.Shown += delegate { txtChangelog.DeselectAll(); };

            ApplyDialogTheme(dlg);
            ApplyNativeScrollbarTheme(txtChangelog, GetThemeColors(CurrentThemeName()).UseDarkScrollbar);
            dlg.ShowDialog(this);
        }

        private void ShowError(string context, Exception ex)
        {
            ShowThemedMessage("Mod Manager Error", "An error occurred while " + context + ".\n\nTechnical Details: " + ex.Message);
        }

        private void OnCheckboxSettingChanged(object sender, EventArgs e)
        {
            UpdateDropInstructionText();
            SaveCheckboxSettings();
        }

        private void UpdateDropInstructionText()
        {
            string matchingPart = chkSmartMatching.Checked ? "Auto-extracts Paks, Reads Readmes" : "Auto-extracts Paks";
            string iniPart = chkAutoEngineIni.Checked ? " & Smart-Merges Engine.ini" : "";
            
            lblDropInstruction.Text = "Drag and Drop .pak, .zip or ReadMe Files Here\n\n(" + matchingPart + iniPart + ")";
        }

        private void LoadInitialPath()
        {
            if (File.Exists(ConfigFileName))
            {
                try
                {
                    string json = File.ReadAllText(ConfigFileName);
                    if (json.Contains("\"target_path\":"))
                    {
                        int start = json.IndexOf("\"target_path\":") + 14;
                        int firstQuote = json.IndexOf("\"", start);
                        int secondQuote = json.IndexOf("\"", firstQuote + 1);
                        if (firstQuote != -1 && secondQuote != -1)
                        {
                            txtGamePath.Text = json.Substring(firstQuote + 1, secondQuote - firstQuote - 1).Replace("\\\\", "\\");
                            return;
                        }
                    }
                }
                catch { }
            }
            txtGamePath.Text = DefaultGamePath;
        }

        private void PersistConfigPath(string path)
        {
            try
            {
                string json = "{\"target_path\":\"" + path.Replace("\\", "\\\\") + "\"}";
                File.WriteAllText(ConfigFileName, json);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowError("Saving Configuration Settings", ex);
            }
        }

        private void ShowThemedMessage(string title, string message)
        {
            const int textWidth = 340;

            Size measured = TextRenderer.MeasureText(message, Font, new Size(textWidth, 0), TextFormatFlags.WordBreak);
            int textHeight = Math.Max(40, measured.Height);

            Form dlg = new Form
            {
                Text = title,
                FormBorderStyle = FormBorderStyle.FixedDialog,
                StartPosition = FormStartPosition.CenterParent,
                MaximizeBox = false,
                MinimizeBox = false,
                ClientSize = new Size(380, textHeight + 90)
            };

            Label lblMessage = new Label
            {
                Text = message,
                Location = new Point(20, 15),
                Size = new Size(textWidth, textHeight),
                AutoSize = false
            };
            dlg.Controls.Add(lblMessage);

            ShinyButton btnOk = new ShinyButton { Text = "OK", DialogResult = DialogResult.OK, Location = new Point(140, textHeight + 35), Width = 100, Height = 30 };
            dlg.Controls.Add(btnOk);
            dlg.AcceptButton = btnOk;
            dlg.CancelButton = btnOk;

            ApplyDialogTheme(dlg);
            dlg.ShowDialog(this);
        }

        // Themed replacement for MessageBox.Show(..., MessageBoxButtons.YesNo, ...). Returns
        // DialogResult.Yes or DialogResult.No so call sites that check the result work exactly
        // like they did with the stock MessageBox.
        private DialogResult ShowThemedConfirm(string title, string message)
        {
            const int textWidth = 340;

            Size measured = TextRenderer.MeasureText(message, Font, new Size(textWidth, 0), TextFormatFlags.WordBreak);
            int textHeight = Math.Max(40, measured.Height);

            Form dlg = new Form
            {
                Text = title,
                FormBorderStyle = FormBorderStyle.FixedDialog,
                StartPosition = FormStartPosition.CenterParent,
                MaximizeBox = false,
                MinimizeBox = false,
                ClientSize = new Size(380, textHeight + 90)
            };

            Label lblMessage = new Label
            {
                Text = message,
                Location = new Point(20, 15),
                Size = new Size(textWidth, textHeight),
                AutoSize = false
            };
            dlg.Controls.Add(lblMessage);

            ShinyButton btnYes = new ShinyButton { Text = "Yes", DialogResult = DialogResult.Yes, Location = new Point(120, textHeight + 35), Width = 100, Height = 30 };
            ShinyButton btnNo = new ShinyButton { Text = "No", DialogResult = DialogResult.No, Location = new Point(230, textHeight + 35), Width = 100, Height = 30 };
            dlg.Controls.Add(btnYes);
            dlg.Controls.Add(btnNo);
            dlg.AcceptButton = btnYes;
            dlg.CancelButton = btnNo;

            ApplyDialogTheme(dlg);
            return dlg.ShowDialog(this);
        }

        // Themed replacement for Microsoft.VisualBasic.Interaction.InputBox(...) - that's a
        // legacy native VB dialog that WinForms code has no way to theme at all (not even
        // ApplyDialogTheme can reach it, since it isn't a Form this app owns), which is why
        // "Add Server" and friends always showed up as a plain white system dialog no matter
        // what theme was active. Returns "" on Cancel, matching InputBox's own behavior, so
        // every existing `if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(result)) return;` call site keeps
        // working unchanged.
        private string ShowThemedInputBox(string prompt, string title, string defaultValue)
        {
            const int textWidth = 340;

            Size measured = TextRenderer.MeasureText(prompt, Font, new Size(textWidth, 0), TextFormatFlags.WordBreak);
            int promptHeight = Math.Max(20, measured.Height);

            Form dlg = new Form
            {
                Text = title,
                FormBorderStyle = FormBorderStyle.FixedDialog,
                StartPosition = FormStartPosition.CenterParent,
                MaximizeBox = false,
                MinimizeBox = false,
                ClientSize = new Size(380, promptHeight + 110)
            };

            Label lblPrompt = new Label
            {
                Text = prompt,
                Location = new Point(20, 15),
                Size = new Size(textWidth, promptHeight),
                AutoSize = false
            };
            dlg.Controls.Add(lblPrompt);

            TextBox txtInput = new TextBox
            {
                Text = defaultValue ?? "",
                Location = new Point(20, promptHeight + 25),
                Width = textWidth,
                BorderStyle = BorderStyle.FixedSingle
            };
            dlg.Controls.Add(txtInput);
            AttachVirtualKeyboardOnFocus(txtInput);

            ShinyButton btnOk = new ShinyButton { Text = "OK", DialogResult = DialogResult.OK, Location = new Point(120, promptHeight + 60), Width = 100, Height = 30 };
            ShinyButton btnCancel = new ShinyButton { Text = "Cancel", DialogResult = DialogResult.Cancel, Location = new Point(230, promptHeight + 60), Width = 100, Height = 30 };
            dlg.Controls.Add(btnOk);
            dlg.Controls.Add(btnCancel);
            dlg.AcceptButton = btnOk;
            dlg.CancelButton = btnCancel;

            dlg.Load += delegate
            {
                txtInput.Focus();
                txtInput.SelectAll();

                // AttachVirtualKeyboardOnFocus only fires the keyboard when the setting is on -
                // but this dialog is the one place in the app where a controller-only Console
                // Mode session has genuinely no other way to type anything at all, so it's
                // always summoned here regardless of that setting.
                if (chkConsoleMode != null && chkConsoleMode.Checked && (chkVirtualKeyboard == null || !chkVirtualKeyboard.Checked))
                {
                    ShowVirtualKeyboard(txtInput);
                }
            };

            ApplyDialogTheme(dlg);
            DialogResult result = dlg.ShowDialog(this);
            return (result == DialogResult.OK) ? txtInput.Text : "";
        }


        private void OnBrowsePathClicked(object sender, EventArgs e)
        {
            using (FolderBrowserDialog dialog = new FolderBrowserDialog())
            {
                if (dialog.ShowDialog() == DialogResult.OK)
                {
                    txtGamePath.Text = dialog.SelectedPath;
                    PersistConfigPath(dialog.SelectedPath);
                }
            }
        }

        private void OnOpenDirectoryClicked(object sender, EventArgs e)
        {
            string path = txtGamePath.Text;
            if (Directory.Exists(path))
            {
                try { Process.Start("explorer.exe", path); }
                catch (Exception ex) { ShowError("Opening Game Directory in Windows Explorer", ex); }
            }
            else
            {
                ShowThemedMessage("Folder Not Found", "The specified folder directory does not exist.");
            }
        }

        private void OnOpenSaveDirectoryClicked(object sender, EventArgs e)
        {
            string savePath = Path.Combine(Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.LocalApplicationData), @"MotorTown\Saved\SaveGames");
            try
            {
                if (!Directory.Exists(savePath))
                {
                    Directory.CreateDirectory(savePath);
                }
                Process.Start("explorer.exe", savePath);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowError("Opening Save File Directory in Windows Explorer", ex);
            }
        }

        private void RefreshServerList()
        {
            try
            {
                cachedServerFolders.Clear();
                cboServerDropdown.Items.Clear();

                foreach (var dir in Directory.GetDirectories(serverStorageDir))
                {
                    string folderName = Path.GetFileName(dir);
                    if (!folderName.Equals("Backup_Vanilla", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) &&
                        !folderName.Equals("Backup_Saves", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) &&
                        !folderName.Equals("Backup_CharacterSaves", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) &&
                        !folderName.Equals("UndoCache", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) &&
                        !folderName.Equals("MTModManager", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                    {
                        cachedServerFolders.Add(folderName);
                    }
                }

                FilterServers(txtServerSearchBox.Text);

                if (cboServerDropdown.Items.Count > 0)
                    cboServerDropdown.SelectedIndex = 0;
                else
                    LoadSelectedServerPaks();
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                ShowError("Loading Server Folders List", ex);
            }
        }

        private void OnServerSearchChanged(object sender, EventArgs e)
        {
            // The server picker already ran the filter for every keystroke typed into its own
            // search row; writing that query back into this (Console Mode-hidden) box
            // afterwards must not run the whole thing a second time and reset the selection.
