                new PointF(tipX, tipY),
                new PointF(tipX + size * (float)Math.Cos(leftRad), tipY + size * (float)Math.Sin(leftRad)),
                new PointF(tipX + size * (float)Math.Cos(rightRad), tipY + size * (float)Math.Sin(rightRad))
            };

            using (SolidBrush headBrush = new SolidBrush(pen.Color))
            {
                g.FillPolygon(headBrush, head);
            }
        }

        // Circular refresh arrow - a ~300 degree arc with a solid arrowhead on the leading end.
        private static void PaintRefresh(Graphics g, RectangleF r, Pen pen)
        {
            RectangleF arcRect = new RectangleF(r.X + r.Width * 0.1f, r.Y + r.Height * 0.1f, r.Width * 0.8f, r.Height * 0.8f);
            const float startAngle = -30f;
            const float sweepAngle = 290f;
            g.DrawArc(pen, arcRect, startAngle, sweepAngle);

            float cx = arcRect.X + arcRect.Width / 2f;
            float cy = arcRect.Y + arcRect.Height / 2f;
            float radius = arcRect.Width / 2f;

            // Head sits on the END of the sweep, pointing the way the stroke is travelling
            // (tangent, +90 degrees from the radius), so it reads as the arrow continuing
            // round rather than as a stray tick floating next to the circle.
            double endRad = (startAngle + sweepAngle) * Math.PI / 180.0;
            float tipX = cx + radius * (float)Math.Cos(endRad);
            float tipY = cy + radius * (float)Math.Sin(endRad);
            FillArrowHead(g, pen, tipX, tipY, endRad + Math.PI / 2.0, radius * 0.62f);
        }

        // Curved arrow sweeping back to the left - "undo" - and its mirror image, "redo".
        // Both used to draw their arrowhead as two separate lines tangent to the arc. One of
        // those two barbs ran almost parallel to the curve itself, so it blended into it and
        // the head looked like a single stroke with no point on the far side - more like a
        // crescent with a tick than an arrow. Both now share PaintCurvedArrow below, which
        // puts a solid filled triangle on the end of the arc instead, so the head is
        // unambiguous at 20px and at Console Mode's larger tile size alike.
        private static void PaintUndo(Graphics g, RectangleF r, Pen pen)
        {
            PaintCurvedArrow(g, r, pen, false);
        }

        // "Redo" - the exact same curved arrow as PaintUndo, mirrored horizontally about the
        // icon's own center so it sweeps the opposite way, instead of re-deriving the same
        // arc/arrowhead trig by hand. The explicit Matrix (rather than chained
        // Translate/Scale/Translate calls) avoids any ambiguity about GDI+'s transform
        // composition order: it directly encodes x' = -x + 2*cx, y' = y.
        private static void PaintRedo(Graphics g, RectangleF r, Pen pen)
        {
            PaintCurvedArrow(g, r, pen, true);
        }

        private static void PaintCurvedArrow(Graphics g, RectangleF r, Pen pen, bool mirrored)
        {
            float cx = r.X + r.Width / 2f, cy = r.Y + r.Height / 2f;
            float radius = Math.Min(r.Width, r.Height) * 0.36f;
            RectangleF arcRect = new RectangleF(cx - radius, cy - radius, radius * 2f, radius * 2f);

            System.Drawing.Drawing2D.GraphicsState state = g.Save();
            if (mirrored)
            {
                System.Drawing.Drawing2D.Matrix mirror = new System.Drawing.Drawing2D.Matrix(-1f, 0f, 0f, 1f, 2f * cx, 0f);
                g.MultiplyTransform(mirror, System.Drawing.Drawing2D.MatrixOrder.Prepend);
            }

            const float startAngle = 35f;
            const float sweepAngle = 265f;
            g.DrawArc(pen, arcRect, startAngle, sweepAngle);

            // The head goes on the START of the sweep and points backwards along the tangent
            // there (-90 degrees from the radius), i.e. the direction the stroke is coming
            // from - that is the "returning" end that makes the glyph read as undo.
            double startRad = startAngle * Math.PI / 180.0;
            float tipX = cx + radius * (float)Math.Cos(startRad);
            float tipY = cy + radius * (float)Math.Sin(startRad);
            FillArrowHead(g, pen, tipX, tipY, startRad - Math.PI / 2.0, radius * 0.72f);

            g.Restore(state);
        }

        // Double-headed vertical arrow - "resize" (grow/shrink the mod list).
        private static void PaintResize(Graphics g, RectangleF r, Pen pen)
        {
            float cx = r.X + r.Width / 2f;
            float topY = r.Y + r.Height * 0.1f, botY = r.Bottom - r.Height * 0.1f;
            g.DrawLine(pen, cx, topY, cx, botY);
            g.DrawLine(pen, cx - r.Width * 0.22f, topY + r.Height * 0.22f, cx, topY);
            g.DrawLine(pen, cx + r.Width * 0.22f, topY + r.Height * 0.22f, cx, topY);
            g.DrawLine(pen, cx - r.Width * 0.22f, botY - r.Height * 0.22f, cx, botY);
            g.DrawLine(pen, cx + r.Width * 0.22f, botY - r.Height * 0.22f, cx, botY);
        }

        // Two lines converging into one with an arrowhead - "merge".
        private static void PaintMerge(Graphics g, RectangleF r, Pen pen)
        {
            float midY = r.Y + r.Height / 2f;
            float endX = r.Right - r.Width * 0.12f;
            g.DrawLine(pen, r.X, r.Y + r.Height * 0.15f, endX, midY);
            g.DrawLine(pen, r.X, r.Bottom - r.Height * 0.15f, endX, midY);
            g.DrawLine(pen, endX, midY, endX - r.Width * 0.22f, midY - r.Height * 0.18f);
            g.DrawLine(pen, endX, midY, endX - r.Width * 0.22f, midY + r.Height * 0.18f);
        }

        private static void PaintFolder(Graphics g, RectangleF r, Pen pen)
        {
            RectangleF tab = new RectangleF(r.X, r.Y + r.Height * 0.05f, r.Width * 0.42f, r.Height * 0.18f);
            g.DrawRectangle(pen, tab.X, tab.Y, tab.Width, tab.Height);
            g.DrawRectangle(pen, r.X, tab.Bottom, r.Width, r.Height - tab.Height - r.Height * 0.05f);
        }

        // A document with a folded top-right corner and two lines of "text".
        private static void PaintFile(Graphics g, RectangleF r, Pen pen)
        {
            float foldSize = r.Width * 0.3f;
            RectangleF body = new RectangleF(r.X + r.Width * 0.15f, r.Y, r.Width * 0.7f, r.Height);
            g.DrawLine(pen, body.X, body.Y, body.Right - foldSize, body.Y);
            g.DrawLine(pen, body.Right - foldSize, body.Y, body.Right, body.Y + foldSize);
            g.DrawLine(pen, body.Right, body.Y + foldSize, body.Right, body.Bottom);
            g.DrawLine(pen, body.Right, body.Bottom, body.X, body.Bottom);
            g.DrawLine(pen, body.X, body.Bottom, body.X, body.Y);
            float lineY = body.Y + body.Height * 0.52f;
            g.DrawLine(pen, body.X + body.Width * 0.18f, lineY, body.Right - body.Width * 0.18f, lineY);
            g.DrawLine(pen, body.X + body.Width * 0.18f, lineY + body.Height * 0.18f, body.Right - body.Width * 0.34f, lineY + body.Height * 0.18f);
        }

        // Generic "community chat" glyph for the Discord corner icon - a rounded speech
        // bubble with a small pointer tail, deliberately generic rather than a redraw of any
        // particular chat app's actual logo/mascot.
        private static void PaintDiscord(Graphics g, RectangleF r, Pen pen, SolidBrush brush)
        {
            RectangleF bubble = new RectangleF(r.X, r.Y, r.Width, r.Height * 0.72f);
            using (System.Drawing.Drawing2D.GraphicsPath path = RoundedRect(bubble, r.Width * 0.22f))
            {
                g.DrawPath(pen, path);
            }

            // Small pointer tail bottom-left, like a speech bubble's tip.
            PointF tailA = new PointF(bubble.X + bubble.Width * 0.22f, bubble.Bottom - pen.Width * 0.4f);
            PointF tailB = new PointF(bubble.X + bubble.Width * 0.10f, r.Bottom);
            PointF tailC = new PointF(bubble.X + bubble.Width * 0.42f, bubble.Bottom - pen.Width * 0.4f);
            g.FillPolygon(pen.Brush, new[] { tailA, tailB, tailC });

            // Three small dots inside the bubble, reading as "chat" at a glance.
            float dotR = Math.Max(1f, r.Width * 0.07f);
            float dotY = bubble.Y + bubble.Height * 0.5f - dotR;
            float spacing = bubble.Width * 0.24f;
            float startX = bubble.X + bubble.Width * 0.5f - spacing - dotR;
            for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++)
            {
                g.FillEllipse(brush, startX + spacing * i, dotY, dotR * 2f, dotR * 2f);
            }
        }

        // Rounded-rectangle path helper shared by icons that need one (currently just the
        // Discord speech bubble) - GDI+ has no built-in rounded-rect primitive.
        private static System.Drawing.Drawing2D.GraphicsPath RoundedRect(RectangleF bounds, float radius)
        {
            System.Drawing.Drawing2D.GraphicsPath path = new System.Drawing.Drawing2D.GraphicsPath();
            float d = radius * 2f;
            path.AddArc(bounds.X, bounds.Y, d, d, 180, 90);
            path.AddArc(bounds.Right - d, bounds.Y, d, d, 270, 90);
            path.AddArc(bounds.Right - d, bounds.Bottom - d, d, d, 0, 90);
            path.AddArc(bounds.X, bounds.Bottom - d, d, d, 90, 90);
            path.CloseFigure();
            return path;
        }
    }

    public class ShinyButton : Button
    {
        private bool isHovering = false;
        private bool isPressed = false;

        // None on every ordinary button (Browse..., Deploy Mods To Game, etc.) so this can't
        // change how any of the ~30 existing ShinyButton usages elsewhere in the app look.
        // Only Console Mode's sidebar tabs and content tiles set this.
        public ConsoleIconKind Icon = ConsoleIconKind.None;

        // true for the narrow sidebar tabs (icon stacked above the label); false for the wide
        // content tiles (icon to the left of the label, in line with it).
        public bool IconAboveText = false;

        // Draws this button as a dropdown FIELD rather than as a button: label left-aligned,
        // a separator and a chevron on the right. Used by the custom Theme / Target Server
        // fields that replaced the native ComboBoxes.
        public bool DropDownField = false;

        public ShinyButton()
        {
            SetStyle(ControlStyles.AllPaintingInWmPaint | ControlStyles.UserPaint | ControlStyles.OptimizedDoubleBuffer | ControlStyles.ResizeRedraw, true);
            FlatStyle = FlatStyle.Flat;
            FlatAppearance.BorderSize = 0;
            Cursor = Cursors.Hand;
        }

        protected override void OnMouseEnter(EventArgs e)
        {
            base.OnMouseEnter(e);
            isHovering = true;
            Invalidate();
        }

        protected override void OnMouseLeave(EventArgs e)
        {
            base.OnMouseLeave(e);
            isHovering = false;
            isPressed = false;
            Invalidate();
        }

        protected override void OnMouseDown(MouseEventArgs mevent)
        {
            base.OnMouseDown(mevent);
            isPressed = true;
            Invalidate();
        }

        protected override void OnMouseUp(MouseEventArgs mevent)
        {
            base.OnMouseUp(mevent);
            isPressed = false;
            Invalidate();
        }

        protected override void OnPaintBackground(PaintEventArgs pevent)
        {
            // Intentionally does nothing: OnPaint below fills the button's entire
            // rectangular bounds itself on every repaint, so there's no separate
            // "background" layer left to paint here. Painting one anyway (even matching
            // colors) risks a visible seam where the two paint passes meet if the button is
            // resized or DPI-scaled between them - the previous corner-color-mismatch bug
            // came from exactly that kind of two-layer approach.
        }

        protected override void OnPaint(PaintEventArgs pevent)
        {
            Graphics g = pevent.Graphics;
            g.SmoothingMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.SmoothingMode.None;
            g.PixelOffsetMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.PixelOffsetMode.HighSpeed;

            Rectangle bounds = new Rectangle(0, 0, Width, Height);

            // The disabled fill used to be a fixed dark gray, which on a light theme was
            // darker than the enabled button and read as emphasis rather than as "disabled".
            bool lightBase = IsLightColor(BackColor);
            Color baseColor = Enabled ? BackColor : (lightBase ? Color.FromArgb(206, 208, 212) : Color.FromArgb(90, 90, 90));
            Color topColor = Lighten(baseColor, isPressed ? -6 : (isHovering ? 28 : 16));
            Color bottomColor = Darken(baseColor, isPressed ? 16 : 4);

            // One continuous gradient across the full rectangle - a few extra blend stops
            // give it a soft glossy look without a second overlay shape, which is what
            // previously produced a visible horizontal seam where the overlay's edge met
            // the body fill underneath it.
            using (System.Drawing.Drawing2D.LinearGradientBrush bodyBrush =
                new System.Drawing.Drawing2D.LinearGradientBrush(new Rectangle(0, 0, Math.Max(1, Width), Math.Max(1, Height) + 1), topColor, bottomColor, System.Drawing.Drawing2D.LinearGradientMode.Vertical))
            {
                System.Drawing.Drawing2D.ColorBlend blend = new System.Drawing.Drawing2D.ColorBlend(4);
                blend.Colors = new Color[] { topColor, Lighten(topColor, isPressed ? 0 : 10), baseColor, bottomColor };
                blend.Positions = new float[] { 0f, 0.18f, 0.55f, 1f };
                bodyBrush.InterpolationColors = blend;

                g.FillRectangle(bodyBrush, bounds);
            }

            // A fixed 45-step darken is plenty of contrast on a dark button but almost
            // nothing on a pale one, which is why Light Mode's buttons had no discernible
            // edge and blended into the window background. Pale fills now get a much stronger
            // outline so every button still reads as a distinct raised control.
            int borderDarken = IsLightColor(baseColor) ? 95 : 45;
            using (Pen borderPen = new Pen(Darken(baseColor, borderDarken), 1f))
            {
                g.DrawRectangle(borderPen, 0, 0, Width - 1, Height - 1);
            }

            g.SmoothingMode = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.SmoothingMode.AntiAlias;
            g.TextRenderingHint = System.Drawing.Text.TextRenderingHint.ClearTypeGridFit;

            Rectangle textBounds = bounds;
            // WordBreak alongside EndEllipsis: a label that's too long even for the full
            // width of a single-column tile now wraps onto a second line instead of just
            // being cut off at the button's edge (still ellipsized if it somehow overflows
            // even that) - see the Console Mode Settings menu's "Console Mode (Steam Deck):
            // ON/OFF"-style entries, which used to lose their ON/OFF state to a plain
            // single-line ellipsis.
            //
            // Fix: WordBreak was only ever meant for those tall Console Mode tiles/picker
            // entries (74-88px), but this flag set applies to every plain ShinyButton in the
            // app - including small ~28px toolbar buttons like "Undo". A short button that
            // wraps has nowhere near enough height for a second line, so the wrapped second
            // line (e.g. the "(1)" of "Undo (1)") was getting silently clipped off at the
            // bottom instead of ellipsized or kept on one line. Only allowing the wrap on
            // buttons tall enough to actually show two lines keeps the intentional
            // Console Mode behavior while letting short buttons fall back to a normal
            // single-line ellipsis, same as before WordBreak was introduced.
            bool allowTextWrap = Height >= 40;
            TextFormatFlags textFlags = TextFormatFlags.HorizontalCenter | TextFormatFlags.VerticalCenter | TextFormatFlags.EndEllipsis;
            if (allowTextWrap) textFlags |= TextFormatFlags.WordBreak;

            if (Icon != ConsoleIconKind.None)
            {
                Color iconColor = Enabled ? ForeColor : Color.FromArgb(170, 170, 170);

                if (IconAboveText)
                {
                    float iconSize = Math.Min(Height * 0.34f, 30f);
                    RectangleF iconRect = new RectangleF((Width - iconSize) / 2f, Height * 0.14f, iconSize, iconSize);
                    ConsoleIcons.Paint(Icon, g, iconRect, iconColor);
                    int textTop = (int)(iconRect.Bottom + 2);
                    textBounds = new Rectangle(2, textTop, Width - 4, Math.Max(1, Height - textTop - 4));
                    textFlags = TextFormatFlags.HorizontalCenter | TextFormatFlags.Top | TextFormatFlags.EndEllipsis | TextFormatFlags.WordBreak;
                }
                else
                {
                    float iconSize = Math.Min(Height * 0.55f, 26f);
                    RectangleF iconRect = new RectangleF(12f, (Height - iconSize) / 2f, iconSize, iconSize);
                    ConsoleIcons.Paint(Icon, g, iconRect, iconColor);
                    int textLeft = (int)(iconRect.Right + 12f);
                    textBounds = new Rectangle(textLeft, 0, Math.Max(10, Width - textLeft - 8), Height);
                    textFlags = TextFormatFlags.Left | TextFormatFlags.VerticalCenter | TextFormatFlags.EndEllipsis;
                }
            }

            // A ShinyButton standing in for a dropdown: label pinned left, a separator and a
            // chevron on the right, so it reads as a field you open rather than as a button.
            if (DropDownField)
            {
                const int arrowZone = 26;
                int separatorX = Math.Max(12, Width - arrowZone - 6);

                textBounds = new Rectangle(9, 0, Math.Max(10, separatorX - 15), Height);
                textFlags = TextFormatFlags.Left | TextFormatFlags.VerticalCenter | TextFormatFlags.EndEllipsis;

                Color glyphColor = Enabled ? ForeColor : Color.FromArgb(170, 170, 170);

                using (Pen separatorPen = new Pen(Color.FromArgb(70, glyphColor), 1f))
                {
                    g.DrawLine(separatorPen, separatorX, 4, separatorX, Math.Max(5, Height - 5));
                }

                float cx = separatorX + (Width - separatorX) / 2f;
                float cy = Height / 2f;
                using (SolidBrush arrowBrush = new SolidBrush(glyphColor))
                {
                    g.FillPolygon(arrowBrush, new PointF[]
                    {
                        new PointF(cx - 4.5f, cy - 2.5f),
                        new PointF(cx + 4.5f, cy - 2.5f),
                        new PointF(cx, cy + 3.5f)
                    });
                }
            }

            TextRenderer.DrawText(g, Text, Font, textBounds, ForeColor, textFlags);

            if (Focused && ShowFocusCues)
            {
                Rectangle focusRect = Rectangle.Inflate(bounds, -4, -4);
                // Translucent white is invisible on a pale button, so the focus dots follow
                // the button's own brightness instead of always being white.
                Color focusColor = IsLightColor(baseColor) ? Color.FromArgb(160, 0, 0, 0) : Color.FromArgb(140, 255, 255, 255);
                using (Pen focusPen = new Pen(focusColor) { DashStyle = System.Drawing.Drawing2D.DashStyle.Dot })
                {
                    g.DrawRectangle(focusPen, focusRect);
                }
            }
        }

        // Perceptual-ish brightness test (the standard Rec. 601 luma weights) rather than a
        // plain RGB average, so a mid blue isn't mistaken for a light color just because its
        // blue channel is high.
        private static bool IsLightColor(Color c)
        {
            return (c.R * 299 + c.G * 587 + c.B * 114) / 1000 > 165;
        }

        private static Color Lighten(Color c, int amount)
        {
            return Color.FromArgb(c.A, Clamp(c.R + amount), Clamp(c.G + amount), Clamp(c.B + amount));
        }

        private static Color Darken(Color c, int amount)
        {
            return Color.FromArgb(c.A, Clamp(c.R - amount), Clamp(c.G - amount), Clamp(c.B - amount));
        }

        private static int Clamp(int v)
        {
            return v < 0 ? 0 : (v > 255 ? 255 : v);
        }
    }
}
"@

$cscPath = "C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\csc.exe"

if (-not (Test-Path $cscPath)) {
    Write-Host "ERROR: Could not find the .NET Framework compiler at:" -ForegroundColor Red
    Write-Host "  $cscPath" -ForegroundColor Red
    Write-Host "This usually means .NET Framework 4.x isn't installed, or your Windows install has it in a different folder." -ForegroundColor Red
    Read-Host "Press Enter to close"
    exit 1
}

if (-not (Test-Path "ModManagerIcon.ico")) {
    Write-Host "ModManagerIcon.ico not found next to this script - compiling without a custom icon." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    & $cscPath /target:winexe /out:ModManager.exe /r:System.dll /r:System.Drawing.dll /r:System.Windows.Forms.dll /r:System.IO.Compression.dll /r:System.IO.Compression.FileSystem.dll /r:System.Net.Http.dll /r:Microsoft.VisualBasic.dll ModManager.cs
} else {
    & $cscPath /target:winexe /out:ModManager.exe /win32icon:ModManagerIcon.ico /resource:ModManagerIcon.ico,ModManagerIcon.ico /r:System.dll /r:System.Drawing.dll /r:System.Windows.Forms.dll /r:System.IO.Compression.dll /r:System.IO.Compression.FileSystem.dll /r:System.Net.Http.dll /r:Microsoft.VisualBasic.dll ModManager.cs
}

# IMPORTANT: this used to be "if ($?) { ... }" with no else branch at all, so if csc.exe
# failed for ANY reason, the script just silently ended - no error, no exe, nothing telling
# you why. Checking $LASTEXITCODE explicitly and adding the else branch below means a failed
# compile now always prints something and waits so the window doesn't just disappear.
if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0 -and (Test-Path "ModManager.exe")) {
    Write-Host "Compilation successful! Starting ModManager.exe..." -ForegroundColor Green

    # Fix: Windows caches file/shortcut icons separately from the exe itself, keyed loosely
    # off the file rather than re-read fresh every time. Embedding a new ModManagerIcon.ico
    # into ModManager.exe doesn't reliably invalidate that cache, so a desktop shortcut to
    # this exe can keep showing the OLD icon indefinitely even though the running app's own
    # titlebar/taskbar icon (loaded straight from ModManagerIcon.ico at runtime - see the
    # Form's Icon assignment - not from the cache) already shows the new one right away.
    # ie4uinit.exe is the same built-in tool Microsoft's own icon-cache-troubleshooting
    # guidance uses to rebuild it; running it here after every successful compile means a
    # fresh icon shows up on the desktop shortcut without the person having to know that
    # trick or dig through Explorer settings themselves. It only rebuilds the cache -
    # nothing else running is touched - so it's safe to run unconditionally.
    try {
        Start-Process "ie4uinit.exe" -ArgumentList "-ClearIconCache" -WindowStyle Hidden -Wait -ErrorAction Stop
    } catch {
        # Non-fatal: worst case is a desktop shortcut still showing the old icon until the
        # person logs off/on or refreshes it by hand - the app itself still launches fine.
    }

    Start-Process "ModManager.exe"
} else {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "COMPILATION FAILED (csc.exe exit code $LASTEXITCODE)." -ForegroundColor Red
    Write-Host "Scroll up to see the actual error(s) csc.exe printed above this line - they'll look like 'ModManager.cs(1234,56): error CS.....'" -ForegroundColor Red
    Read-Host "Press Enter to close"
}
